subject: Pearl Harbor National Memorial
reason: Multi-site memorial: resolve USS Arizona Memorial, visitor center and other fixed structures individually. The story reference point is not an anchor for all of them.
summary: A national memorial on Oahu encompassing the USS Arizona Memorial, Battleship Row mooring quays, and other sites that together preserve the story of December 7, 1941.

subject: Ariccia Lightning
summary: Twenty-five kilometers south of Rome, in a volcanic crater rimmed with chestnut and oak, the strangest priesthood in the ancient world waited for the next man who would come to kill him.

subject: Battle of Sarandí
summary: On a morning in 1825, a thousand horsemen under Juan Antonio Lavalleja routed a Brazilian army on the open Uruguayan plains - and turned a daring landing of thirty-three exiles into a war for a nation.

subject: Battle of Sarandí

subject: Chatham Islands
summary: At the edge of the International Date Line, where the Roaring Forties crash against volcanic rock, a tiny archipelago holds the world's rarest seabird and the haunted memory of a peaceful people.

subject: Chatham Islands

subject: Falkland Islands
summary: A wind-scoured archipelago where penguins outnumber humans a hundred to one, sheep farms stretch to the horizon, and the echoes of a brief, fierce war still resonate across the treeless hills.

subject: Falkland Islands

story.title: Roy Sullivan: The Human Lightning Rod

subject: Roy Sullivan
summary: Where a Virginia park ranger was struck by lightning seven times between 1942 and 1977, surviving each strike to earn a Guinness World Record as the person struck by lightning the most times.

subject: Tierra del Fuego
summary: The Land of Fire - a windswept archipelago at the bottom of South America where the Andes dissolve into the sea, ancient forests meet the Beagle Channel, and Cape Horn guards the passage between oceans.

subject: Tierra del Fuego
summary: The Land of Fire - a windswept archipelago at the bottom of South America where the Andes dissolve into the sea, ancient forests meet the Beagle Channel, and Cape Horn guards the passage between oceans.

subject: Tonga
summary: The last Polynesian kingdom - 169 islands scattered across the South Pacific where a living monarchy rules, humpback whales breed in crystal waters, and Sunday silence still falls across the entire nation.

subject: Tonga
summary: The last Polynesian kingdom - 169 islands scattered across the South Pacific where a living monarchy rules, humpback whales breed in crystal waters, and Sunday silence still falls across the entire nation.

subject: 101 California Street Shooting
summary: A 1993 mass shooting in a San Francisco high-rise that killed eight people and became a catalyst for federal assault weapons legislation.

subject: 1356 Lisbon earthquake
summary: A forgotten medieval earthquake that devastated Lisbon on Saint Bartholomew's Day in 1356, destroying the city's bread ovens and shaking buildings for fifteen minutes, only to be rediscovered centuries later through an inscription on a castle wall.

subject: 1382 Dover Straits Earthquake
summary: An estimated magnitude 6.0 earthquake under the Strait of Dover at 3 pm on 21 May 1382 that damaged Canterbury Cathedral, interrupted a heresy synod against John Wycliffe in London, and was felt across the Low Countries.

story.title: The 16th Street Baptist Church Bombing: Four Girls and the Sunday That Changed America

subject: 16th Street Baptist Church bombing
summary: On September 15, 1963, Ku Klux Klan members detonated dynamite beneath the 16th Street Baptist Church in Birmingham, Alabama, killing four young girls preparing for Youth Day services -- a crime so unconscionable that it galvanized the nation and helped propel the Civil Rights Act of 1964 into law.

subject: 1703 Genroku earthquake
summary: A magnitude 8.1-8.4 megathrust earthquake that struck the Kanto region on the last night of 1703, destroying Odawara Castle, triggering massive tsunami waves, and killing at least 5,233 people along 400 kilometers of Japanese coastline.

subject: 1839 Martinique earthquake
summary: On the morning of January 11, 1839, a magnitude 7.8 earthquake devastated Martinique, leveling Saint-Pierre and Fort Royal and killing hundreds in what remains one of the Caribbean's deadliest seismic events.

story.title: 1847 Zenkoji Earthquake: The Night the Pilgrims' City Fell

subject: 1847 Zenkoji earthquake
summary: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck Nagano at 9:30 pm on May 8, 1847, killing at least 8,600 people -- many of them pilgrims visiting the revered Zenkoji temple -- then triggering landslides that dammed a river and unleashed catastrophic flooding nineteen days later.

subject: 1892 Thirsk Rail Crash
summary: A North Eastern Railway disaster on 2 November 1892 caused by a signalman who had been awake more than 46 hours after his infant daughter's death, killing ten people in foggy night near Manor House signal box.

subject: 1896 Barcelona Corpus Christi procession bombing
summary: A bomb dropped from a building onto a religious procession in 1896 killed twelve people and ignited a cycle of anarchist violence and state repression that would define Barcelona for decades.

subject: 1902 Ibrox disaster
summary: A newly built wooden stand at Ibrox Park collapsed during a Scotland-England match in 1902, killing 25 spectators and injuring over 500 in Britain's first major stadium disaster.

subject: 1904 Oslo earthquake
summary: On a Sunday morning in October 1904, Scandinavia's most powerful modern earthquake shook the Oslofjord so hard it destroyed a church, triggered tsunamis in Swedish lakes, and broke the region's first seismograph.

subject: 1906 Dundee Fire
summary: On the evening of 19 July 1906, a bonded whisky warehouse at the corner of Trades Lane and Seagate caught fire, and burning whisky ran through the streets of Dundee for twelve hours.

subject: 1915 Vanceboro international bridge bombing
summary: A German saboteur carried a suitcase of dynamite from New York to the Maine-New Brunswick border by sleeping car, changed into his army uniform, and bombed a railway bridge -- a bungled act of espionage that foreshadowed the larger Black Tom explosion a year later.

subject: 1929 Cumaná earthquake
summary: A magnitude 6.7 earthquake and tsunami destroyed over 3,500 homes in Cumana on January 17, 1929, stopped a church clock, and may have killed as many as 1,600 people in one of Venezuela's most devastating seismic events.

subject: 1932 Moweaqua Coal Mine disaster
summary: On Christmas Eve 1932 a methane gas explosion killed 54 miners in Moweaqua, Illinois. The disaster, one of the worst in the state's coal history, shaped the town's identity and is commemorated by a museum and a memorial near the former shaft.

subject: 1933 Dublin Riot
summary: On St Patrick's Day 1933 a Catholic mob marched on a small communist headquarters and laid siege to it - while the defenders ate a quiet meal next door.

subject: 1933 Long Beach earthquake
summary: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake that killed 120 people, destroyed 70 schools, and transformed California's building codes forever.

subject: 1935 Labor Day Hurricane
summary: The most intense hurricane ever to strike the United States obliterated the town of Islamorada and killed hundreds of World War I veterans camped in the Florida Keys, triggering a political scandal that reached the White House.

subject: 1935 Shinchiku-Taichu Earthquake
summary: The deadliest earthquake in Taiwan's recorded history struck at dawn on April 21, 1935, killing 3,276 people, and the ruins of the Longteng Bridge that collapsed that morning still stand in Miaoli as a monument to the destruction.

subject: 1936 Bundaberg distillery fire
summary: When lightning struck the Bundaberg Rum distillery in 1936, burning spirit poured into the Burnett River and set the water itself alight.

subject: 1937 Dominguez Canyon rail crash
summary: On April 26, 1937, a D&RGW train plunged into Wells Gulch near Dominguez Canyon after a fire destroyed the trestle bridge just hours after the same crew had safely crossed it that morning.

subject: 1940 Norton Fitzwarren Rail Crash
summary: On a wartime November night in 1940, a Great Western driver whose house had been bombed the previous evening misread signals in the blackout near Taunton and derailed his express. Twenty-seven people died.

subject: 1944 Bombay explosion
summary: When a freighter carrying explosives, cotton, gold, and Spitfires caught fire in Bombay's Victoria Dock during World War II, the resulting blasts killed up to 1,300 people and left 80,000 homeless.

subject: 1951 Miami Airlines C-46 crash
summary: A converted military transport crashed into Elizabeth, New Jersey, moments after takeoff from Newark Airport in December 1951, killing all 56 aboard and triggering a national reckoning over aviation safety.

subject: 1954 BOAC Lockheed Constellation crash
summary: On March 13, 1954, a BOAC Lockheed Constellation struck a seawall while landing at Kallang Airport in Singapore, killing 33 of 40 aboard -- a tragedy traced to a captain who had been on duty for over 21 hours.

subject: 1959 San Diego F3H crash
summary: A young Navy pilot made a split-second choice to sacrifice himself rather than eject over an elementary school, saving as many as 700 lives.

subject: 1962 South Vietnamese Independence Palace bombing
summary: Two South Vietnamese Air Force pilots bombed their own president's palace in Saigon in 1962, an assassination attempt that failed when a 500-pound bomb landed next to Diệm and did not explode.

subject: 1964 Brinks Hotel bombing
summary: On Christmas Eve 1964, a Viet Cong car bomb ripped through the Brinks Hotel in downtown Saigon, killing two Americans and wounding sixty, in an attack that shattered the illusion of safety in the South Vietnamese capital.

subject: 1964 Niigata earthquake
summary: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake that turned Niigata's ground to liquid, toppling apartment buildings intact on their sides and igniting an oil refinery fire that burned for twelve days -- reshaping how the world understands soil liquefaction.

subject: 1965 La Ligua earthquake
summary: A Sunday earthquake in central Chile collapsed a mining dam and buried the town of El Cobre under a river of waste, killing hundreds in minutes and forcing a nation to confront how it cared for its own.

subject: 1967 Thirsk Rail Crash
summary: A waddling cement wagon hurled the King's Cross-to-Aberdeen express into wreckage at 75 mph, killing seven on a clear July afternoon in 1967.

subject: 1969 Tulbagh earthquake
summary: At 10:03 PM on September 29, 1969, a magnitude 6.3 earthquake struck the Western Cape -- South Africa's most destructive seismic event -- killing twelve people and leveling historic Church Street in Tulbagh.

subject: 1971 Ibrox disaster
summary: Sixty-six people were crushed to death on Stairway 13 at Ibrox Stadium during a Rangers-Celtic Old Firm match on 2 January 1971, in the worst British football disaster until Hillsborough.

subject: 1972 Sidney Lanier Bridge collapse
summary: A helmsman turned right when ordered left, sending a cargo ship into a Georgia bridge on a rainy November night in 1972 - killing ten people, stranding a coastal highway for six months, and eventually convincing the state to replace the bridge entirely.

subject: 1974 Mitsubishi Heavy Industries bombing
summary: On a lunchtime Friday in August 1974, a bomb hidden in a flower pot outside Mitsubishi Heavy Industries headquarters in Tokyo's Marunouchi district killed eight people and injured 376 -- Japan's deadliest terrorist attack until the 1995 sarin gas attack.

subject: 1974 Saint John gas explosion
summary: On a Friday night in January 1974, a tractor-trailer knocked over a gasoline pump at a service station near the Reversing Falls Bridge in Saint John, triggering an explosion that killed five people.

subject: 1975 Bagan earthquake
summary: A magnitude-6.8 earthquake struck Bagan on July 8, 1975, irreparably damaging temples that art historians ranked alongside Angkor Wat -- the worst seismic disaster in 900 years of recorded Burmese history.

subject: 1975 Dibbles Bridge Coach Crash
summary: A day trip to the Yorkshire Dales ended in the worst road accident in British history when a coach's brakes failed on a steep hill above the River Dibb.

subject: 1976 Mason County Jail Bombing
summary: A 1976 suicide bombing at the Mason County Courthouse in Point Pleasant, West Virginia that killed five people - the result of a young couple's suicide pact following the murder of their infant daughter.

subject: 1978 Finnish Air Force DC-3 crash
summary: A 1978 military aviation disaster near Kuopio that killed fifteen prominent Finns, including three members of parliament, and narrowly missed claiming a future president.

subject: 1979 Nice tsunami
summary: When a section of landfill at Nice Airport collapsed into the sea on October 16, 1979, it triggered two tsunamis that killed 18 people and permanently altered the city's coastline development.

subject: 1981 Antwerp synagogue bombing
summary: A truck bomb exploded outside a Portuguese Jewish synagogue in Antwerp's diamond district on October 20, 1981, killing three and wounding 106 just minutes before Simchat Torah services.

subject: 1982 Salang Tunnel fire
summary: A catastrophic fire inside Afghanistan's Salang Tunnel on November 3, 1982, during the Soviet-Afghan War, killed between 176 and possibly 2,700 people -- and the truth of what happened remains contested to this day.

subject: 1983 Beirut barracks bombings
summary: Twin truck bombs killed 241 American and 58 French military peacekeepers at their barracks near Beirut International Airport on October 23, 1983, in the deadliest single-day loss for the U.S. Marines since Iwo Jima.

subject: 1983 US embassy bombing in Beirut
summary: A suicide truck bomb destroyed the U.S. Embassy in West Beirut on April 18, 1983, killing 63 people including the CIA's top Middle East analyst and most of the agency's Beirut station, in the deadliest attack on an American diplomatic mission up to that time.

subject: 1983 United States Senate bombing
summary: A bomb detonated inside the U.S. Capitol on the evening of November 7, 1983, shattering the corridor outside the Senate Chamber and permanently changing how Americans access their own government.

subject: 1987 Dhein massacre
summary: Over a thousand Dinka civilians - people who had sought sanctuary in a church and then in railway wagons - were killed in two days in a Darfur town by Muraheleen militia, with police participation.

subject: 1988 Oakland Elementary School Shooting
summary: On September 26, 1988, an elementary school in Greenwood, South Carolina lost Tequila Thomas and Shequila Bradley to a gunman the system had failed to stop.

subject: 1989 Temple of the Tooth attack
summary: In February 1989, the JVP attacked Sri Lanka's holiest Buddhist shrine during a Sinhalese Marxist insurrection driven by grievances about inequality and Indian intervention.

subject: 1992 Aden hotel bombings
summary: In December 1992, bombs struck two Aden hotels housing US Marines bound for Somalia -- an attack later claimed by Osama bin Laden as al-Qaeda's opening strike against the United States.

subject: 1992 Windsor Castle fire
summary: A spotlight pressed against a curtain started a fire that devastated 115 rooms of Windsor Castle, cost 36.5 million pounds to repair, and led to the Queen paying income tax for the first time since the 1930s.

subject: 1993 East Carter High School Shooting
summary: An English teacher and a head custodian were killed in a Grayson, Kentucky classroom in 1993 - one of the early American school shootings that did not yet feel like a pattern.

subject: 1993 Harrods Bombing
summary: A smaller bomb, a stranger pair of bombers, and a department store that had grown used to being a target.

subject: 1996 Channel Tunnel fire
summary: On 18 November 1996, fire broke out on a freight shuttle deep beneath the English Channel - testing the world's longest undersea tunnel barely two years after it opened.

subject: 1998 Temple of the Tooth attack
summary: An LTTE truck bomb devastated Sri Lanka's most sacred Buddhist shrine in January 1998, killing seventeen people and striking at the symbolic heart of Sinhalese identity during a brutal civil war.

subject: 1998 United States Capitol shooting
summary: On a July afternoon in 1998, two Capitol Police officers died protecting tourists and a congressman's staff from a man with paranoid schizophrenia - the first police officers ever to lie in honor in the Rotunda.

subject: 1999 Jiji Earthquake
summary: Taiwan's deadliest earthquake in a century struck at 1:47 AM on September 21, 1999, releasing energy equivalent to the Tsar Bomba and reshaping the island's landscape, building codes, and national identity.

subject: 2000 Jarafa mosque massacre
summary: An attacker opened fire through the window of a mosque in a village outside Omdurman during evening prayers, killing at least 22 worshippers - part of a bitter sectarian pattern between two Sudanese Islamic movements.

subject: 2001 Indian Parliament attack
summary: On a winter morning in December 2001, five armed men drove a car with forged government stickers through the gates of India's Parliament, triggering a gun battle that killed nine people and brought two nuclear-armed nations to the brink of war.

subject: 2002 Amarnath pilgrimage massacre
summary: In August 2002, gunmen opened fire on unarmed pilgrims at the Nunwan base camp near Pahalgam, the third consecutive year that terrorists targeted the ancient Hindu pilgrimage to the Amarnath cave shrine in Kashmir.

subject: 2002 Appalachian School of Law shooting
summary: On January 16, 2002, three people died at a small law school in Grundy, Virginia: Dean Anthony Sutin, Professor Thomas Blackwell, and first-year student Angela Dales.

subject: 2002 Mecca girls' school fire
summary: Fifteen schoolgirls died in a March 2002 fire in Mecca after religious police prevented rescuers from entering the building, according to witnesses, because the students were not wearing modest clothing.

story.title: The Day a Stolen Cessna Hit a Tampa Skyscraper

subject: 2002 Tampa Cessna 172 crash
summary: On January 5, 2002 - four months after September 11 - a 15-year-old student pilot stole a Cessna 172 and deliberately flew it into the Bank of America Tower in downtown Tampa, killing only himself but triggering a national reckoning over general aviation security.

subject: 2003 Istanbul Bombings
summary: In November 2003, four truck bombs struck Istanbul in two waves five days apart — first at two synagogues on November 15, then at the British Consulate and HSBC headquarters on November 20 — killing 59 people in total and wounding more than 750.

subject: 2003 Rocori High School shooting
summary: On September 24, 2003, a school shooting at Rocori High School in Cold Spring, Minnesota, killed two students and forced a small community to reckon with tragedy, accountability, and the long aftermath of violence.

subject: 2004 Istanbul Restaurant Attack
summary: On March 9, 2004, two armed militants attacked a restaurant in Istanbul's Kartal district frequented by Freemasons, killing one person and injuring five others in one of the city's early 21st-century acts of terrorism.

subject: 2004 Kumbakonam School fire
summary: On July 16, 2004, a fire at an unlicensed private school in Kumbakonam, Tamil Nadu, killed 94 children between the ages of five and nine -- a tragedy born of overcrowding, thatched roofs, locked doors, and years of uninspected neglect.

subject: 2005 Iranian Air Force C-130 crash
summary: A military C-130 carrying journalists to cover naval exercises crashed into a ten-story apartment building in Tehran, killing at least 106 people and exposing the toll of decades-long sanctions on Iran's aging aircraft fleet.

subject: 2006 Chapel Hill Vehicle Ramming Attack
summary: On March 3, 2006, a recent UNC graduate drove a rented SUV into students gathered at the campus quad known as the Pit. Nine people were injured. The attacker, who immediately turned himself in, said he wanted to 'avenge' Muslims worldwide.

subject: 2007 Delaware State University shooting
summary: Two seventeen-year-old freshmen were shot at Delaware State University on September 21, 2007. One died. The case is still unsolved nearly two decades later.

subject: 2008 Channel Tunnel fire
summary: On 11 September 2008, a lorry on a freight shuttle caught fire 11 kilometres into the Channel Tunnel, and someone smashed a window with a hammer to get out.

subject: 2008 Danish embassy bombing in Islamabad
summary: On June 2, 2008, a suicide car bomb detonated outside the Danish embassy in Islamabad, killing at least six people in an al-Qaeda attack linked to the Jyllands-Posten Muhammad cartoons controversy.

story.title: The Sugar Turned to Fire: The Imperial Sugar Refinery Explosion of 2008

subject: 2008 Georgia Imperial Sugar refinery explosion
summary: On February 7, 2008, accumulated sugar dust ignited beneath the storage silos of a 92-year-old refinery in Port Wentworth, Georgia, killing fourteen workers and injuring thirty-six in an explosion the U.S. Chemical Safety Board called 'entirely preventable.'

subject: 2008 Kabul Serena Hotel attack
summary: A Taliban assault on Kabul's only five-star hotel in January 2008 killed six people, narrowly missed the Norwegian foreign minister, and shattered the illusion that any place in wartime Afghanistan could be truly secure.

subject: 2008 Namdaemun fire
summary: In 2008, an arsonist destroyed South Korea's National Treasure No. 1 -- the 600-year-old Sungnyemun gate -- with paint thinner and a cigarette lighter, igniting a national reckoning over heritage protection.

subject: 2008 Nouakchott Israeli embassy attack
summary: Before dawn on 1 February 2008, gunmen opened fire outside Israel's embassy in Mauritania's capital, a small attack with large consequences for one of the Arab world's rare ties to Israel.

subject: 2008 Pétion-Ville school collapse
summary: On November 7, 2008, the three-story College La Promesse Evangelique collapsed in Petion-Ville, Haiti, killing at least 93 people - mostly children - in a disaster caused by construction so poor the builder admitted he needed no engineer because he had the word of God.

subject: 2008 Universal Studios fire
summary: A backlot fire that destroyed King Kong and the Back to the Future courthouse, but whose true devastation to music history remained hidden for over a decade.

story.title: 2008 attack on the United States embassy in Sanaa

subject: 2008 attack on the United States embassy in Sanaa
summary: Susan Elbaneh had just married her husband in Yemen and was waiting in line at the US embassy in Sanaa with paperwork for their return to America when the attack began. Nineteen people died that morning.

story.title: 2008 Bombing of Indian Embassy in Kabul

subject: 2008 bombing of Indian embassy in Kabul
summary: A 2008 suicide car bombing outside the Indian embassy in Kabul killed 58 people and exposed the tangled web of regional rivalries -- between India, Pakistan, and the Taliban -- that made Afghanistan's capital a proxy battleground.

story.title: The CAPECO Explosion: When Puerto Rico's Night Sky Turned Orange

subject: 2009 Cataño oil refinery fire
summary: At 12:23 AM on October 23, 2009, an explosion at the Caribbean Petroleum Corporation depot near San Juan generated a blast felt like a 2.8-magnitude earthquake, destroyed 11 storage tanks, and forced the evacuation of 1,500 residents from surrounding communities.

subject: 2009 ConAgra Foods Plant Explosion
summary: On a June morning in Garner, North Carolina, a faulty natural gas purge inside the world's only Slim Jim factory exploded, killing four workers and reshaping a town.

subject: 2010 Santiago Prison Fire
summary: Before dawn in December 2010, fire swept a grossly overcrowded Santiago prison and killed 81 men - many of them young, many serving small sentences, all trapped behind locked gates.

subject: 2010 Times Square car bombing attempt
summary: A failed car bomb in the heart of Times Square was foiled by alert street vendors, an amateurish explosive design, and a suspect who left his house keys in the getaway vehicle.

subject: 2010 Zahedan bombings
summary: On July 15, 2010, two suicide bombers struck worshippers gathered at Zahedan's Grand Mosque, killing 27 people and exposing the sectarian fault lines of Iran's restive southeastern frontier.

subject: 2011 White House shooting
summary: Seven bullets hit the second floor of the White House on a November night in 2011 - and the Secret Service did not realize it for four days.

story.title: 2011 Attack on the British Embassy in Iran

subject: 2011 attack on the British Embassy in Iran
summary: On November 29, 2011, a crowd of roughly 1,000 protesters stormed the British Embassy in Tehran, ransacking offices, stealing documents, and setting fire to a building, triggering the most severe rupture in UK-Iran relations in decades.

subject: 2012 Dhaka garment factory fire
summary: A catastrophic fire at the Tazreen Fashion factory in Ashulia, Dhaka killed at least 117 garment workers in November 2012, exposing the deadly cost of fast fashion and sparking global demands for worker safety reform in Bangladesh.

subject: 2013 Glasgow helicopter crash
summary: A police helicopter crashed into The Clutha pub in central Glasgow on 29 November 2013, killing ten people during a live music night, after the pilot failed to respond to multiple fuel warnings.

subject: 2013 Rosario Gas Explosion
summary: A smell of gas, a phone call that no one logged, and then a nine-story building came down on an ordinary Tuesday morning in Rosario, killing twenty-two people.

subject: 2013 Yemeni Ministry of Defense attack
summary: Gunmen stormed a hospital inside Yemen's Ministry of Defense compound and began shooting doctors, nurses, and patients. Fifty-two died. Al-Qaeda later issued an apology, saying one gunman had disobeyed orders.

subject: 2014 Jinnah International Airport attack
summary: On the night of June 8, 2014, ten militants disguised as airport security guards stormed Karachi's Jinnah International Airport, triggering a five-hour siege that killed 36 people.

subject: 2014 Peshawar school massacre
summary: On 16 December 2014, six Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan gunmen stormed the Army Public School in Peshawar, killing 149 people including 132 schoolchildren in the deadliest terrorist attack in Pakistan's history.

subject: 2014 Taipei Metro Attack
summary: On May 21, 2014, a stabbing attack on a Taipei Metro train between Longshan Temple and Jiangzicui stations killed four people and injured 24, shattering the system's reputation as one of Asia's safest.

subject: 2015 Bangkok bombing
summary: A pipe bomb detonated at Bangkok's Erawan Shrine during evening rush hour on August 17, 2015, killing twenty people and injuring 125, in an attack linked to transnational networks smuggling Uyghur refugees through Southeast Asia.

subject: 2015 Chapel Hill Shooting
summary: On February 10, 2015, three young Muslim Americans - Deah Barakat, Yusor Mohammad Abu-Salha, and Razan Mohammad Abu-Salha - were murdered execution-style in their apartment near UNC. The killer pleaded guilty in 2019 and is serving consecutive life sentences.

subject: 2015 Sabiha Gökçen Airport Bombing
summary: In the early hours of 23 December 2015, a mortar attack on the apron of Sabiha Gökçen International Airport killed airport cleaner Zehra Yamaç and wounded a colleague — a night of violence that illuminated the human cost of a war fought far from the front lines.

subject: 2015 Shoreham Airshow crash
summary: On a sunny August afternoon in 2015, a vintage Hawker Hunter jet failed to complete a loop over Shoreham Airport and crashed onto the A27 road below, killing eleven people in the deadliest UK airshow disaster in over sixty years.

subject: 2016 Atatürk Airport Attack
summary: On 28 June 2016, three attackers carried out coordinated gun and bomb attacks at Istanbul's Atatürk Airport, killing 45 people and wounding more than 230 others — an act of violence that struck at the heart of one of the world's busiest international transit hubs during the holy month of Ramadan.

subject: 2016 Hoboken train crash
summary: A commuter train that never slowed down crashed through the bumper at Hoboken Terminal during morning rush hour, killing one person and injuring 114, because its engineer had fallen asleep at the controls from undiagnosed sleep apnea.

subject: 2016 I-10 tour bus crash
summary: Just after 5 a.m. on October 23, 2016, a tour bus returning to Los Angeles from a Coachella Valley casino struck a stationary semi-trailer on Interstate 10 near Palm Springs, killing 13 people — the deadliest bus accident in California in decades.

subject: 2016 Southern Taiwan Earthquake
summary: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake that struck during Lunar New Year, killed 117 people, and exposed cooking-oil cans packed inside the walls of a collapsed 17-story building.

subject: 2016 Sunbird Aviation Britten-Norman Islander Crash
summary: A routine charter flight in Papua New Guinea ended in catastrophe when a Britten-Norman Islander with a failed engine and a fatally miscalculated center of gravity pitched up and spun into the ground near Kiunga Airport.

subject: 2016 Taoyuan Bus Fire
summary: On July 19, 2016, a tour bus carrying Chinese tourists burst into flames on a highway near Taoyuan Airport, killing all 26 people aboard -- an act investigators later determined was deliberate arson by the driver.

subject: 2017 Bronx apartment fire
summary: A child playing with stove knobs started a fire that killed thirteen people in a Belmont apartment building, exposing how a single open door could turn a stairwell into a chimney.

subject: 2017 Jakarta bombings
summary: On the evening of May 24, 2017, two suicide bombers detonated pressure-cooker explosives at the Kampung Melayu bus terminal in East Jakarta, killing three police officers in what was then the deadliest single attack on Indonesian law enforcement.

subject: 2017 London Bridge attack
summary: A terrorist vehicle-ramming and stabbing attack on 3 June 2017 that killed eight people and injured 48 on London Bridge and in Borough Market before police shot the three attackers dead.

subject: 2017 Westminster attack
summary: On 22 March 2017, a lone attacker drove a car into pedestrians on Westminster Bridge and stabbed a police officer at the gates of Parliament, killing five people in the heart of London's democracy.

subject: 2018 Leicester Helicopter Crash
summary: On 27 October 2018, a helicopter carrying Leicester City owner Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha crashed in a stadium car park moments after lifting off from the pitch, killing all five people aboard.

subject: 2019 Jolo Cathedral Bombings
summary: Twin bombings during Sunday mass at the Cathedral of Our Lady of Mount Carmel in Jolo killed twenty people and injured over a hundred, an act linked to Abu Sayyaf and funded by ransom money.

story.title: The Last Boeing 707: A Wrong Runway in the Fog

subject: 2019 Saha Airlines Boeing 707 crash
summary: On January 14, 2019, the last civilian Boeing 707 in the world landed at the wrong airport near Tehran, overran a runway half the length it needed, and crashed through a wall into a residential neighborhood, killing fifteen of sixteen crew.

subject: 2020 Aden airport attack
summary: Three guided missiles struck Aden International Airport on December 30, 2020, as Yemen's new unity government arrived -- killing 28 people, mostly civilians, in an attack the UN called a potential war crime.

subject: 2020 Hong Kong Garrison Helicopter Crash
summary: On 30 March 2020, a PLA helicopter crashed into an electricity transmission tower in the hills of Tai Lam Country Park, reportedly killing four crew members — the first recorded military aviation accident involving Chinese troops in Hong Kong since the 1997 handover, and one that authorities worked to keep nearly opaque.

subject: 2020 Nashville bombing
summary: On Christmas morning 2020, a lone bomber detonated an RV on Nashville's Second Avenue after broadcasting evacuation warnings from loudspeakers -- killing only himself, knocking out AT&T communications across the region, and grounding flights from Nashville International Airport.

subject: 2020 Royal Chapel of Milot fire
summary: A predawn fire destroyed the dome and interior of a UNESCO World Heritage chapel in northern Haiti -- a building that had already survived an earthquake, two centuries of neglect, and the collapse of the kingdom that built it.

subject: 2021 Kabul airport attack
summary: An ISIS-K suicide bombing at Abbey Gate during the chaotic American evacuation of Kabul on 26 August 2021 killed 13 U.S. service members and at least 170 Afghan civilians, becoming the deadliest day for U.S. forces in Afghanistan in a decade.

subject: 2021 Kaohsiung Building Fire
summary: On October 14, 2021, a fire tore through a crumbling thirteen-story tower in Kaohsiung's Yancheng District, killing forty-six people and exposing decades of neglect toward the city's most vulnerable residents.

subject: 2021 Nagaland killings
summary: On a December evening in 2021, an Indian Army special forces unit ambushed a pickup truck carrying coal miners home to their village in Nagaland, killing six unarmed civilians and setting off a crisis that reached the floor of Parliament.

subject: 2021 Northern Peru earthquake
summary: A magnitude 7.5 quake that struck deep beneath the Peruvian Amazon at dawn, reducing a four-century-old church tower to rubble and claiming lives across two borders.

story.title: The 2021 Osaka Building Fire: A Clinic Meant for Healing

subject: 2021 Osaka building fire
summary: On December 17, 2021, an arson attack at a fourth-floor psychiatric clinic in Osaka's Kita ward killed 26 people who had come seeking help for their mental health, exposing tragic gaps in Japan's building safety codes and sparking a nationwide reckoning with fire escape design.

subject: 2021 Palmas FR plane crash
summary: A small airfield near Porto Nacional where four footballers, a team president, and a veteran pilot took off one January morning and never climbed.

subject: 2021 Philippine Air Force C-130 Crash
summary: The deadliest aviation disaster in Philippine Air Force history occurred when a C-130 Hercules overshot the runway at Jolo Airport on July 4, 2021, killing fifty-three people.

subject: 2021 Salisbury Rail Crash
summary: On a wet October evening near Salisbury, two passenger trains collided in a tunnel - the first such collision in Britain since Ladbroke Grove in 1999. The cause was leaf mulch on the rails.

subject: 2021 eruption of La Soufrière
summary: In April 2021, La Soufriere on Saint Vincent erupted explosively after months of dome-building, forcing 16,000 people to evacuate amid a pandemic and burying the island's northern half in ash.

subject: 2022 Bronx apartment fire
summary: A defective space heater and two broken self-closing doors turned a single apartment fire into the deadliest blaze New York City had seen in three decades, killing seventeen people in a Bronx high-rise on January 9, 2022.

subject: 2022 Mutiny Bay DHC-3 crash
summary: On September 4, 2022, a floatplane carrying ten people from Friday Harbor to Renton nosedived into Mutiny Bay off Whidbey Island, a tragedy traced to a missing lock ring the size of a wedding band.

subject: 2022 Parliament of South Africa fire
summary: On 2 January 2022, arson gutted the National Assembly building in Cape Town's parliamentary complex, displacing South Africa's legislature and exposing years of maintenance failures in one of the country's most important buildings.

subject: 2022 University of Virginia shooting
summary: On November 13, 2022, a former walk-on football player opened fire on a chartered bus returning from a class trip to see a play about Emmett Till, killing three teammates from the team he had briefly belonged to.

subject: 2023 Johannesburg building fire
summary: A 2023 fire at 80 Albert Street in Johannesburg killed 77 people in a building whose history stretches from apartheid-era pass office to overcrowded refuge for the city's most vulnerable residents.

subject: 2023 Lafayette Square U-Haul crash
summary: A 19-year-old Missouri high school graduate flew to Dulles, rented a U-Haul, and rammed the security barriers north of the White House on a May night in 2023 - then unfurled a Nazi flag and told the Secret Service he wanted to seize power.

subject: 2023 Peshawar mosque bombing
summary: On 30 January 2023, a suicide bomber disguised as a police officer detonated 12 kilograms of TNT inside the Police Lines mosque in Peshawar's high-security zone, killing 84 people and injuring 217 during congregational Zuhr prayers.

story.title: 2023 Attack on the Azerbaijani Embassy in Tehran

subject: 2023 attack on the Azerbaijani embassy in Tehran
summary: On January 27, 2023, a lone gunman armed with a Kalashnikov stormed Azerbaijan's embassy in Tehran, killing the head of security and triggering a diplomatic crisis between the two nations.

subject: 2024 Istanbul Church Shooting
summary: On the morning of 28 January 2024, two masked gunmen attacked the Church of Santa Maria in Sarıyer during Sunday Mass, killing worshipper Tuncer Cihan — an act of violence that struck one of Istanbul's oldest Catholic congregations and sent condolences from Rome to the city's doors.

subject: 2024 Istanbul Palace of Justice Attack
summary: On 6 February 2024, two armed attackers opened fire at a security checkpoint outside the Istanbul Justice Palace (Çağlayan courthouse), killing a civilian and dying themselves in the confrontation, while six people — three of them police officers — were wounded.

subject: 2024 Ivanovo Ilyushin Il-76 crash
summary: A routine military transport flight from Ivanovo-Severny airfield ended in catastrophe when an engine fire forced the aircraft down moments after takeoff, killing all fifteen people aboard.

subject: 2024 Lixinsha Bridge Collapse
summary: On 22 February 2024, a barge struck the Lixinsha Bridge in Guangzhou's Nansha district, causing a span to collapse and sending vehicles into the Pearl River — five people died in the accident.

subject: 2024 Mmamatlakala Bus Crash
summary: On Easter Thursday 2024, a bus carrying pilgrims to South Africa's holiest gathering plunged from a Limpopo bridge; of the forty-six aboard, only an eight-year-old girl survived.

subject: 2024 Valencia Residential Complex Fire
summary: In February 2024 a high-rise in Valencia's Campanar district burned in minutes, its cladding spreading flame like a fuse - the city's deadliest fire in nearly six centuries.

subject: 2025 Dhaka Chengdu J-7 crash
summary: A Bangladesh Air Force fighter jet crashed into a school in Dhaka during a first solo flight, killing 37 people including 32 students.

subject: 2025 Homs mosque bombing
summary: A bombing during Friday prayers at an Alawite mosque in Homs exposed the fragile fault lines of post-Assad Syria, killing eight worshippers and igniting protests across the country.

subject: 2025 Kartalkaya hotel fire
summary: It was winter break, and 238 guests were asleep in a Turkish ski resort hotel when a kitchen fire spread through walls without sprinklers, smoke detectors, or working alarms - 78 people died, at least 34 of them children.

story.title: 2025 North Carolina Cessna Citation II Crash

subject: 2025 North Carolina Cessna Citation II Crash
summary: On December 18, 2025, a 1981 Cessna Citation II owned by retired NASCAR driver Greg Biffle crashed approaching Statesville Regional Airport, killing all seven aboard including Biffle, his wife, and their two children.

subject: 2025 Sino-Metals Leach Zambia dam disaster
summary: On 18 February 2025, a tailings dam at a Chinese-owned copper mine in northern Zambia collapsed, releasing approximately 50 million liters of acidic toxic waste into the Kafue River and cutting off water to 700,000 people in Kitwe.

story.title: 2025 Taichung Shin Kong Mitsukoshi Gas Explosion

subject: 2025 Taichung Shin Kong Mitsukoshi Gas Explosion
summary: On February 13, 2025, a gas explosion tore through a closed construction floor of the Shin Kong Mitsukoshi department store in Taichung's Xitun District, killing five people — including a two-year-old girl from Macau — and injuring 38 others in the deadliest incident in the history of Taiwanese department stores.

story.title: 2025 Assassination of Iranian Supreme Court Judges

subject: 2025 assassination of Iranian Supreme Court judges
summary: On January 18, 2025, a service worker who had served tea in Iran's Palace of Justice for nearly eight years stabbed a bodyguard, took his handgun, and shot dead two Supreme Court judges -- both of whom had been sanctioned by Western governments over human rights abuses.

story.title: 22 January 1971 Surgut Aeroflot Antonov An-12 Crash

subject: 22 January 1971 Surgut Aeroflot Antonov An-12 crash
summary: On a freezing January night in 1971, an Aeroflot An-12 cargo plane iced over on approach to Surgut and crashed into the Siberian darkness, killing all fourteen aboard. Nine days later, a nearly identical crash at the same airport would finally force changes to Soviet aviation safety.

subject: 6 October 1976 massacre
summary: On October 6, 1976, Thai police and right-wing paramilitaries stormed Thammasat University in Bangkok, killing dozens of student protesters in a massacre that Thailand's government has spent half a century trying to forget.

subject: Abadan building collapse
summary: A ten-story building that was only permitted for six floors collapsed in the Iranian oil city of Abadan in May 2022, killing at least 43 people and igniting nationwide protests against corruption and negligence.

subject: Aberfan disaster
summary: On 21 October 1966, a colliery spoil tip collapsed onto a primary school in the Welsh village of Aberfan, killing 116 children and 28 adults in one of the most devastating disasters in British history.

subject: Abu Salim Prison massacre
summary: In June 1996, an estimated 1,270 prisoners were shot dead in the courtyards of Abu Salim prison in Tripoli -- a massacre the Gaddafi regime denied for eight years and whose victims' families would help ignite the 2011 Libyan revolution.

subject: Aerocon Flight 25
summary: When a commuter plane crashed and caught fire at Riberalta Airport in 2013, the airport had no fire truck -- five hundred townspeople rushed to the wreckage with sticks and metal bars and pulled ten survivors from the burning fuselage.

story.title: African theatre of World War I

subject: African theatre of World War I
summary: From Morocco to Mozambique, the Great War spilled across a continent the European powers had only just divided among themselves, and the African soldiers, carriers, and villagers caught in it paid the heaviest price.

subject: Air Florida Flight 90
summary: On January 13, 1982, a Boeing 737 crashed into the 14th Street Bridge over the Potomac River seconds after takeoff from Washington National Airport, killing 78 people -- and producing acts of civilian heroism that redefined American emergency response.

subject: All Nippon Airways Flight 61
summary: A 1999 hijacking at Tokyo's Haneda Airport in which a man exploited a security loophole he had warned authorities about a month earlier, killing the captain before passengers and crew wrestled back control of a Boeing 747 carrying 517 people.

subject: Aloha IslandAir Flight 1712
summary: A small commuter plane carrying Molokaʻi high school athletes crashed into a mountainside in the dark on October 28, 1989, killing all twenty people aboard and devastating a tight-knit island community.

subject: Alpine Motel Apartments fire
summary: Las Vegas's deadliest fire exposed how a landlord's neglect and broken safety systems turned a low-income apartment building into a death trap on a December morning in 2019.

subject: Alto Río Building Collapse
summary: A brand-new apartment tower in Concepción broke cleanly in half during the 2010 earthquake, killing eight people and ending in a verdict that left a nation furious.

subject: American Airlines Flight 11
summary: The first plane to strike on September 11, 2001, American Airlines Flight 11 was hijacked fifteen minutes after takeoff from Boston and flown into the North Tower of the World Trade Center, killing all 92 people aboard and more than a thousand in the building above the impact zone.

subject: American Airlines Flight 331
summary: Three days before Christmas 2009, an American Airlines 737 overran a rain-soaked runway in Kingston, broke through the airport fence, and slid across a highway to the edge of the Caribbean Sea -- and everyone survived.

subject: American Airlines Flight 6780
summary: The second of three plane crashes to strike Elizabeth, New Jersey, in less than two months, killing 30 people in January 1952 and leading to the closure of Newark Airport for nine months.

subject: American Airlines Flight 77
summary: The story of the September 11, 2001 attack on the Pentagon -- the rescue, the recovery, and the memorials that honor the 184 lives lost when Flight 77 struck the western face of America's military headquarters.

subject: Amoycan Industrial Centre Fire
summary: In June 2016, a fire inside a self-storage facility in a 66-year-old Kowloon industrial building burned for 108 hours — Hong Kong's longest-burning blaze in two decades — and killed two firefighters.

subject: Armagh rail disaster
summary: On a June morning in 1889, a Sunday school excursion train stalled on a steep hill outside Armagh. The decision to split it in two led to the worst railway disaster in Irish history -- and changed rail safety law forever.

subject: Armley Asbestos Disaster
summary: A Leeds factory exported blue asbestos to sixty countries and left its own neighbours coated in dust their children played in, leading to decades of illness and a landmark court ruling.

subject: Assassination of Abraham Lincoln
summary: On a spring evening at Ford's Theatre, a single Deringer shot ended the presidency that had held the Union together.

subject: Assassination of Empress Myeongseong
summary: In the predawn hours of October 8, 1895, Japanese agents stormed Gyeongbokgung Palace and murdered Korea's Queen Min, an act of political violence that reshaped the peninsula's future.

subject: Assassination of Fernando Villavicencio
summary: Eleven days before Ecuador's 2023 election, a corruption-investigating journalist turned presidential candidate was shot dead outside a Quito school - the first Ecuadorian candidate killed while campaigning since 1978.

subject: Assassination of Indira Gandhi
summary: On October 31, 1984, India's Prime Minister was shot dead by two of her own bodyguards in the garden of her New Delhi residence, an act of retribution for Operation Blue Star that unleashed one of the worst episodes of communal violence in independent India's history.

subject: Assassination of James A. Garfield
summary: A delusional office seeker's bullet killed the 20th president, but it was his doctors' unwashed hands that sealed his fate at the Baltimore and Potomac Railroad Station in Washington, D.C.

subject: Assassination of Julius Caesar
summary: On the Ides of March in 44 BC, a conspiracy of sixty Roman senators stabbed Julius Caesar twenty-three times inside the Theatre of Pompey, an act that failed to save the Republic and instead hastened its collapse into empire.

subject: Assassination of Kim Jong-nam
summary: In February 2017, two women smeared VX nerve agent on the face of Kim Jong-nam at a busy Malaysian airport terminal, killing the North Korean leader's half-brother in one of the most brazen state-sponsored assassinations of the modern era.

subject: Assassination of Luis Carrero Blanco
summary: On December 20, 1973, ETA assassinated Franco's prime minister by detonating a tunnel bomb beneath his car in Madrid, an explosion so powerful it launched the vehicle over a five-story building and altered the trajectory of Spain's transition from dictatorship.

subject: Assassination of Mahatma Gandhi
summary: On a January evening in 1948, three bullets fired at a prayer meeting in New Delhi's Birla House ended the life of the man who had led India to independence through nonviolence.

subject: Assassination of Nikos Temponeras
summary: Nikos Temponeras was a mathematics teacher in Patras who went to stand with his students during a school occupation in January 1991. He did not come home. His death — at the hands of a youth party official — set off a wave of grief and protest that shook Greece.

subject: Assassination of Orlando Letelier
summary: A car bomb planted by Chilean secret police killed a former diplomat on Embassy Row in Washington, D.C. -- state-sponsored terrorism ordered by General Augusto Pinochet on American soil.

subject: Assassination of Robert F. Kennedy
summary: Robert F. Kennedy was shot in the kitchen corridor of the Ambassador Hotel in Los Angeles just after midnight on June 5, 1968, minutes after winning the California presidential primary. He died the following day.

story.title: Assassination of Shinzo Abe: The Shots That Shook Japan

subject: Assassination of Shinzo Abe
summary: On a quiet Friday morning in July 2022, Japan's longest-serving prime minister was shot dead with a homemade gun during a campaign speech outside a train station in Nara, an act of political violence almost unimaginable in one of the world's safest countries.

story.title: The Assassination of William McKinley: The Handshake That Changed America

subject: Assassination of William McKinley
summary: At 4:07 p.m. on September 6, 1901, a man with a revolver hidden under a handkerchief reached out to shake the president's hand inside Buffalo's Temple of Music - and the twentieth century began.

story.title: The Astor Place Riot: When Shakespeare Turned Deadly

subject: Astor Place Riot
summary: On May 10, 1849, a feud between an American actor and an English actor over who played Shakespeare better escalated into a full-scale riot outside a Manhattan opera house, leaving at least 22 dead and marking the moment class warfare erupted on New York's streets.

subject: Attack on Broome
summary: On 3 March 1942, nine Japanese Zeros strafed Broome's flying boats and airfield, killing at least 88 people -- many of them Dutch refugees fleeing the fall of Java.

story.title: Attempted Assassination of Gerald Ford in San Francisco

subject: Attempted Assassination of Gerald Ford in San Francisco
summary: The 1975 attempt on President Ford's life outside the St. Francis Hotel, foiled by a bystander whose heroism was complicated by the fact that saving the president outed him as gay.

story.title: Attempted assassination of Harry S. Truman

subject: Attempted assassination of Harry S. Truman
summary: On a renovation-displaced afternoon in 1950, two Puerto Rican nationalists tried to shoot their way into Blair House and ended up in the largest gunfight in Secret Service history.

subject: Attempted assassination of Theodore Roosevelt
summary: On an October evening in 1912, a bullet struck Theodore Roosevelt in the chest outside a Milwaukee hotel - and the former president, blood soaking his shirt, delivered a 50-minute speech before accepting medical attention.

subject: Attica Prison riot
summary: On September 13, 1971, state troopers stormed Attica Correctional Facility in what an official commission called the bloodiest one-day encounter between Americans since the Civil War. Forty-three people died in total: 33 inmates and 10 hostages, nearly all killed by law enforcement gunfire.

subject: Australian Embassy bombing in Jakarta
summary: On September 9, 2004, a one-tonne car bomb detonated outside the Australian embassy in Jakarta's Kuningan District, killing nine people and wounding over 150 in an attack that exposed the deadly reach of Jemaah Islamiyah across Southeast Asia.

subject: Baldwin Hills Dam disaster
summary: In 1963, a reservoir built to protect Los Angeles from catastrophe became one itself, as 250 million gallons of water burst through an earthen dam and swept through South Los Angeles neighborhoods.

subject: Balvano train disaster
summary: On a March night in 1944, a grossly overloaded freight train stalled inside a mountain tunnel in southern Italy, and 517 people -- most of them civilians riding illegally to barter for food -- suffocated from carbon monoxide produced by low-grade wartime coal.

subject: Battle Abbey
summary: A Benedictine abbey founded by William the Conqueror as penance for the dead of Hastings, its high altar set on the spot where King Harold fell on 14 October 1066.

subject: Battle of Adwalton Moor
summary: The 1643 Civil War battle on the Old Roman Road between Bradford and Wakefield that handed Royalist forces control of Yorkshire and helped force Parliament into alliance with Scotland.

subject: Battle of Agüi
summary: On a narrow, broken road above Chiloé's northern shore, a young British officer fell wounded leading sixty men against a Spanish fort that would not fall for another six years.

subject: Battle of Alamana
summary: On 22 April 1821, Greek commander Athanasios Diakos held the bridge at Alamana with 48 men against an Ottoman army of thousands — and when captured, refused an offer of mercy with words that became part of Greek national memory.

subject: Battle of Ann
summary: A three-month siege in which the Arakan Army methodically encircled and captured the Myanmar military's Western Command headquarters -- the culmination of a year-long offensive that reshaped control of Rakhine State.

subject: Battle of Ansi
summary: A three-month siege in 645 CE where a Goguryeo fortress repelled Emperor Taizong's Tang army, killing over 20,000 troops and forcing one of China's greatest rulers into a devastating winter retreat.

subject: Battle of Arkansas Post
summary: A three-day Civil War engagement where 31,000 Union troops and ironclad warships overwhelmed 5,000 Confederates at Fort Hindman on the Arkansas River -- a battle Grant initially called a 'wild-goose chase' before recognizing its strategic value in the Vicksburg campaign.

subject: Battle of Arlington Mills
summary: Nine Virginia militiamen, a grist mill on Four Mile Run, and the first volley fired in the long shadow of the Capitol.

subject: Battle of Arnhem
summary: John Frost's lightly armed paratroopers held the northern end of the Arnhem road bridge for four days. The relief that was supposed to take two days never arrived.

subject: Battle of Assandun
summary: The 1016 battle on Essex soil that ended the Anglo-Saxon House of Wessex's grip on England and put the Danish king Cnut on the throne - decided, in part, by a single act of treachery.

subject: Battle of Badgam
summary: A single company of Indian soldiers held off a thousand tribal raiders near Srinagar's airfield on November 3, 1947, buying time that shaped the course of the first Indo-Pakistani war.

subject: Battle of Baltimore
summary: The September 1814 defense of Baltimore -- where citizen soldiers, a star-shaped fort, and an oversized flag stopped the British Empire and gave America its national anthem.

subject: Battle of Bamber Bridge
summary: In June 1943 a Lancashire village backed Black American GIs against the segregation their own army tried to impose, and a night of gunfire ended with one soldier dead and a mass court-martial.

subject: Battle of Bau
summary: On a jungle hilltop in Sarawak in 1965, a sixteen-man Gurkha advance party attacked an entrenched Indonesian company, and Lance Corporal Rambahadur Limbu earned the Victoria Cross.

subject: Battle of Beaufort (1945)
summary: The last significant battle in North Borneo, where Australian troops fought through jungle and monsoon rains to liberate a railway town, and one soldier earned the Victoria Cross.

subject: Battle of Beaugency (1429)
summary: The fourth engagement in Joan of Arc's Loire campaign, where French forces recaptured a strategically vital bridge and a disgraced constable risked everything to fight alongside the Maid of Orléans.

subject: Battle of Beaver Dam Creek
summary: The first battle of the Seven Days began with Stonewall Jackson asleep four miles away while A.P. Hill threw his green Confederate troops at Union entrenchments behind a small creek - the opening note of the campaign that would define Robert E. Lee.

subject: Battle of Belchite (1937)
summary: A Spanish Civil War battle that left a town in permanent ruins, preserved by Franco as a monument and haunted by the propaganda of both sides.

subject: Battle of Bentonville
summary: The last major clash between Sherman and Johnston's armies, fought over three desperate days in the Carolina pines, where the Confederacy made its final stand in the Western Theater.

subject: Battle of Binh Ba
summary: A fierce three-day house-to-house battle in a Vietnamese village where Australian tanks and infantry fought room by room to dislodge entrenched PAVN and Viet Cong forces, effectively ending large-scale clashes in Phuoc Tuy Province.

subject: Battle of Bomarsund
summary: A forgotten Crimean War battlefield in the Baltic where steam-powered warships rendered an unfinished Russian fortress obsolete, forever changing the strategic balance of the Aland Islands.

subject: Battle of Boroughbridge
summary: A bridge, a ford, and a king's vengeance: on 16 March 1322, tactics learned fighting the Scots were turned against English rebels, ending the Despenser War and sealing the Earl of Lancaster's fate.

subject: Battle of Boroughmuir
summary: In 1335 a Flemish count went looking for chivalric adventure in Scotland - and ended his night besieged on the ruined rock of Edinburgh Castle, behind a wall built from his own dead horses.

subject: Battle of Bothwell Bridge
summary: The 1679 battle on the River Clyde crushed Scotland's Covenanter rebellion and ushered in the brutal years known as the Killing Time.

subject: Battle of Boykin's Mill
summary: On April 18, 1865 - nine days after Appomattox - a fourteen-year-old Confederate home guard killed the last Union officer to die in combat in the Civil War, near a millpond in Kershaw County.

subject: Battle of Brice's Cross Roads
summary: A Civil War masterclass in cavalry tactics where Nathan Bedford Forrest's roughly 4,800 Confederate horsemen routed a Union force nearly twice their size near a Mississippi crossroads, sending the survivors fleeing across six counties back to Memphis.

subject: Battle of Britain, Northfleet
summary: A Kent pub built by RAF veterans in 1947 stood for nearly seventy years - until contractors knocked it down in 2016 without permission.

subject: Battle of Brześć Litewski
summary: An improvised Polish garrison defended the old fortress at Brześć for three days in September 1939 against Heinz Guderian's entire Panzer corps; when they withdrew, the Wehrmacht handed the fortress to the Red Army at a joint parade.

subject: Battle of Burton Bridge (1322)
summary: A four-day standoff at the medieval Burton Bridge in March 1322, where Edward II crossed the River Trent to chase his cousin Thomas of Lancaster toward execution, and where a black calf was said to have foretold the whole disaster.

subject: Battle of Burton Bridge (1643)
summary: A Royalist cavalry charge across a 36-arch medieval bridge in July 1643 that opened the road for Queen Henrietta Maria to reach her husband Charles I at Oxford, the second time English armies had fought over the same stretch of stone.

subject: Battle of Calderón Bridge
summary: A single exploding ammunition wagon turned 100,000 insurgents into a fleeing mob and delayed Mexican independence by a decade.

subject: Battle of Camarón
summary: On April 30, 1863, sixty-five French Foreign Legionnaires held off 2,000 Mexican soldiers for nearly eleven hours at a hacienda near Veracruz -- a tactical defeat that became the Legion's founding myth and is commemorated every year by both nations.

subject: Battle of Carinish
summary: The 1601 battle at Trinity Temple on North Uist -- possibly the last engagement fought with bows and arrows in the British Isles -- and the remarkable tale of hospitality, treachery, and pipers that followed.

subject: Battle of Cartagena (1758)
summary: In one night off a neutral Spanish port, a British squadron scattered a French relief fleet and quietly sealed the fate of a fortress an ocean away.

subject: Battle of Castalla
summary: The 1813 victory over Marshal Suchet at Castalla was won on a castle-topped ridge above Alicante - and made possible the day before by a five-hour rearguard stand at a mountain pass.

subject: Battle of Castle Itter
summary: The strangest battle of World War II, fought on May 5, 1945, when American soldiers, Wehrmacht defectors, an SS officer, and French prisoners of war defended an Austrian castle against a Waffen-SS assault.

subject: Battle of Champions
summary: A 15th-century trial by combat at a Caithness chapel that ended in a massacre and a feud that took five centuries to end.

subject: Battle of Charlotte
summary: On September 26, 1780, Patriot militia stung Cornwallis's vanguard at the Mecklenburg courthouse - earning Charlotte the nickname "the Hornet's Nest" and a mascot that's still buzzing.

subject: Battle of Chedabucto
summary: In 1690, New England raiders destroyed a French fort and 50,000 crowns of fish at Chedabucto Bay, igniting a cycle of reprisal that would define Acadian-English relations for generations.

story.title: The Last Ride of Pancho Villa

subject: Battle of Ciudad Juárez (1919)
summary: On June 15, 1919, Pancho Villa's rebel army attacked Ciudad Juarez, triggering the last major U.S. military intervention of the Mexican Revolution when stray bullets began killing American civilians across the Rio Grande in El Paso.

subject: Battle of Colson's Mill
summary: A small skirmish at a North Carolina mill in July 1780 cost Lord Cornwallis thousands of Loyalist recruits at the worst possible moment.

subject: Battle of Columbus (1865)
summary: On Easter Sunday 1865, Union cavalry stormed Columbus, Georgia in a chaotic night battle where enemies raced side-by-side across a covered bridge -- a clash many historians call the last true battle of the Civil War.

subject: Battle of Corregidor
summary: In May 1942, the island fortress of Corregidor -- the last American stronghold in the Philippines -- fell to Japanese forces after months of relentless bombardment, ending one of the most desperate stands of the Pacific War.

subject: Battle of Corregidor (1945)
summary: In February 1945, American paratroopers dropped onto a tiny island fortress to reclaim the Rock that had become a symbol of defiance and defeat three years earlier.

subject: Battle of Cropredy Bridge
summary: A summer skirmish over a small Oxfordshire bridge in 1644 - the day Sir William Waller nearly captured King Charles I, and instead lost his army.

subject: Battle of Cumberland Church
summary: Two days before Appomattox, the Army of Northern Virginia held its last successful defensive stand at a small Methodist church north of Farmville, and Grant chose that evening to ask Robert E. Lee, for the first time, to surrender.

subject: Battle of Cynossema
summary: In 411 BC an outnumbered Athenian fleet won a narrow victory at the Dog's Tomb in the Hellespont, restoring confidence to a city that had just suffered through an oligarchic coup at home.

subject: Battle of Dingle's Mill
summary: On Easter Sunday 1865, as Lee and Grant met at Appomattox, Union forces clashed with Confederate militia at a millpond three miles south of Sumter - a battle whose timing made it strangely meaningless.

subject: Battle of Dover Strait (1916)
summary: A night in October 1916 when German torpedo boats raided the Dover Barrage, the drifter crews defended their nets with rifles, and one British destroyer captain answered the wrong signal with the wrong assumption.

subject: Battle of Drøbak Sound
summary: On the morning of 9 April 1940, an aging Norwegian coastal fortress with obsolete guns and a hidden torpedo battery sank the German cruiser Blucher in the Oslofjord, buying King Haakon VII and his government just enough time to escape the Nazi invasion.

subject: Battle of Dublin
summary: A week of artillery bombardment and street fighting in June-July 1922 began Ireland's Civil War, destroyed irreplaceable historical records, and killed 80 people including the Republican leader who walked out of a burning hotel alone with a revolver.

subject: Battle of Dunbar (1296)
summary: The opening field battle of the Wars of Scottish Independence, fought near a castle whose lady was loyal to the wrong side.

subject: Battle of Dunkeld
summary: The 1689 battle where Cameronian Covenanters held Dunkeld's cathedral against four-to-one Jacobite odds for sixteen hours, stripping lead from rooftops to keep firing when their ammunition ran out.

subject: Battle of Fairfax Court House (1861)
summary: Before dawn on June 1, 1861, a Union cavalry raid through a sleepy Virginia village produced the Civil War's first combat death - Captain John Q. Marr of the Warrenton Rifles, killed in a clover field he could no longer see.

subject: Battle of Fajardo
summary: A chaotic night battle at a lighthouse on Puerto Rico's northeastern tip where 22 U.S. Navy sailors held off Spanish troops during the Spanish-American War -- while sheltering 60 civilian women and children inside.

subject: Battle of Fort Apache
summary: A September 1881 Apache counterattack on a U.S. cavalry garrison that helped ignite the final Apache war and Geronimo's last stand.

subject: Battle of Fort Brooke
summary: A cunning Union raid in 1863 used a diversionary bombardment to mask a 14-mile overland march through the Florida wilderness, destroying Confederate blockade runners hidden on Tampa's Hillsborough River.

subject: Battle of Fort Coimbra
summary: The opening engagement of the Paraguayan War's Mato Grosso campaign, where a tiny Brazilian garrison held a river fortress against 3,200 Paraguayan troops before escaping by night without losing a single defender.

subject: Battle of Fort Cumberland (1776)
summary: A ragtag rebel force tried to bring the American Revolution to Nova Scotia in 1776, besieging a crumbling fort on the Chignecto isthmus in a doomed campaign that would determine whether Britain's Maritime colonies joined the uprising.

subject: Battle of Fort Davidson
summary: A desperate 1864 Civil War engagement where 1,456 Union defenders inside a small hexagonal earthwork repulsed repeated Confederate assaults by thousands of troops, then escaped under cover of darkness -- detonating the fort's magazine and derailing Sterling Price's campaign to recapture Missouri.

subject: Battle of Fort Dearborn
summary: On August 15, 1812, a fifteen-minute ambush near the south bank of the Chicago River killed dozens of American soldiers, militia, women, and children - and set in motion the forced removal of the Potawatomi from the land that would become Chicago.

story.title: Battle of Fort Eben-Emael: Twenty Minutes That Rewrote Modern War

subject: Battle of Fort Eben-Emael
summary: On 10 May 1940, seventy-eight German paratroopers in silent gliders landed atop the world's most impregnable fortress and broke it open in twenty minutes - the first strategic airborne assault in military history.

subject: Battle of Fort Necessity
summary: On a rain-soaked alpine meadow in the Allegheny Mountains, a 22-year-old George Washington fought his first battle and signed his only surrender, accidentally igniting a global war.

subject: Battle of Fort Pillow
summary: On April 12, 1864, Confederate cavalry under Nathan Bedford Forrest overran a Union garrison on the Mississippi River where half the defenders were Black soldiers -- and what happened after they surrendered became one of the Civil War's most harrowing atrocities.

subject: Battle of Fort Sanders
summary: A forty-minute assault that became one of the Civil War's most lopsided Union victories, fought over an earthen fort in Knoxville that Longstreet fatally misjudged.

subject: Battle of Fort Stevens
summary: The only Civil War battle fought inside Washington, D.C., where Abraham Lincoln came under enemy fire while watching from the parapet.

subject: Battle of Gallipoli (1416)
summary: On 29 May 1416, a Venetian fleet meant to deliver an embassy to the Ottoman sultan ended up sinking his navy outside its main base, in a battle so successful it embarrassed Venice into pretending it had never been planned.

subject: Battle of Gemas
summary: At a wooden bridge in the Malayan jungle, Australian soldiers of the 2/30th Battalion sprang an ambush that killed or wounded nearly 800 Japanese troops -- one of only two Allied victories in the entire Malayan campaign of 1942.

story.title: Battle of Geok Tepe: The Fall of the Blue Hill

subject: Battle of Geok Tepe
summary: In January 1881, a Russian siege detonated a massive mine beneath the walls of a Turkmen fortress at Geok Tepe, killing thousands of defenders and civilians in a slaughter so extreme that even the commanding general was removed from his post.

subject: Battle of Gloucester Point (1861)
summary: Three weeks after Fort Sumter, two ships, one shore battery, and zero casualties opened the Civil War in Virginia.

subject: Battle of Gondra
summary: Beneath the trenches of Fort Gondra, Paraguayan soldiers dug a tunnel by hand to surprise the enemy from behind, in one of the strangest feats of South America's deadliest modern war.

subject: Battle of Graham's Fort
summary: The smallest battle of the American Revolution, fought at a log cabin on Buffalo Creek in 1780, where a seventeen-year-old woman reportedly saved her brother and changed the day.

subject: Battle of Great Bridge
summary: A lopsided Revolutionary War clash on a Virginia causeway ended British rule in the colony, cost one rebel a thumb wound, and sent the Royal Governor fleeing to sea, never to return.

subject: Battle of Groningen
summary: For four days in April 1945, Canadian infantry fought house by house through one of the Netherlands' most beautiful medieval cities, forbidden to use artillery because civilians were still inside.

subject: Battle of Guerrero
summary: The last true cavalry charge in American military history, when exhausted troopers of the 7th Cavalry nearly captured Pancho Villa in the mountains of Chihuahua.

subject: Battle of Guilford Court House
summary: The Revolutionary War battle that Cornwallis won on the field but lost in every way that mattered -- a Pyrrhic victory that sent the British stumbling toward Yorktown and the end of their American empire.

subject: Battle of Hanko (1941)
summary: Soviet troops held a leased naval base on Finnish soil for six months of trench warfare and lighthouse raids, then evacuated 23,000 men through Finnish minefields.

subject: Battle of Hegra Fortress
summary: In April 1940, 250 Norwegian volunteers and one nurse held a decommissioned mountain fortress against German forces for 25 days, becoming the last pocket of resistance in southern Norway.

subject: Battle of Heiligerlee (1568)
summary: On 23 May 1568, on a stretch of heath near a monastery in eastern Groningen, the Dutch Revolt began with a small ambush, an unlikely victory, and the death of a young man whose name still echoes in the Dutch national anthem.

subject: Battle of Hill 170
summary: In January 1945, British commandos clung to a wooded ridge in the Arakan swamps for four days under relentless Japanese shelling -- a stand that broke the Japanese 54th Division and earned one lieutenant a posthumous Victoria Cross.

story.title: The Battle of Hitotoribashi: A Son's Vengeance Against Impossible Odds

subject: Battle of Hitotoribashi
summary: In January 1586, eighteen-year-old Date Masamune -- the future One-Eyed Dragon of Oshu -- faced a coalition of 30,000 enemy troops with just 7,000 of his own near Motomiya Castle in Fukushima, seeking revenge for his father's murder.

subject: Battle of Hämeenlinna
summary: On 26 April 1918 a German division and Finnish White troops took Hämeenlinna from the Red Guard — and immediately built a prison camp where 2,300 people died.

subject: Battle of I-10
summary: For over a century, two border universities separated by 42 miles of Interstate 10 have waged one of college football's oldest and most fiercely local rivalries, competing for a silver prospector's shovel and civic bragging rights.

subject: Battle of Inverlochy (1431)
summary: A fifteenth-century battle near modern Fort William where Donald Balloch's Highland force destroyed a royalist army, killing the Earl of Caithness and over a thousand men.

subject: Battle of Jieqiao
summary: At a bridge crossing on the Qing River in 191 or 192 AD, disciplined crossbowmen shattered an elite cavalry charge, proving that infantry training could defeat mounted power in one of the Eastern Han dynasty's most tactically documented battles.

subject: Battle of Kadesh
summary: In 1274 BC, Ramesses II marched into a Hittite trap near the Orontes River -- then fought his way out in the most documented battle of the ancient world, a clash whose propaganda echoes survive on temple walls from Luxor to Abu Simbel.

subject: Battle of Kalijati
summary: The swift Japanese seizure of a vital airfield on Java's north coast in March 1942 doomed two Dutch counterattacks and set the stage for the fall of the entire Dutch East Indies.

subject: Battle of Karavia Bay
summary: One night in February 1944, five American destroyers crept into Rabaul's harbor mouth and traded fire with shore batteries that had been left to rot - the first surface action ever fought against the fortress the Japanese once called the Gibraltar of the Pacific.

subject: Battle of Kendari
summary: In a single day in January 1942, Japanese forces captured the best airfield in the Dutch East Indies -- not because their assault was brilliant, but because Dutch leadership had already collapsed.

subject: Battle of Kessler's Cross Lanes
summary: An August 1861 surprise attack scattered the 7th Ohio Infantry across the Nicholas County hills - and sent one Union major on an extraordinary 80-mile retreat through Confederate territory.

subject: Battle of Kiyosu Castle
summary: The series of battles from 1552 to 1554 where a seventeen-year-old Oda Nobunaga seized Kiyosu Castle from his own cousin, winning his first major victory and launching the campaign that would eventually unify Japan.

subject: Battle of Koljonvirta
summary: The last Swedish victory on Finnish soil, fought in October 1808 during the Finnish War, immortalized in Finnish national poetry through the legend of Sven Dufva defending a bridge against impossible odds.

subject: Battle of Kunduz (2015)
summary: The first major Afghan city to fall to the Taliban since 2001, Kunduz became a proving ground for Afghan security forces on their own -- and the site of a catastrophic airstrike on a hospital that killed 42 people.

subject: Battle of Kuwait International Airport
summary: The largest tank battle in Marine Corps history unfolded across three days in February 1991, as elements of 18 divisions clashed on the flat desert approaches to Kuwait International Airport.

subject: Battle of Landguard Fort
summary: On 2 July 1667, fifteen hundred Dutch marines landed on a Suffolk beach to take a fort defending Harwich harbour - and were repelled. It is recorded as the last opposed invasion of English soil.

subject: Battle of Lashio
summary: In July 2024, the Three Brotherhood Alliance captured the Myanmar military's Northeastern Command headquarters in Lashio, dealing the junta one of its most devastating defeats in the ongoing civil war.

subject: Battle of Ledra Palace
summary: In July 1974, a luxury hotel in central Nicosia became the front line of the Turkish invasion of Cyprus, and a small group of Greek Cypriot national guardsmen held it against paratroopers, mortar fire, and threats of napalm.

subject: Battle of Liberty Place
summary: A violent 1874 insurrection on Canal Street where 5,000 White League paramilitaries seized the Louisiana statehouse for three days, and whose commemorative monument took 143 years to remove.

subject: Battle of Lima Site 85
summary: The largest single ground combat loss of U.S. Air Force personnel in the Vietnam War, fought on a sacred Hmong mountaintop in Laos where a secret radar installation guided American bombers over North Vietnam.

subject: Battle of Lincoln (1141)
summary: The day in February 1141 when King Stephen was captured under his own castle walls, briefly toppling a king in the middle of the chaos that nearly tore England in two.

subject: Battle of Lincoln (1878)
summary: The five-day firefight that climaxed the Lincoln County War, trapped Billy the Kid in a burning adobe house, and cemented the mythology of the Old West.

subject: Battle of Lindley's Fort
summary: A July 1776 backcountry battle where 150 South Carolina militia held off a Cherokee-Loyalist force decorated with war paint, just outside present-day Laurens.

subject: Battle of Lindley's Mill
summary: A four-hour Revolutionary War ambush along Cane Creek in September 1781, where 300 Patriot militiamen tried and failed to rescue North Carolina's governor from a column of Loyalists - and where Colonel Hector McNeill and Major John Nall killed each other in single combat at the same instant.

subject: Battle of Linlithgow Bridge
summary: A mother's gambit to free her teenage royal son turned a ford on the River Avon into one of Scotland's bloodier 1526 skirmishes.

subject: Battle of Lisnagarvey
summary: A one-sided rout in Ulster on 6 December 1649 — the engagement that broke Scottish-Royalist resistance to Cromwell's Parliament and sealed the fate of Carrickfergus.

story.title: The Battle of Longue-Pointe: Ethan Allen's Worst Idea

subject: Battle of Longue-Pointe
summary: On September 25, 1775, the folk hero who had captured Fort Ticonderoga attempted to seize Montreal with 110 men and no backup -- and ended up in chains, shipped to England, and eventually immortalized in a city park named for his humiliation.

subject: Battle of Lostwithiel
summary: Charles I personally cornered an entire Parliamentarian army in the Fowey valley in August 1644. The greatest defeat Parliament would suffer in the Civil War.

subject: Battle of Lyndanisse
summary: On a midsummer evening in 1219, an Estonian army nearly drove a Danish crusader force into the sea — and according to a legend Danes still tell, that was the moment a red flag with a white cross fell from heaven and gave Denmark its national banner.

subject: Battle of Lyngør
summary: A 15-minute naval barrage in 1812 among Norway's narrow skerries ended Denmark-Norway's last warship and, with it, the kingdom's role in the Napoleonic Wars.

subject: Battle of Makryplagi
summary: In 1264, at a mountain pass near Gardiki Castle on the borders of Messenia and Arcadia, a Frankish Achaean army shattered the Byzantine forces attempting to reconquer the Peloponnese — sealed by an exchange of words between the defeated general and his captor that cut to the heart of who really owned the land.

subject: Battle of Maldon
summary: On a tidal causeway in Essex in August 991, an English ealdorman let a Viking army cross to fight him on level ground, and the Old English poem about his death may be the greatest battle elegy ever written.

subject: Battle of Mazagran
