summary: A minor colonial siege that Paris turned into a national legend, complete with medals, merchandise, and a replica fort on the Champs-Elysees -- until London called it a hoax.

subject: Battle of Meadow Bridge
summary: Trapped between Richmond's guns and a flooded river, Sheridan's cavalry crossed a stripped railroad bridge tie by tie on May 12, 1864 - and escaped a Confederate trap.

subject: Battle of Meung-sur-Loire
summary: In June 1429, Joan of Arc's forces bypassed a fortified town and castle to seize a critical Loire bridge, severing English movement in a lightning strike that helped turn the Hundred Years' War.

subject: Battle of Mobley's Meeting House
summary: In June 1780, after a string of Patriot defeats, a small Whig force surprised a Loyalist camp west of Winnsboro - one of the first symbolic wins of the southern campaign, where most casualties came from falls down a steep embankment.

subject: Battle of Modon (1500)
summary: In August 1500, the Ottoman admiral Kemal Reis seized the Venetian fortress of Modon on the southwestern tip of Greece, ending over a century of Venetian control and stripping Venice of what it called 'the two eyes of the Republic.'

subject: Battle of Moel-y-don
summary: On 6 November 1282, a Welsh army caught an English force halfway across a bridge of boats on the Menai Strait and drove them into a rising tide.

subject: Battle of Monte Cassino
summary: Four Allied assaults over four months in 1944 tried to break through the German Gustav Line at a Benedictine abbey founded in 529 AD -- a battle that cost 75,000 casualties and destroyed one of Western civilization's oldest monasteries.

subject: Battle of Mortimer's Cross
summary: At dawn on 2 February 1461, three suns rose over a Herefordshire crossroads, and a panicked teenage commander turned them into a divine omen that won him a kingdom.

subject: Battle of Mount Longdon
summary: The bloodiest British battle of the Falklands War, a night of hand-to-hand fighting in the rocks above Stanley where a British paratrooper won a posthumous Victoria Cross and young conscripts on both sides paid a terrible price.

subject: Battle of Muraki Castle
summary: On January 24, 1554, the young Oda Nobunaga loaded arquebus-armed troops onto ships at Atsuta port, sailed down Ise Bay, and blasted his way into Muraki Castle -- an amphibious gunpowder assault that announced a new kind of Japanese warfare.

subject: Battle of Musgrove Mill
summary: On August 19, 1780, 200 Patriot partisans outnumbered two-to-one drew Loyalist regulars into an ambush at a ford of the Enoree River - a small fight that lifted backcountry morale after the disaster at Camden.

subject: Battle of Nalapani
summary: In 1814, a Nepali garrison of six hundred held a small hill fort near Dehradun against thousands of British and Indian troops for over a month, establishing the Gurkha reputation that endures to this day.

subject: Battle of Namutoni
summary: In 1904, five hundred Ondonga warriors under Chief Nehale lyaMpingana overran a German fort held by just seven men on the edge of the Etosha Pan.

subject: Battle of Natural Bridge
summary: On March 6, 1865, a ragtag force of Confederate soldiers, old men, and teenage cadets as young as 14 held a river crossing south of Tallahassee, keeping it the only Southern capital east of the Mississippi never captured by the Union.

subject: Battle of Naulila
summary: A mistranslation at a remote fort on the Angola-Namibia border in 1914 spiraled into German reprisals, a famous case in international law, and a catastrophe that killed more than 150,000 people who never fired a shot.

subject: Battle of Nesbit Moor (1355)
summary: A textbook border ambush in August 1355: Scots and French knights lured an English garrison out of Norham Castle and won the day, leaving a place name behind - Slaughter Hill.

subject: Battle of Neville's Cross
summary: A 1346 battle where a 12,000-strong Scottish invasion army, summoned by the French king as a diversion, was crushed half a mile from Durham Cathedral and its king captured hiding under a bridge.

subject: Battle of New Market
summary: The only battle in American history where a school's student body fought as an organized combat unit, the 1864 clash in the Shenandoah Valley sent VMI cadets as young as 15 into the mud and gunfire.

subject: Battle of Newburn
summary: The 1640 battle where a 20,000-strong Scottish Covenanter army crushed a smaller English force at a Tyne ford, capturing Newcastle and forcing Charles I to recall the Parliament that would eventually undo him.

subject: Battle of Nicopolis (1798)
summary: In October 1798, a small French garrison and their local allies made a desperate stand among the ruins of ancient Nicopolis against the forces of Ali Pasha of Ioannina — and the town of Preveza paid the price.

subject: Battle of Ojinaga
summary: Pancho Villa's decisive victory that ended Federal control of northern Mexico, captured on film by American cameras while the legendary writer Ambrose Bierce vanished into history.

subject: Battle of Old Byland
summary: In October 1322, Robert the Bruce came within minutes of capturing the King of England at his own dinner table in Rievaulx Abbey.

subject: Battle of Orewin Bridge
summary: The 11 December 1282 battle near Builth Wells where Llywelyn ap Gruffudd, the last sovereign Prince of Wales, was lured from his army and killed - ending Welsh independence.

subject: Battle of Oswestry
summary: On a summer afternoon in 1644, 200 Parliamentarian foot soldiers took a Royalist garrison town by spies' intelligence and a single cannon blast through the main gate.

subject: Battle of Paitilla Airport
summary: A SEAL team assault to destroy Manuel Noriega's escape plane became one of the most controversial special operations engagements in U.S. military history.

story.title: The Battle of Paulus Hook: A 23-Year-Old's Midnight Gamble

subject: Battle of Paulus Hook
summary: In August 1779, a young Princeton graduate named Light Horse Harry Lee led 400 Continental soldiers on a 14-mile nighttime march through New Jersey swamps to raid a British fort at what is now downtown Jersey City, capturing 158 prisoners and earning the only gold medal Congress gave to a non-general during the Revolution.

subject: Battle of Pickett's Mill
summary: In the tangled Georgia woods near a creek named for a grist mill, Ambrose Bierce watched his brigade march into what he instantly recognized as a 'criminal blunder' -- a failed flanking attack that became one of the Atlanta campaign's forgotten bloodbaths.

subject: Battle of Piperdean
summary: A 1435 Anglo-Scottish border skirmish that William Douglas, 2nd Earl of Angus, won by attacking the English column before it could reach Dunbar Castle.

subject: Battle of Platte Bridge
summary: The largest coordinated Indigenous offensive on the Great Plains brought 3,000 warriors against a wooden bridge on the North Platte River, featuring a roster of legendary names including Crazy Horse, Red Cloud, and Roman Nose.

subject: Battle of Port-Républicain
summary: When a British fleet seized revolutionary Port-au-Prince in 1794, the city's defenders fought from fort to fort in a battle shaped as much by betrayal and rainstorms as by guns.

subject: Battle of Powick Bridge
summary: The first cavalry engagement of the English Civil War, fought in a meadow south of Worcester on 23 September 1642 - the day Prince Rupert's name became feared.

subject: Battle of Praça da Sé
summary: On October 7, 1934, anti-fascists and Integralists clashed in the heart of São Paulo's cathedral square, producing Brazil's first major street battle against homegrown fascism.

subject: Battle of Qala-i-Jangi
summary: A prisoner uprising at a 19th-century fortress near Mazar-i-Sharif in November 2001 became one of the bloodiest engagements of the early Afghanistan war, killing the first American combat casualty and producing a landmark Supreme Court case.

subject: Battle of Quifangondo
summary: On the eve of Angolan independence in 1975, a chaotic assault on a small village's waterworks became the decisive battle of a proxy war involving Cuba, South Africa, Zaire, and the CIA.

subject: Battle of Ramsour's Mill
summary: A savage Revolutionary War clash in North Carolina where neighbors, brothers, and friends fought each other with muskets used as clubs, splitting a community apart on a foggy June morning in 1780.

subject: Battle of Rowton Heath
summary: On 24 September 1645, King Charles I climbed a tower on the walls of Chester and watched his last northern army be destroyed on the heath below.

subject: Battle of Saguntum
summary: To defend Sagunto's ancient hill from Napoleon's army in 1811, its defenders tore down a Roman theatre for stone - and still lost the battle that opened the road to Valencia.

subject: Battle of Saint George
summary: On 9 September 1320, the Byzantine governor Andronikos Asen captured the castle of Saint George in Arcadia by ruse and ambushed a Latin relief force, securing the Arcadian heartland of the Morea for Byzantium.

subject: Battle of Saint-Eustache
summary: On December 14, 1837, 201 poorly armed Patriotes barricaded inside a church faced 1,280 British regulars and artillery in the decisive battle of the Lower Canada Rebellion -- a four-hour siege that ended with the church in flames and 70 rebels dead, their leader shot jumping from a window.

subject: Battle of Saltley Gate
summary: On 10 February 1972, fifteen thousand pickets stood outside a Birmingham coke depot and the chief constable closed the gates. The miners' strike had its pivotal victory, and a regional union official named Arthur Scargill became a national figure.

subject: Battle of San Roque
summary: The battlefield where General José María Paz won the first of four victories now lies beneath the waters of a popular resort lake.

subject: Battle of San Salvador (1641)
summary: A Dutch-led expedition against the Spanish fortress at Keelung in 1641 that failed militarily but succeeded politically, turning Spain's indigenous allies against them and setting the stage for the fall of Spanish Formosa.

subject: Battle of Santa Rosa
summary: In fourteen minutes on March 20, 1856, a Costa Rican army routed an invading force of American and European filibusters at Hacienda Santa Rosa, crushing William Walker's dream of a slave-holding empire in Central America.

subject: Battle of Santa Rosa Island
summary: An early Civil War night raid on a Florida barrier island where Confederate forces surprised Union troops but failed to capture Fort Pickens, one of only four Southern forts that never fell to the Confederacy.

subject: Battle of Saumur (1940)
summary: In June 1940, after France had already asked for a ceasefire, 800 cavalry school cadets held the Loire bridges at Saumur for two days against 10,000 German troops.

subject: Battle of Savage's Station
summary: The fourth of the Seven Days Battles, June 29, 1862, where Magruder hit the retreating Union rear guard and 2,500 wounded soldiers were abandoned to capture in a field hospital.

subject: Battle of Sittang Bridge
summary: In February 1942, the desperate decision to blow the Sittang Bridge with two brigades still on the wrong side sealed the fate of Burma and opened the road to Rangoon for the Japanese advance.

story.title: The Battle of Spanish Fort: Twelve Days That Ended the War on Mobile Bay

subject: Battle of Spanish Fort
summary: In the spring of 1865, roughly 2,000 Confederate defenders held Spanish Fort for twelve days against a Union force of 32,000, one of the last major sieges of the Civil War before Mobile fell.

subject: Battle of Spotsylvania Court House
summary: Two weeks of trench fighting at a crossroads in Virginia that gave the Civil War its Bloody Angle - 32,000 casualties, an oak tree cut down by musket fire, and Grant's promise to fight it out if it took all summer.

subject: Battle of St. Louis
summary: Most Americans do not know that the Revolutionary War was fought on the Mississippi -- but on May 26, 1780, a Spanish captain, a French militia, and a hastily built stone tower held off a British-allied force of nearly 1,000 warriors to defend the village that would become St. Louis.

subject: Battle of Stamford Bridge
summary: On 25 September 1066, King Harold Godwinson destroyed a Norwegian invasion force in a battle that ended the Viking Age in England, only to march south and meet his own fate at Hastings three weeks later.

subject: Battle of Sufetula (647)
summary: At the Roman ruins of Sufetula in 647 AD, a rebel Byzantine governor met a Rashidun Caliphate army in a battle that shattered imperial control over North Africa forever.

subject: Battle of Suoi Bong Trang
summary: A night battle in the Vietnamese jungle where Australian and American forces repelled a massive Viet Cong assault while defending road-building engineers in Binh Duong Province in February 1966.

subject: Battle of Tadcaster
summary: On 7 December 1642, two Parliamentarian forces held a stone bridge over the River Wharfe for six hours against four times their number - then slipped away in darkness when the gunpowder ran out.

subject: Battle of Tarakan (1945)
summary: An Australian brigade fought for weeks to capture a small island airfield that proved too damaged to use, turning a well-executed amphibious assault into one of the Pacific War's most debated operations.

subject: Battle of Tarbat
summary: A 1480s clan battle that ended with a Mackay raiding party burned alive in the sanctuary church at Portmahomack.

subject: Battle of Te-li-Ssu
summary: Fought on June 14-15, 1904, during the Russo-Japanese War, the Battle of Te-li-Ssu was a decisive Japanese flanking victory that ended Russia's only offensive attempt to relieve the besieged fortress of Port Arthur.

subject: Battle of Thị Nại Bay
summary: In February 1283, a Mongol fleet of 5,000 men crashed into Champa's wooden coastal fortress at Thị Nại Bay — and won the battle while losing the war, as the Cham king retreated to the mountains and refused to surrender.

story.title: Battle of Tippecanoe: The Fight That Made a President

subject: Battle of Tippecanoe
summary: A pre-dawn attack on November 7, 1811, near the confluence of the Tippecanoe and Wabash rivers pitted a thousand American soldiers against Tecumseh's confederacy, destroyed the village of Prophetstown, and gave William Henry Harrison the nickname that carried him to the White House.

subject: Battle of Tipton Green
summary: A Civil War skirmish near Dudley Castle on 12 June 1644, where both sides claimed victory and a stubborn Parliamentary general refused to leave his cannons behind.

subject: Battle of Torrence's Tavern
summary: A widow's tavern, rain-soaked gunpowder, and Tarleton's dragoons collide in a confused afternoon skirmish that helps decide the fate of the Southern Campaign.

subject: Battle of Triangle Hill
summary: A 42-day battle in 1952 where UN forces with overwhelming firepower failed to dislodge Chinese defenders from tunnel-laced ridges near Korea's Iron Triangle, halting American offensive ambitions for the rest of the war.

subject: Battle of Trincomalee
summary: A 1782 naval clash off Ceylon's eastern coast where a brilliant but mutinous French fleet under Suffren fought a dogged British squadron under Hughes, in a forgotten theater of the American Revolution.

subject: Battle of Tsimba Ridge
summary: Three weeks of jungle fighting in northern Bougainville where an Australian battalion ground through a horseshoe-shaped volcanic fortress held by a Japanese colonel who was a master of jungle warfare.

subject: Battle of Tuthill
summary: On All Souls' Day 1401, Owain Glyndwr raised a golden dragon over a Welsh army outside Caernarfon Castle - and lost three hundred men trying to take the walls.

subject: Battle of Uji (1180)
summary: The desperate bridge fight at Uji in 1180 that killed a disgraced prince and an aging poet-warrior but ignited the Genpei War, the five-year samurai conflict that would reshape Japan forever.

subject: Battle of Upton
summary: Eighteen Parliamentary soldiers crawled across a broken bridge in pre-dawn darkness on 28 August 1651, set off a fight inside a burning church, and made the Battle of Worcester possible.

subject: Battle of Utsunomiya Castle
summary: In May 1868, samurai, commoners, and the remnants of the Shinsengumi seized Utsunomiya Castle in a lightning strike during the Boshin War -- only to find themselves trapped between imperial forces closing in from two directions.

subject: Battle of Valtetsi
summary: On 12–13 May 1821, Greek revolutionaries holding four fortified tower houses at Valtetsi repelled a combined Ottoman and Albanian force of 5,000 men — the first decisive Greek victory of the War of Independence.

subject: Battle of Vella Lavella (land)
summary: The bypass that worked: Allied troops skipped Kolombangara's 12,000-strong Japanese garrison and landed on Vella Lavella instead, trading a frontal assault for an airfield.

subject: Battle of Veracruz (1838)
summary: A dispute over a ransacked pastry shop triggered a French naval bombardment that destroyed a fortress considered impregnable, launched the era of modern shell artillery, and gave Santa Anna the war wound that revived his political career.

subject: Battle of Wakde
summary: For three days in May 1944, 1,500 American soldiers crossed a two-mile channel to take an island 1.5 miles long - and paid for every yard of its coral airfield.

subject: Battle of Walcheren Causeway
summary: For three days in late October and early November 1944, Canadian and Scottish soldiers had to cross a 40-metre-wide raised road between mud flats to reach a German garrison dug in on a flooded island - a small, brutal action that has lived in Calgary's regimental memory ever since.

subject: Battle of Weihaiwei
summary: The last major battle of the First Sino-Japanese War, where a Chinese admiral refused surrender and chose death, and the fall of a fortress considered superior to Hong Kong shattered Qing maritime power.

subject: Battle of Wetzell's Mill
summary: Nine days before Guilford Courthouse, two armies raced for a Carolina creek crossing. The smaller force lost the ford but bought the time that won the war.

subject: Battle of White Sulphur Springs
summary: Two days of fighting at Rocky Gap in August 1863 - a Confederate victory that ended Brigadier General William W. Averell's raid against a Greenbrier County law library.

subject: Battle of Williamsburg
summary: On May 5, 1862, more than 70,000 soldiers fought through mud and abatis around Fort Magruder in the Peninsula Campaign's first pitched battle.

subject: Battle of Winnington Bridge
summary: The last battle of the English Civil War wasn't really a battle. It was nine years after Charles I lost his head, a stuttering Royalist rising fell apart on a Cheshire riverbank, and the country shrugged.

subject: Battle of Yan Province
summary: A desperate struggle between warlords Cao Cao and Lu Bu for control of Yan Province in 194-195 AD, featuring betrayal, ambush, famine, and one of history's luckiest escapes through a burning gate.

subject: Battle of York
summary: On April 27, 1813, an American force of 1,700 soldiers stormed York, the capital of Upper Canada, in a chaotic battle that killed a brigadier general, saw the British blow up their own fort, and set off a cycle of retaliatory burning that would eventually reach Washington, D.C.

subject: Battle of the Bogue
summary: On 23–26 February 1841, British forces stormed the Humen forts guarding the Pearl River gateway to Canton, killing hundreds of Chinese defenders including Admiral Guan Tianpei — a decisive engagement of the First Opium War.

subject: Battle of the Bosporus
summary: On a storm-lashed February night in 1352, nearly 90 ships from three Mediterranean powers collided in the dark narrows of the Bosporus, fighting over who would control the gateway to the Black Sea.

story.title: Battle of the Brig of Dee

subject: Battle of the Brig of Dee
summary: Two days of cannon fire at a 16th-century bridge south of Aberdeen — the only serious fighting of the First Bishops' War, won by a clever feint upstream.

subject: Battle of the Hotels
summary: In the opening months of the Lebanese Civil War, rival militias fought for control of Beirut's luxury hotel district, turning the Holiday Inn, the Phoenicia, and the St. Georges into fortified sniper nests and artillery platforms in a battle that lasted from October 1975 to April 1976.

subject: Battle of the Milvian Bridge
summary: A single battle at a bridge over the Tiber in AD 312 between rival emperors Constantine and Maxentius reshaped the Roman Empire and set Christianity on the path from persecuted sect to state religion.

subject: Battle of the North Inch
summary: The 1396 trial by combat in Perth where thirty Highland champions from each side fought to the death in a purpose-built arena, watched by King Robert III -- a spectacle so vivid it inspired Walter Scott's novel The Fair Maid of Perth.

story.title: Battle of the Persian Gate: Persia's Thermopylae

subject: Battle of the Persian Gate
summary: In the winter of 330 BC, a Persian commander named Ariobarzanes held Alexander the Great's army at bay for a month in a narrow Zagros mountain pass, inflicting some of Alexander's heaviest losses before being outflanked and overwhelmed.

subject: Battle of the Spoiling Dyke
summary: In 1578, MacDonalds burned a church full of MacLeod worshippers on Skye, then found themselves trapped by a falling tide -- the MacLeod counter-attack buried the dead under a collapsed turf wall.

subject: Battle of the Twin Villages
summary: In 1759, a Spanish army marched north from San Antonio to punish the Wichita tribes -- only to find a moated, palisaded fortress flying the French flag, defended by warriors carrying French muskets, with Comanche tipis ringing the perimeter.

subject: Battle off Horaniu
summary: A brief, inconclusive night action in the Solomons where American radar found a Japanese convoy, sank five small ships, and failed to stop the barges that were the whole point of the voyage.

subject: Beijing Television Cultural Center fire
summary: An unsanctioned fireworks display on Chinese New Year 2009 engulfed a nearly completed skyscraper next to CCTV's iconic headquarters, sparking a national scandal over hubris and censorship.

subject: Berkeley Balcony Collapse
summary: A 2015 balcony collapse at a Berkeley apartment building that killed six young Irish visitors and one Irish-American, exposed construction failures, and changed California building inspection law.

subject: Bernera Riot
summary: In 1874 on a small Hebridean island, three crofters were arrested, hundreds marched on the laird's castle, and Scotland's century of evictions finally began to crack.

subject: Beyazıt Massacre
summary: On 16 March 1978, seven students leaving Istanbul University were killed in a bomb and gun attack at Beyazıt Square — a day remembered in Turkey as one of the starkest acts of political violence against young people in the country's modern history.

subject: Birmingham pub bombings
summary: The 1974 bombing of two Birmingham pubs killed 21 people and injured 182, leading to one of the worst miscarriages of justice in British legal history when six innocent men were imprisoned for sixteen years.

story.title: Black Tom: The Night German Spies Blew Up New York Harbor

subject: Black Tom explosion
summary: On July 30, 1916, German saboteurs detonated a massive munitions depot on a man-made island in New York Harbor, producing one of the largest non-nuclear explosions in history, sending shrapnel into the Statue of Liberty, and permanently closing Lady Liberty's torch to visitors.

subject: Blue Market Massacre
summary: On 13 March 1999, three attackers set fire to the Blue Market, a small department store in Göztepe on Istanbul's Asian side, killing 13 civilians who had come to shop on a Saturday afternoon.

subject: Boksburg explosion
summary: On Christmas Eve 2022, a gas tanker wedged beneath a railway bridge in Boksburg and caught fire; the explosion that followed killed 41 people, many of them nurses and patients at the hospital next door.

subject: Boland Hall fire
summary: A 2000 dormitory fire at Seton Hall University in South Orange, New Jersey, started as a drunken prank and killed three students - transforming campus fire safety standards nationwide.

subject: Bologna massacre
summary: A clock frozen at 10:25 marks the moment a suitcase bomb tore through Bologna's central railway station on August 2, 1980, killing 85 people in the deadliest terrorist attack in postwar Italy.

subject: Bombing of Wewak
summary: Over five days in August 1943, the Fifth Air Force destroyed about 170 Japanese aircraft at Wewak using parachute-retarded fragmentation bombs and a secret airfield kept hidden with dust.

subject: Botroseya Church bombing
summary: A 2016 suicide bombing at a chapel adjoining Cairo's most important Coptic cathedral killed 29 worshippers and exposed the vulnerability of Egypt's Christian minority.

story.title: Bribie Island Second World War Fortifications

subject: Bribie Island Second World War Fortifications
summary: Heritage-listed concrete gun emplacements, searchlights, and mine-control huts built to guard the doorway to Brisbane in 1942 -- now half-buried in shifting dunes and lantana, a haunting fort that the sea is slowly carrying away.

subject: Bridge Gulch massacre
summary: At dawn on April 23, 1852, a posse of 70 men attacked a sleeping Wintu encampment in Trinity County, killing more than 150 people who had no connection to the crime they were being punished for.

subject: Brihadeeswarar temple fire
summary: On June 7, 1997, a firecracker ignited thatched ceremonial structures at the Brihadisvara Temple in Thanjavur during its consecration ceremony, killing 48 people in the fire and stampede that followed -- a sacred occasion turned to catastrophe.

subject: British expedition to Palembang
summary: In April 1812, a British fleet pushed up the Musi River to seize the Sultanate of Palembang, only to find the sultan had fled and left his fortress empty.

subject: Broken at the River's Edge
summary: When a Boeing 737 overran the short runway at Manokwari's Rendani Airport in 2010, it broke into three pieces -- and every person aboard survived.

subject: Bronx-Lebanon Hospital attack
summary: On June 30, 2017, a former physician returned to the Bronx-Lebanon Hospital Center with a concealed rifle and opened fire on the staff who had once been his colleagues, killing one doctor and wounding six others before taking his own life.

subject: Brooklyn Theatre fire
summary: On December 5, 1876, a fire broke out during a performance of The Two Orphans at the Brooklyn Theatre, killing at least 278 people in the third-deadliest theater fire in American history, most of them trapped in the upper gallery by smoke and a single inadequate stairway.

subject: Burma campaign
summary: The forgotten theater where a million Allied soldiers fought through jungle, monsoon, and disease to inflict Japan's greatest land defeat of World War II.

subject: Burunga massacre
summary: On May 26, 1971, Pakistani soldiers lured Hindu villagers to the Burunga High School grounds in Sylhet with promises of peace cards, then systematically separated, shot, and burned at least 71 people in one of the Bangladesh Liberation War's targeted ethnic killings.

subject: Caldecott Tunnel fire
summary: A 1982 gasoline tanker fire in the Caldecott Tunnel that killed seven people and changed how engineers think about tunnel safety and the chimney effect.

subject: Cambodian campaign
summary: In 1970 two armies crossed into Cambodia to capture a headquarters that had packed up and left six weeks earlier — and the country they entered never recovered.

subject: Campinas Cathedral shooting
summary: On 11 December 2018, five people were killed during Mass at the Metropolitan Cathedral in Campinas, Brazil -- a tragedy that shook a community and drew responses from the Pope and Brazil's president.

subject: Canadian Pacific Air Lines Flight 402
summary: On a fog-shrouded night in March 1966, a DC-8 struck a seawall at Haneda Airport after its crew reversed a decision to divert -- and less than 24 hours later, a second jetliner taxied past the wreckage and itself crashed near Mount Fuji, killing everyone aboard.

subject: Carandiru massacre
summary: On October 2, 1992, military police killed 111 prisoners at São Paulo's overcrowded Carandiru Penitentiary — one of Brazil's worst human rights violations and a tragedy whose legal reckoning remains unfinished.

subject: Carmen de Patagones School Shooting
summary: On a spring morning in 2004, three teenagers were killed in their own classroom in a small Patagonian town, in a tragedy that Argentina still mourns and struggles to understand.

subject: Castle Gate Mine disaster
summary: A single match struck in darkness triggered three explosions that killed 172 men in Utah's second-deadliest mining disaster, leaving a town full of widows and fatherless children.

subject: Catterick Bridge Explosion
summary: A wartime ammunition explosion in the goods yard at Catterick Bridge railway station on 4 February 1944 killed twelve people and injured over a hundred, largely hushed up under wartime censorship.

subject: Cave of the Patriarchs massacre
summary: On February 25, 1994, an American-Israeli settler opened fire on Palestinian worshippers during dawn prayers at the Ibrahimi Mosque in Hebron, killing 29 people and wounding 125 in an act that derailed the Oslo peace process.

subject: Central Government War Headquarters
summary: 120 feet beneath the Wiltshire countryside lies a 35-acre underground city built to house the British government - and four thousand people - through a nuclear war that, in the end, never came.

subject: Charing Cross Roof Collapse
summary: Twelve minutes' warning saved hundreds when the wrought-iron arch over Charing Cross station collapsed in 1905 - but six men still died, including three rebuilding the theatre next door.

story.title: Charleston: The Holy City Where the Civil War Began

subject: Charleston
summary: The South Carolina port city where history weighs heavy on pastel houses - where the first shots of the Civil War were fired at Fort Sumter, where the slave trade concentrated, and where the preservation of antebellum beauty requires reckoning with antebellum horror.

subject: Charleston church shooting
summary: On June 17, 2015, a white supremacist murdered nine people during Bible study at Emanuel African Methodist Episcopal Church in Charleston - the oldest Black church in the South - an act of hatred that catalyzed the removal of the Confederate flag from the South Carolina State House.

subject: Chernobyl disaster
summary: The April 26, 1986 explosion of Reactor 4 at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant in Soviet Ukraine killed 31 people in the immediate aftermath, evacuated 350,000 from a 30-kilometer zone, exposed roughly 600,000 cleanup workers to radiation, and remains the worst nuclear power accident in history.

story.title: Chicago: The City That Rose From Its Own Ashes

subject: Chicago
summary: The Illinois metropolis where the Great Fire of 1871 destroyed 17,500 buildings and killed 300 - then created the opportunity to build the modern American city, inventing the skyscraper, reversing a river, and proving that catastrophe could become catalyst for becoming the 'City of Broad Shoulders.'

subject: Childers Palace Backpackers Hostel fire
summary: On a winter night in 2000, fifteen young travellers died in a hostel fire in a small Queensland town that has spent the years since remembering them.

subject: China Airlines Flight 140
summary: A 1994 aviation disaster at Nagoya Airport where a fatal conflict between human pilots and an engaged autopilot killed 264 of 271 people aboard an Airbus A300.

subject: China Airlines Flight 204
summary: On 26 October 1989, China Airlines Flight 204 departed Hualien Airport and struck a mountain ten minutes later, killing all 54 people on board — a tragedy that exposed how a single procedural error, unchecked, can become catastrophic.

subject: China Airlines Flight 642
summary: On 22 August 1999, a China Airlines MD-11 rolled, flipped, and caught fire at Hong Kong's new Chek Lap Kok airport during Tropical Storm Sam — killing three of the 315 people on board and becoming the new airport's first fatal accident.

subject: Chiquola Mill Massacre
summary: In September 1934, the mayor of Honea Path, South Carolina ordered armed men to fire into a crowd of striking textile workers -- then ensured no one was ever held accountable.

story.title: The Clerkenwell Outrage: The Explosion That Created Special Branch

subject: Clerkenwell explosion
summary: An 1867 Fenian bombing intended to free a prisoner from Clerkenwell Prison killed 12 civilians, led to the last public hanging in England, and ultimately pushed Gladstone toward Irish Home Rule.

story.title: Cleveland Elementary: The Shooting That Changed the Law

subject: Cleveland Elementary
summary: On January 17, 1989, five children were killed and thirty-one people wounded at a Stockton elementary school in an attack that catalyzed California's first assault weapons ban and exposed the particular vulnerability of refugee communities in America.

subject: Cleveland Elementary School Shooting (San Diego)
summary: On January 29, 1979, a sixteen-year-old opened fire on a San Diego elementary school from across the street, killing two adults and wounding eight children — and later told a reporter she did it because she didn't like Mondays.

subject: Colfax massacre
summary: On Easter Sunday 1873, the deadliest single act of racial violence during Reconstruction unfolded at a Louisiana courthouse, killing up to 153 Black men and producing a Supreme Court ruling that gutted civil rights enforcement for a century.

subject: Collapse of Cần Thơ Bridge
summary: On September 26, 2007, a 90-meter section of the Can Tho Bridge approach ramp collapsed from a height of 30 meters onto workers below, killing 54 and seriously injuring 80 in Vietnam's worst construction disaster.

subject: Collapse of the Space Building
summary: A 24-story residential tower in Medellin's upscale El Poblado neighborhood collapsed in 2013 due to catastrophic structural design failures, killing 12 and exposing systemic flaws in Colombia's building regulations.

story.title: The Collinwood School Fire: 175 Lost in Less Than an Hour

subject: Collinwood school fire
summary: On March 4, 1908, a fire at Cleveland's Lake View School killed 172 students, two teachers, and one rescuer - a disaster that transformed school building codes across America forever.

subject: Columbine Mine massacre
summary: On a cold November morning in 1927, five hundred striking coal miners carrying American flags marched to a company town gate, where state police opened fire, killing six unarmed workers.

subject: Comayagua prison fire
summary: On the night of February 14, 2012, a fire swept through the overcrowded National Penitentiary in Comayagua, Honduras, killing 361 people in the deadliest prison fire ever recorded.

subject: Connellan air disaster
summary: On 5 January 1977, a disgruntled former employee stole a Beechcraft Baron and flew it into the Connellan Airways complex at Alice Springs Airport, killing five people in one of Australia's only deliberate aircraft attacks.

subject: Cornwall Court Fire
summary: On the morning of 10 August 2008, a fire broke out in a Mong Kok nightclub and tore through Cornwall Court — a 15-storey Nathan Road building — killing four people including two firefighters who gave away their oxygen equipment to save the residents they were trying to reach.

subject: Crane Flat Fire Lookout
summary: Yosemite's first fire lookout, built in 1931 to disappear into its meadow rather than dominate it - a stone-and-timber tower that became a prototype for how America builds in its wildest places.

subject: Crimean Campaign
summary: For 250 days the fortress-city of Sevastopol held out against siege before it fell - the centerpiece of a brutal two-year struggle for Crimea in the Second World War.

subject: Cromañón Nightclub Fire
summary: On 30 December 2004, 194 people - most of them young, some of them children - died in a Buenos Aires concert hall whose exits had been chained shut.

subject: Cubana de Aviación Flight 389
summary: The 1998 runway overrun that forced Quito to finally move its airport out of the city, after a Tupolev Tu-154 plowed into a neighborhood soccer field.

subject: Dahlerau Train Disaster
summary: An entire graduating class came home from a school trip in May 1971 and nearly didn't arrive - the deadliest accident in West German history.

story.title: The Dawson College Shooting: Montreal's Third School Tragedy

subject: Dawson College shooting
summary: On a September lunchtime in 2006, a gunman opened fire at a downtown Montreal college, killing one student and wounding nineteen others -- the third fatal school shooting in a city still haunted by the Ecole Polytechnique massacre seventeen years earlier.

subject: De Punt Fire
summary: On a spring evening in 2008, three Dutch firefighters walked into a building that looked routine. None of them came out, and the inquiry that followed rewrote how the Netherlands fights industrial fires.

subject: De la Concorde overpass collapse
summary: A routine Saturday drive across a Laval overpass became a nightmare in 2006, when decades of design flaws, shoddy construction, and neglected maintenance conspired to bring a section of the Boulevard de la Concorde bridge crashing down onto Autoroute 19.

subject: Deal barracks bombing
summary: On 22 September 1989, the IRA killed eleven Royal Marine bandsmen at the School of Music in Deal. They were young men who, as the memorial inscription says, only ever wanted to play music.

subject: December 2016 Istanbul Bombings
summary: On the night of 10 December 2016, two bombs outside the Vodafone Park stadium in Beşiktaş killed 48 people — among them 39 police officers who had been doing their jobs when the attack came.

subject: Dee Bridge disaster
summary: The 1847 collapse of Robert Stephenson's cast-iron bridge at Chester killed five people and changed the future of British engineering forever.

subject: Deeper Life Bible Church shooting
summary: A 2012 church shooting near Okene, Nigeria, killed 19 worshippers preparing for Bible study -- and a retaliatory mosque attack the next day killed three more, exposing the fragile religious fault line running through central Nigeria.

subject: Diorama "Battle of the Dnieper"
summary: Inside a painted canvas the size of a house, one of the deadliest river crossings in history unfolds around the viewer in Dnipro.

subject: Doñana disaster
summary: When a mine tailings dam burst near Seville in 1998, toxic sludge raced down the Guadiamar River toward one of Europe's largest nature reserves, poisoning 4,600 hectares and threatening half a million migratory birds.

subject: Dunblane massacre
summary: The 1996 shooting at Dunblane Primary School killed sixteen children and their teacher, devastating a small Scottish town and transforming Britain's gun laws forever.

subject: Dundee school shooting
summary: The 1967 shooting at St John's High School in Dundee, where teacher Nanette Hanson gave her life protecting her pupils -- an act of courage that earned her the Albert Medal, Britain's highest civilian honour for bravery.

story.title: Dynamite, Detectives, and the Governor's Porch

subject: Dynamite, Detectives, and the Governor's Porch
summary: When twenty-five sticks of dynamite exploded outside California's Governor's Mansion in 1917, the real mystery was not who planted the bomb but who wanted people to think the IWW did it.

subject: East African campaign (World War I)
summary: The forgotten World War I theatre where German commander Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck tied down nearly a million Allied personnel across four years of guerrilla warfare in the African bush, while at least 350,000 African civilians died in the campaign's wake.

story.title: Egerton Railway Station Bus Boycott Massacre

subject: Egerton railway station bus boycott massacre
summary: On 4 August 1983, Ciskei police opened fire on unarmed commuters at Egerton railway station in Mdantsane, killing eleven people whose only act of defiance was trying to catch a train to work during a bus boycott over a five-cent fare increase.

subject: Eltham Well Hall rail crash
summary: On 11 June 1972 an excursion train carrying day-trippers from Margate hit a 20mph curve at 65mph. The driver was drunk. Six people died, including the driver himself.

subject: Emery Worldwide Airlines Flight 17
summary: A cargo plane's routine departure from Sacramento Mather Airport ended in catastrophe when a maintenance oversight turned a reliable DC-8 into an uncontrollable aircraft, killing all three crew members.

subject: Emsdetten school shooting
summary: On a Monday morning in November 2006, a former student walked into a Westphalian school with a rifle and smoke bombs. Eight people were wounded. He was the only one to die. The town has been carrying it ever since.

subject: Everett massacre
summary: On November 5, 1916, armed vigilantes opened fire on a steamship full of labor organizers arriving at the Everett dock, killing at least five workers in one of the bloodiest episodes of Pacific Northwest labor history.

subject: Execution Bridge, Ghent
summary: A medieval stone bridge where condemned men lost their heads, remembered for a legend of a son who could not kill his father.

story.title: The Execution of Charles I: The Day England Killed Its King

subject: Execution of Charles I
summary: On a freezing January afternoon in 1649, Charles I stepped onto a scaffold outside the Banqueting House on Whitehall and was beheaded with a single blow -- a moment that redefined the relationship between monarch and people in Britain forever.

subject: Expedition to Canton
summary: Over two days in April 1847 — midway between the two Opium Wars — a British force moved up the Pearl River from the Humen Strait to the walls of Canton, capturing every fort along the way in a show of coercive force that stopped short of the city itself.

subject: February 2007 Salvadoran congressmen killings
summary: Three Salvadoran congressmen and their driver were murdered near Guatemala City in February 2007 - then the four police suspects were killed inside a maximum-security prison, and the prosecutors investigating those killings were murdered in turn.

subject: Feyzin disaster
summary: A routine sampling operation at a French refinery in 1966 spiraled into Western Europe's worst petrochemical disaster, killing 18 people and transforming industrial safety standards across the continent.

subject: Fifteen Minutes at UC Merced
summary: On a quiet Wednesday morning in November 2015, a freshman's knife attack shattered the calm of California's newest university campus - and the bravery of a construction worker and campus police ended it in under fifteen minutes.

story.title: Fire Temple of Isfahan: Where Sacred Flames Once Watched Over Persia

subject: Fire Temple of Isfahan
summary: On a hill 210 meters above the Isfahan plain, Zoroastrian priests once tended sacred fires in chambers built with four arches open to the sky - a Sasanian-era complex now crumbling under neglect and treasure hunters' shovels.

subject: Fire Temple of Yazd
summary: Iran's only Atash Behram holds a sacred flame that has burned continuously since approximately 470 AD, tended by Zoroastrian priests for over fifteen centuries.

subject: First Battle of Fort Fisher
summary: A bold Union scheme to blow up a powder ship and storm the Confederacy's mightiest coastal fortress ended in embarrassing failure on the North Carolina coast in December 1864.

subject: First Battle of Fort Wagner
summary: On Morris Island in July 1863, Union troops stormed a sand-and-palmetto redoubt that stretched across the island's narrow neck - the first of two bloody assaults on Fort Wagner that would come to define the Charleston campaign.

subject: First Battle of Porto
summary: When Napoleon's Marshal Soult stormed Porto in 1809, thousands of civilians drowned as a pontoon bridge collapsed beneath the weight of people fleeing French cavalry.

subject: First Battle of Rappahannock Station
summary: A three-hour artillery duel on August 23, 1862, between 50 cannons that destroyed a railroad bridge and pinned an entire Confederate corps - while Stonewall Jackson slipped upriver to set up Second Manassas.

subject: First Battle of Torreón
summary: In late September 1913, Pancho Villa -- a guerrilla leader with no experience commanding large armies -- attacked a fortified city defended by federal artillery, and won in five days, seizing the weapons that would fuel his revolution.

subject: First Battle of the Stronghold
summary: A fog-shrouded lava fortress where 53 Modoc warriors defeated 400 US Army soldiers without suffering a single casualty.

subject: First Interstate Tower fire
summary: On May 4, 1988, a fire tore through sixteen floors of Los Angeles' tallest building while its sprinkler system sat ninety percent complete but inoperative, killing one man and rewriting fire codes nationwide.

subject: Flight 19
summary: Five TBM Avenger torpedo bombers vanished on a routine training flight from Fort Lauderdale on December 5, 1945 -- and the search plane sent to find them exploded in midair. Eighty years later, none of the 27 missing men or six aircraft have been found.

story.title: The FIU Bridge Collapse: When Innovation Became Catastrophe

subject: Florida International University pedestrian bridge collapse
summary: A pedestrian bridge meant to protect students from traffic collapsed onto those very cars it was designed to cross safely above, killing six people and exposing fatal flaws in an experimental concrete design that had never been tried before.

subject: Fonda Milagros Nightclub Fire
summary: A 2023 fire in a cluster of Murcia nightclubs killed thirteen people, most of them young migrants, in a building that had been ordered closed a year earlier.

subject: Fort Lee lane closure scandal
summary: The political scandal known as 'Bridgegate,' in which aides to New Jersey Governor Chris Christie weaponized traffic on the George Washington Bridge for political revenge.

story.title: Fort Mill Ridge Civil War Trenches

subject: Fort Mill Ridge Civil War Trenches
summary: A surviving network of Civil War earthworks dug by Confederate artillery, refurbished by Union infantry, and now an open-air museum on a West Virginia ridge.

subject: Fort Parker massacre
summary: An 1836 raid on a Texian frontier fort launched one of the most extraordinary captivity sagas in American history, producing a Comanche war chief whose surrender marked the end of the southern Plains wars.

subject: Fountain Valley massacre
summary: On September 6, 1972, a mass shooting at a St. Croix golf course killed eight people and shattered the island's tourism economy for decades -- an act of violence rooted in racial tension that left lasting scars on the U.S. Virgin Islands.

subject: Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse
summary: A loose wire in a terminal block plunged a 10,000-container ship into darkness, and thirty seconds later the third-longest continuous truss bridge in the world was gone.

subject: Franklin Dam Controversy
summary: A single photograph of mist on a wild river helped topple an Australian government and save the Franklin from a dam, in the campaign that gave the modern green movement its first great victory.

subject: Freckleton Air Disaster
summary: On 23 August 1944, a USAAF B-24 Liberator crashed into a Lancashire village during a sudden storm, striking a school and a cafe. Sixty-one people died, including 38 children.

subject: Freetown Fuel Tanker Explosion
summary: On the night of 5 November 2021, a fuel-tanker collision at a Freetown junction caused an explosion that killed 154 people — a memorial to the ordinary lives lost at Wellington's PMB intersection.

subject: Furiani disaster
summary: A hastily built stadium stand collapsed before a French Cup semifinal in Corsica, killing 18 and injuring over 2,300 in France's worst sporting disaster.

subject: Gasconade Bridge train disaster
summary: The first major deadly bridge collapse in American history killed over 30 people on November 1, 1855, when a 760-foot wooden trestle over Missouri's Gasconade River gave way beneath an inaugural excursion train -- derailing St. Louis's dream of becoming the starting point for the transcontinental railroad.

subject: Georgian Airways Flight 834
summary: A UN-chartered jet crashed at Kinshasa's N'Djili Airport during a thunderstorm in 2011, killing 32 of 33 aboard in the deadliest aviation disaster in United Nations history.

subject: Ghost Ship warehouse fire
summary: The 2016 warehouse fire that killed 36 people during an electronic music event in Oakland, exposing the Bay Area housing crisis and forever changing how cities view artist spaces.

subject: Gikondo massacre
summary: On April 9, 1994, Interahamwe militia entered a Polish Pallottine mission church in the Gikondo neighborhood of Kigali and murdered approximately 110 Tutsi men, women, and children who had sought sanctuary there.

subject: Gila River War Relocation Center
summary: An American concentration camp that became Arizona's fourth-largest city, where 13,000 Japanese Americans built a baseball diamond, a theater, and lives of dignity amid injustice.

subject: Glen Cinema disaster
summary: On Hogmanay 1929, up to 1,000 children packed into a Paisley cinema for a matinee. When smoke filled the auditorium and panic broke out, 71 of them never came home.

subject: Golden Dragon Massacre
summary: A 1977 gang shooting in a Chinatown restaurant that killed five innocent diners and missed every one of its intended targets.

subject: Goliad massacre
summary: On Palm Sunday 1836, between 425 and 445 Texian prisoners of war were marched from Fort Defiance and shot under Santa Anna's direct orders -- a betrayal that became the rallying cry of the Texas Revolution.

subject: Great Fire of Hamburg
summary: For three days in May 1842 a cigar-factory fire ate a third of Hamburg's old town — and the reckoning afterwards invented modern reinsurance.

subject: Great Siege of Scarborough Castle
summary: For five months in 1645, Parliament's largest cannon hammered the cliff-top keep of Scarborough Castle from inside a medieval church - and when the powder ran out and the well went dry, only twenty-five of the original five hundred defenders were still fit to fight.

subject: Greenwich Village townhouse explosion
summary: On March 6, 1970, a bomb factory in the basement of a Greenwich Village townhouse accidentally detonated, killing three members of the Weather Underground and exposing a plot to attack Fort Dix and Columbia University.

story.title: The Grenfell Tower Fire: 72 Lives, and a Reckoning That Has Not Ended

subject: Grenfell Tower fire
summary: In the early hours of 14 June 2017, a fire in a North Kensington tower block killed 72 people. Warnings had been ignored, flammable cladding had been installed, and a 'stay put' policy trapped residents in their homes. The community's fight for justice continues.

story.title: Gwen Araujo and the Law She Changed

subject: Gwen Araujo and the Law She Changed
summary: In 2002, a seventeen-year-old transgender girl was murdered at a house party in Newark, California. Her death exposed a legal loophole that allowed killers to blame their victims' identities -- and the fight to close it changed California law.

subject: Halifax V9977 Crash, Welsh Bicknor
summary: On 7 June 1942 a Halifax bomber testing the secret H2S radar went down above the Wye Valley, killing all eleven aboard, including the inventor of stereo sound.

subject: Harrow Court fire
summary: On a February night in 2005, a tealight candle melted through a television in a Stevenage tower block - and the fire that followed killed Natalie Close in her bed and two firefighters who came to save her, twelve years before Grenfell.

subject: Hattie Cotton Elementary School bombing
summary: Hours after a six-year-old Black girl attended her first day at a formerly all-white Nashville school in September 1957, segregationists dynamited the building -- an act of terror that galvanized the city's civil rights movement and was never solved.

subject: Hawks Nest Tunnel disaster
summary: In the early 1930s, hundreds of workers -- most of them Black migrants from the South -- died of silicosis while drilling a hydroelectric tunnel through Gauley Mountain in West Virginia, making it the deadliest industrial disaster in American history.

subject: Heysel Stadium disaster
summary: The 1985 tragedy at Brussels' Heysel Stadium where 39 fans died before the European Cup final, an event that UEFA later called 'the darkest hour in the history of its competitions.'

subject: Hillsborough disaster
summary: The 1989 crowd crush at Hillsborough Stadium that killed 97 Liverpool fans, and the families' thirty-year fight to overturn lies, blame, and institutional cover-up.

subject: Hindmarsh Island Bridge Controversy
summary: A low concrete bridge near Goolwa became the centre of a decade-long battle over Ngarrindjeri sacred knowledge, the limits of belief, and who gets to decide what is true.

subject: Hintze Ribeiro Bridge collapse
summary: On the evening of 4 March 2001, a 114-year-old bridge over Portugal's Douro River collapsed during heavy rains, sending a bus and three cars into the water and killing 59 people whose bodies the river carried thirty kilometers to the Atlantic.

subject: Honolulu Courthouse riot
summary: The 1874 Honolulu Courthouse riot erupted when Native Hawaiians stormed the legislature after American-allied lawmakers chose David Kalakaua over the popular Queen Emma, setting in motion the chain of events that would end the Hawaiian Kingdom.

subject: Hotel Caledonien fire
summary: A 1986 fire at a 12-story hotel in Kristiansand killed 14 people, all from smoke inhalation, after guests discovered their window handles had been removed and escape routes were impassable.

subject: Hotel Corona de Aragón fire
summary: A devastating 1979 hotel fire in Zaragoza that killed at least 80 people and spawned decades of conspiracy theories about Basque separatist involvement.

subject: Hotel Polen Fire
summary: On a Monday morning in 1977, a five-story wooden hotel on the Rokin filled with smoke before most of its guests had finished sleeping.

subject: Howard Street Tunnel fire
summary: A 60-car CSX freight train derailed beneath downtown Baltimore in July 2001, sparking a chemical fire that burned for days, ruptured a water main, severed internet cables, and paralyzed East Coast rail traffic for weeks.

subject: Humberto Vidal explosion
summary: A 1996 gas explosion in Rio Piedras killed 33 people in a commercial building, the result of a broken underground propane pipe that had been leaking for days while warnings went unheeded.

subject: Huntly rail bridge bombing
summary: A predawn gelignite blast on a Waikato railway bridge in 1951 turned a bitter waterfront dispute into a national crisis, yet the bridge refused to fall and the bombers were never found.

subject: Iglesia de la Compañía Fire
summary: On a December evening in 1863, a Santiago church filled with worshippers became the site of one of the deadliest building fires in history, a loss that reshaped how Chile protects its people.

story.title: Ikeda Elementary School: From Tragedy to Transformation

subject: Ikeda school massacre
summary: A 2001 stabbing attack at an elite Osaka elementary school killed eight children and reshaped how Japan thinks about school safety, turning a place of unimaginable grief into a national symbol of protection and remembrance.

subject: Inaugural games of the Colosseum
summary: In 80 AD, Emperor Titus opened the Flavian Amphitheatre with 100 consecutive days of spectacle -- gladiatorial combat, exotic animal hunts, and possibly naval battles inside the arena itself -- in one of the most extravagant public entertainments in human history.

subject: Inter-Korean Liaison Office bombing
summary: On June 16, 2020, North Korea detonated the Inter-Korean Liaison Office in Kaesong -- a building purpose-built for peace between the two Koreas, destroyed over leaflets floated across the border by defectors.

subject: Interstate 85 bridge collapse
summary: On the evening of March 30, 2017, a fire beneath an Atlanta overpass brought down a section of Interstate 85, shutting one of the South's most critical highways for 43 days and forcing a quarter-million daily commuters to find another way home.

subject: Iranian Embassy Siege
summary: Six days in April and May 1980 that ended on live television, when armed men seized 26 hostages at Princes Gate and the SAS came down the walls.

subject: Iroquois Theatre fire
summary: On December 30, 1903, a fire during a matinee at Chicago's "absolutely fireproof" Iroquois Theatre killed 602 people -- the deadliest single-building disaster in American history until September 11, 2001 -- and forever changed how buildings are designed for human escape.

subject: Islamabad Marriott Hotel bombing
summary: On the evening of September 20, 2008, a dump truck packed with explosives detonated at Islamabad's most prestigious hotel, killing at least 54 people in one of the worst terrorist attacks in Pakistan's history.

subject: Italian Hall disaster
summary: On Christmas Eve 1913, a false shout of 'fire' at a holiday party for striking copper miners in Calumet, Michigan triggered a stampede that killed 73 people - most of them children - in one of America's worst labor-era tragedies.

subject: Izhevsk school shooting
summary: On September 26, 2022, a gunman killed eighteen people at School No. 88 in Izhevsk, Russia, including eleven children, in one of the deadliest school attacks in the country's history.

story.title: Thirty Seconds on Lynch Street: The Jackson State Killings

subject: Jackson State killings
summary: Eleven days after Kent State dominated the headlines, Mississippi police opened fire on a women's dormitory at Jackson State College, killing two students and injuring twelve in a tragedy the nation largely overlooked.

subject: Jakarta Stock Exchange Bombing
summary: On September 13, 2000, a car bomb detonated in the basement parking garage of the Jakarta Stock Exchange, killing fifteen people -- most of them drivers waiting beside their employers' vehicles, caught in a place they had no reason to fear.

subject: Jakarta school bombing
summary: A November 2025 bombing at a Jakarta high school injured 96 people and exposed an alarming network of neo-Nazi radicalization among Indonesian teenagers.

story.title: Japan Air Lines Flight 350: The Struggle at 164 Feet

subject: Japan Air Lines Flight 350
summary: On February 9, 1982, the captain of a Japan Air Lines DC-8 deliberately pushed his controls forward on approach to Tokyo's Haneda Airport, and only the desperate intervention of his first officer and flight engineer prevented an even greater catastrophe in Tokyo Bay.

subject: Joelma Building fire
summary: On February 1, 1974, a short-circuiting air conditioner turned a 25-story São Paulo office tower into a furnace in twenty minutes, killing 179 people in a catastrophe that reshaped fire safety codes worldwide.

subject: Kabul Expedition (1842)
summary: After the annihilation of a 16,500-person column retreating from Kabul in January 1842, Britain sent two armies back through the Khyber Pass to rescue hostages, raze the city's bazaar, and call it a victory.

subject: Kanawha County Textbook War
summary: In 1974, a dispute over multicultural schoolbooks in West Virginia escalated into a months-long boycott, school bombings, and the opening salvo of America's modern culture wars.

subject: Kaohsiung Prison Riot
summary: In February 2015, six inmates at Kaohsiung Prison seized weapons and took the warden hostage in a 14-hour standoff that exposed deep fractures in Taiwan's justice system.

subject: Karlslust Dance Hall Fire
summary: Around eighty Berliners died at the city's first postwar fancy-dress ball when the roof of the Karlslust came down in the coldest winter anyone could remember.

subject: Katekavia Flight 9357
summary: A regional flight's fatal attempt to land in fog at Igarka Airport in 2010 exposed systemic failures in Russian regional aviation that safety investigators had warned about years earlier.

subject: Kauhajoki school shooting
summary: On September 23, 2008, a gunman killed ten people at a vocational college in this small Finnish town -- the second school shooting in Finland in less than a year, and a tragedy that exposed painful gaps in the country's threat assessment systems.

subject: Kett's Rebellion
summary: In the summer of 1549, 16,000 Norfolk commoners camped above Norwich and asked the king to limit the power of the gentry. By December, their leader hung in chains from Norwich Castle.

subject: King's Cross fire
summary: On the evening of 18 November 1987, a wooden escalator at King's Cross St Pancras tube station caught fire, then erupted in a way no one had ever predicted - killing 31 people and ending a century of complacency in how London ran its Underground.

subject: Kingsland explosion
summary: On January 11, 1917, a munitions factory in Lyndhurst, New Jersey, exploded in what was likely an act of German sabotage -- and the doctors at a nearby asylum calmed panicked residents by telling them the war had ended and the blasts were celebratory gunfire.

subject: Kiss Nightclub Fire
summary: On a January night in 2013, a fire in a Santa Maria nightclub took the lives of 242 young people, most of them university students, in one of the deadliest such disasters in history.

subject: Kolavia Flight 348
summary: On New Year's Day 2011, a Tupolev Tu-154 caught fire during engine start at Surgut Airport when worn-out electrical contactors that had never been inspected produced an arc carrying twenty times the normal current, killing three and injuring forty-three.

subject: Komanda massacre
summary: On the night of July 26-27, 2025, Islamic State-affiliated ADF rebels attacked a church vigil in Komanda, Ituri Province, killing at least 43 Congolese civilians including women and children during what should have been a night of prayer.

subject: Kostroma café fire
summary: A flare gun discharged inside a crowded Kostroma nightclub in November 2022 killed 15 people and exposed systemic failures in fire safety, building codes, and emergency response across Russia's entertainment venues.

subject: Kungälv school shooting
summary: Sweden's first school shooting, a 1961 tragedy that sparked the nation's earliest debate about media violence and left a legacy of forgiveness.

story.title: The Koriyama Explosion: A Morning That Shattered Sakura-dori

subject: Kōriyama explosion
summary: A gas explosion leveled a shabu-shabu restaurant on one of Koriyama's busiest streets in July 2020, killing one worker and injuring nineteen others -- the result of corroded gas pipes that went unrepaired despite warnings weeks earlier.

subject: LADE Flight 072
summary: A 1995 charter carrying military families to a graduation never reached Córdoba; a cross on a Sierras peak marks where 53 lives ended.

subject: LAN Chile Flight 1069
summary: In February 1991, a regional jet overran the short runway at the southernmost airport in the world and slid into the Beagle Channel, killing twenty of the seventy-two people aboard.

subject: La Cantuta massacre
summary: At a Lima university campus in July 1992, a military death squad abducted and killed a professor and nine students, igniting a decades-long struggle for justice that would eventually topple a president.

subject: Lahore church bombings
summary: On a Sunday morning in March 2015, two suicide bombers attacked Christian worshippers in Lahore's Youhanabad neighbourhood, killing at least 15 people and igniting days of grief and fury across Pakistan.

subject: Lakanal House fire
summary: Six people died in a 2009 tower-block fire in Camberwell whose warnings, ignored by those who could have heeded them, became the unread preface to Grenfell.

subject: Land's End Disaster
summary: On a 1985 school trip to Land's End, four children were swept off the rocks; the case changed how British schools take pupils outdoors.

subject: Lanjisu internet cafe fire
summary: A 2002 arson at an unlicensed Beijing internet cafe killed 25 people, most of them university students, and triggered a nationwide crackdown that reshaped China's internet regulation.

subject: Last Call on K Street
summary: A gang rivalry erupted into gunfire on Sacramento's K Street at 2 a.m. as bars closed on April 3, 2022, killing six people blocks from the California State Capitol and exposing the city's long-simmering crisis with gun violence.

subject: Laurier Palace Theatre fire
summary: On a Sunday afternoon in January 1927, a fire broke out in a packed Montreal movie theatre where 250 children sat watching a comedy -- and exit doors that opened inward sealed their fate, killing 78.

subject: Lewisham rail crash
summary: On a foggy December evening in 1957, a steam train at thirty miles an hour ran into a stopped commuter service and pulled a railway bridge down on top of it. Ninety people died.

subject: Lexington Avenue explosion
summary: On July 4, 1914, anarchists building a bomb to target John D. Rockefeller's estate accidentally detonated their dynamite supply in a Harlem tenement, killing four people and tearing apart a seven-story building.

subject: Liceu bombing
summary: On opening night 1893, an anarchist threw two bombs into the stalls of Barcelona's opera house, killing up to thirty people and triggering a repression that consumed far more lives than the attack itself.

subject: Llandow air disaster
summary: On 12 March 1950, an overloaded Avro Tudor carrying Welsh rugby fans home from Dublin stalled on approach to Llandow aerodrome, killing 80 people in what was then the world's worst air disaster.

subject: Locked Doors at 1:45 AM
summary: On 8 September 2021, a short circuit in a Tangerang prison block holding 122 inmates in a space built for 38 started a fire that killed 49 people trapped behind locked cell doors.

subject: Lod Airport massacre
summary: In 1972, three Japanese Red Army members recruited by Palestinian militants opened fire inside Israel's main airport, killing 26 people -- most of them Christian pilgrims from Puerto Rico.

subject: Los Angeles Times Bombing
summary: At 1 a.m. on October 1, 1910, sixteen sticks of dynamite exploded in the Los Angeles Times building, killing 21 people and injuring 100 more. The bombing became the center of one of the most consequential trials in American labor history, defended by Clarence Darrow and argued before the entire nation.

subject: Louis Blériot
summary: He made his fortune building car headlamps, crashed half a dozen aircraft, and on the morning of 25 July 1909, flew an underpowered monoplane across the English Channel in thirty-six minutes - and Britain stopped being an island.

subject: Lynching of Ed Johnson
summary: On a March evening in 1906, a mob dragged Ed Johnson from a Chattanooga jail and lynched him from the Walnut Street Bridge -- defying a stay of execution from the U.S. Supreme Court and triggering the only criminal trial the court has ever conducted.

subject: M40 Minibus Crash
summary: Twelve schoolchildren and their teacher died just after midnight on 18 November 1993 when their minibus, returning from a Royal Albert Hall concert, struck a maintenance lorry on the M40 hard shoulder. The disaster reshaped UK law on seat belts in minibuses and coaches.

subject: MGM Grand fire
summary: A faulty pastry case ignited a fireball that killed 85 people at the MGM Grand Hotel in 1980, transforming fire safety codes across Nevada and spawning the largest helicopter rescue in American history.

subject: MacDonald House bombing
summary: A 1965 bombing on Singapore's Orchard Road killed three people and left scars on Indonesia-Singapore relations that took decades to heal.

subject: Man-O-War Cay
summary: A tiny Bahamian island where one family's boat-building legacy has shaped everything for over two centuries, from the town's precise grid to homes built like ships, only to face the strongest Atlantic hurricane on record.

subject: Manchester Arena bombing
summary: On 22 May 2017, twenty-two people, many of them children and young women, were killed in the City Room of Manchester Arena as families waited to take their daughters home from an Ariana Grande concert.

subject: Manx2 Flight 7100
summary: On a foggy February morning in 2011, a small commuter aircraft from Belfast crashed on its third attempt to land at Cork Airport, killing both pilots and four passengers.

subject: Marcopper mining disaster
summary: On the Philippine island of Marinduque, sixteen years of toxic mine tailings dumped into a shallow bay poisoned children and destroyed livelihoods before a catastrophic tunnel collapse in 1996 sent 1.6 million cubic meters of waste flooding down the Boac river system.

story.title: Massacre at the Russian Embassy in Tehran

subject: Massacre at the Russian Embassy in Tehran
summary: In January 1829, an angry mob stormed the Russian Embassy in Tehran and killed nearly everyone inside, including the celebrated playwright Alexander Griboyedov, in a violent collision of diplomacy, imperial humiliation, and religious fury.

story.title: Massacre in the Great Temple of Tenochtitlan

subject: Massacre in the Great Temple of Tenochtitlan
summary: On May 22, 1520, Spanish soldiers sealed the exits of a temple courtyard in Tenochtitlan and slaughtered hundreds of unarmed Mexica nobles and warriors during a religious festival they had been granted permission to hold.

subject: Massacre of Monzievaird
summary: On 21 October 1490, about twenty Murrays sheltering in a thatched church near Hosh were burned alive by their Drummond kinsmen, ending a Highland blood feud and forcing King James IV to make examples by the gallows at Stirling.

subject: Massacre of Naarden
summary: On a cold December day in 1572, a Spanish army accepted Naarden's surrender, herded the men of the town into the church, and burned it down around them.

subject: Massacre of Samothrace (1821)
summary: On a small Aegean island in September 1821, an Ottoman expedition killed roughly 700 men beneath a Byzantine fortress and enslaved at least as many women and children.

subject: Massacre of Thessalonica
summary: Around 390 CE, Roman troops loosed on a crowd of spectators in the hippodrome of Thessalonica killed thousands of citizens; Bishop Ambrose of Milan denied the emperor communion until he repented.

story.title: Massacre of the First Sapper Battalion

subject: Massacre of the First Sapper Battalion
summary: On the morning of 29 February 1948, guards at the Makronisos military prison opened fire on Greek soldiers imprisoned for their political beliefs — men designated 'unreliable' by their own army during the Greek Civil War. The killings that followed on 29 February and 1 March are remembered as the massacre of the First Sapper Battalion.

subject: Monrovia Church massacre
summary: On July 29, 1990, approximately 600 men, women, and children sheltering in St. Peter's Lutheran Church in Monrovia were killed by government soldiers, making it the deadliest single atrocity of the First Liberian Civil War.

subject: Moorgate tube crash
summary: In 1975, a London Underground train drove into a dead-end tunnel wall at speed, killing 43 people in a disaster whose cause has never been explained.

subject: Morant Bay rebellion
summary: In October 1865, a Baptist deacon named Paul Bogle led hundreds of Jamaican peasants to the Morant Bay courthouse to protest injustice -- and the colonial government's brutal response changed Jamaica's constitution forever.

subject: Morrisite War
summary: A forgotten religious conflict in 1862 Utah where a self-proclaimed prophet's apocalyptic commune met a violent end at Kington Fort.

subject: Mud March (American Civil War)
summary: In January 1863, the Union Army of the Potomac tried to cross the Rappahannock River, outflank Robert E. Lee, and salvage a disastrous winter -- but betrayal from within and relentless rain turned the campaign into a quagmire that ended a general's career.

subject: Murder Bay
summary: A notorious slum just blocks from the White House, Murder Bay was Washington D.C.'s center of crime and vice until the federal government bulldozed it to build the Federal Triangle.

story.title: The Murder of Adam Walsh: How One Tragedy Reshaped a Nation

subject: Murder of Adam Walsh
summary: The 1981 abduction and murder of six-year-old Adam Walsh from a Hollywood, Florida, department store launched the missing children's movement, transformed his father into America's most recognized crime victim advocate, and changed the way a country watches over its children.

subject: Murder of Ann Maguire
summary: Ann Maguire taught Spanish at Corpus Christi Catholic College in Leeds for forty years. On 28 April 2014 she was killed in her own classroom by one of her pupils.

story.title: The Brooke Hart Kidnapping and San Jose Lynching

subject: Murder of Brooke Hart and the lynching of Thomas Harold Thurmond and John M. Holmes
summary: The 1933 kidnapping and murder of a department store heir sparked one of California's last lynchings, broadcast live on radio and endorsed by the governor.

subject: Murder of David Amess
summary: On a Friday in October 2021, a sitting Member of Parliament was murdered at his constituency surgery in a Leigh-on-Sea church hall - the second British MP killed in five years.

subject: Murder of Fernando Báez Sosa
summary: An 18-year-old law student, the only son of Paraguayan immigrants, was beaten to death outside a Villa Gesell nightclub in January 2020. His parents turned their grief into a demand for justice that an entire country answered.

subject: Murder of Hannah Graham
summary: An 18-year-old University of Virginia student vanished from Charlottesville's Downtown Mall in 2014, igniting a massive search that uncovered a serial predator and shook a college town's sense of safety.

subject: Murder of Hauwa Liman
summary: Hauwa Mohammed Liman was a 24-year-old nurse, midwife, and university student who was delivering medical care to displaced families in northeastern Nigeria when she was abducted and executed by militants -- her death a war crime that drew worldwide condemnation and a Florence Nightingale Medal.

subject: Murder of June Anne Devaney
summary: On 15 May 1948 a three-year-old girl was abducted from her hospital cot in Blackburn and murdered; finding her killer required fingerprinting more than 46,000 men, the first mass-fingerprinting operation in British history.

subject: Murder of Karen Buckley
summary: Karen Buckley was a 24-year-old Irish nurse and occupational therapy student murdered in Glasgow in April 2015. Her family, her university, and the city held her memory close.

subject: Murder of Lana Clarkson
summary: On February 3, 2003, actress Lana Clarkson was shot and killed inside the Pyrenees Castle mansion in Alhambra, California. The man whose home it was — music producer Phil Spector — was convicted of second-degree murder six years later, after one of the longest trials in Los Angeles history.

subject: Murder of Larry King
summary: The 2008 shooting of 15-year-old Lawrence King at a junior high school in Oxnard sparked a national reckoning on anti-LGBTQ violence, bullying, and the rights of gender-nonconforming youth.

subject: Murder of Lee Rigby
summary: On a bright Wednesday afternoon in Woolwich in 2013, a young father and soldier was killed in the street. The memorial in St George's Garrison Church now carries his name alongside ten others who served and died from this neighbourhood.

subject: Murder of Lindsay Rimer
summary: Lindsay Rimer was a 13-year-old Hebden Bridge schoolgirl who disappeared on a November evening in 1994 and was found murdered five months later, in a case her family has spent more than thirty years asking the public to help solve.

subject: Murder of Lord Darnley
summary: On 10 February 1567 a house in Edinburgh was blown apart with gunpowder, but the body of Mary Queen of Scots's husband was found unmarked in a nearby orchard, apparently strangled.

subject: Murder of Marion Parker
summary: In December 1927, a 12-year-old girl was taken from her Los Angeles school by a man claiming her father had been in an accident, setting off the crime the LA Times called 'the most horrible of the 1920s.'

subject: Murder of Mona Tinsley
summary: A ten-year-old girl who never came home from school in Newark in January 1937, and the long winter and spring her family spent waiting.

subject: Murder of Pamela Werner
summary: The unsolved 1937 murder of a young British woman near Beijing's Fox Tower, a case tangled in colonial rivalries, wartime chaos, and competing theories that still generate debate.

story.title: Murder of Sophie Toscan du Plantier

subject: Murder of Sophie Toscan du Plantier
summary: The 1996 murder of a French television producer at her West Cork holiday cottage became Ireland's most infamous cold case, entangling two countries' legal systems and spawning a global true-crime phenomenon.

subject: Murder of Tessa Majors
summary: The 2019 stabbing of a Barnard College freshman in Morningside Park forced New York to confront the tensions between campus life and the neighborhoods surrounding it.

subject: Murder of Yvonne Fletcher
summary: The 25-year-old police constable shot dead from inside the Libyan embassy on St James's Square in 1984.

subject: Murder of the Notorious B.I.G.
summary: The unsolved 1997 drive-by shooting of Christopher Wallace outside the Petersen Automotive Museum became one of hip-hop's most enduring mysteries.

subject: Musab bin Umair mosque massacre
summary: On a Friday afternoon in August 2014, seventy-three worshippers from the Bani Wais tribe were killed during prayers at a Sunni mosque in Diyala Province, a sectarian atrocity that shook Iraq's fragile political process.

subject: Myojo 56 building fire
summary: A deadly 2001 blaze in a narrow Kabukicho entertainment building killed 44 people trapped behind blocked exits and sealed windows -- the fifth-deadliest fire in postwar Japan, suspected arson that was never solved.

subject: NORTHAG War Headquarters Cannerberg
summary: Fifty metres below a Limburg hillside, NATO ran a secret underground city — eight kilometres of corridors, a hair salon and a three-hole golf course — to fight a war that never came.

subject: Nankana massacre
summary: A predawn march to reclaim a Sikh birthplace gurdwara ended in the slaughter of unarmed worshippers, igniting the reform movement that reshaped Sikh governance.

subject: National Airlines Flight 101
summary: In the winter of 1952, three planes fell from the sky over Elizabeth, New Jersey in less than two months — a sequence of disasters that shut down Newark Airport for nine months and haunted a generation of local residents, including a young Judy Blume.

subject: Naval battle off Tatamagouche
