summary: A cunning deception by a lone New England sloop turned the tide of King George's War, denying French reinforcements and sealing the fate of Fortress Louisbourg in 1745.

subject: Navaly church bombing
summary: On July 9, 1995, hundreds of Tamil civilians sheltering in the Church of St. Peter and Paul in Navaly were bombed during Sri Lanka's civil war. At least 147 people died - families who had been told that churches were safe.

subject: Navarino Massacre
summary: On 19 August 1821, after the Greek capture of Neokastro fortress at Navarino (Pylos), approximately 3,000 Muslim residents who had surrendered under a negotiated agreement were killed — one of the most brutal episodes of the Greek War of Independence.

subject: Neve Shalom Synagogue Massacre
summary: On 6 September 1986, gunmen attacked worshippers during Shabbat services at Istanbul's Neve Shalom Synagogue, killing 22 members of the city's Jewish community in one of the deadliest antisemitic attacks of the 20th century.

subject: New Cross House Fire
summary: In the early hours of 18 January 1981, thirteen young Black Britons died at a teenage birthday party in south London - a fire that set off a movement.

subject: New London School explosion
summary: A 1937 natural gas explosion killed 295 students and teachers at a wealthy East Texas school, prompting the law that gives natural gas its distinctive warning smell.

story.title: New Madrid: America's Sleeping Earthquake Monster

subject: New Madrid
summary: The Missouri fault that produced the largest earthquakes in recorded American history - three in 1811-12 that rang church bells in Boston, made the Mississippi run backward, and created Reelfoot Lake, all in a region that's forgotten it's dangerous.

subject: Northeast Airlines Flight 823
summary: A 1957 crash near Rikers Island that lasted only sixty seconds from takeoff to impact -- and prompted an extraordinary rescue by prison inmates who earned their freedom.

subject: Obafemi Awolowo University massacre
summary: In the predawn hours of July 10, 1999, members of the Black Axe Confraternity attacked a student gathering at Obafemi Awolowo University in Ile-Ife, killing five and wounding eleven in an act of targeted retribution.

subject: Ocean Isle Beach house fire
summary: On October 28, 2007, a three-story beach house on the Brunswick County coast caught fire before dawn. Thirteen college students were inside. Seven of them did not get out.

subject: Oireachtas Golf Society scandal
summary: On 19 August 2020, 81 people sat down to dinner at the Station House Hotel in Clifden the day after the Irish government tightened COVID restrictions to six people per gathering - and within a week the affair had cost Ireland a cabinet minister, an EU Commissioner, and a great deal of public trust.

subject: Oklahoma City bombing
summary: On April 19, 1995, a truck bomb destroyed the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City, killing 168 people in what remains the deadliest act of domestic terrorism in American history.

subject: Old Kowloon Fire Station
summary: Built near the southern terminus of the Kowloon–Canton Railway, this early twentieth-century fire station in Tsim Sha Tsui now anchors the 1881 Heritage luxury complex beside the old Marine Police Headquarters.

subject: One-Two-Go Airlines Flight 269
summary: On a rain-lashed afternoon in September 2007, a budget airline's MD-82 crashed beside the runway at Phuket International Airport, killing 90 people in a disaster investigators would call entirely preventable.

subject: Oradour-sur-Glane massacre
summary: On 10 June 1944, four days after D-Day, soldiers of the 2nd SS Panzer Division Das Reich murdered 642 civilians in the village of Oradour-sur-Glane. The ruins were never rebuilt, preserved by order of Charles de Gaulle as a permanent memorial.

story.title: The Osaka Video Arcade Fire: A Night in Namba That Changed Japan's Safety Laws

subject: Osaka movie theatre fire
summary: In October 2008, an arson attack at a small video arcade called Cats in Osaka's Namba district killed sixteen people trapped in windowless rooms with no sprinklers, no smoke ventilation, and a fire alarm that had been switched off.

story.title: Our Lady of the Angels School Fire

subject: Our Lady of the Angels School fire
summary: On December 1, 1958, a fire at Our Lady of the Angels School on Chicago's West Side killed 92 children and three nuns, exposing fatal gaps in school fire safety codes and triggering nationwide reforms that brought 16,500 older school buildings up to code within a single year.

subject: Owo church attack
summary: On Pentecost Sunday 2022, gunmen stormed St. Francis Xavier Catholic Church in the ancient Yoruba city of Owo, killing at least 40 worshippers and wounding dozens more in one of the deadliest attacks on a place of worship in Nigerian history.

subject: Paisley Canal Disaster
summary: On a sunny Saturday in 1810, a family pleasure boat capsized at a Paisley dock and 84 people drowned - most of them children - in what became the worst disaster of the British Canal Age.

subject: Palm Sunday at the Gate
summary: On Palm Sunday 2021, two suicide bombers on a motorcycle attacked the oldest church in Makassar, Indonesia -- and were stopped at the gate by a security guard whose vigilance prevented a far greater tragedy.

subject: Pan Am Flight 845
summary: A 1971 Boeing 747 takeoff accident at San Francisco International Airport caused by a cascade of miscommunications, wrong runway assignments, and uncorrected speed calculations that sent the aircraft plowing through approach lights at the end of the runway.

story.title: Pension de Vogel homeless hostel fire

subject: Pension de Vogel homeless hostel fire
summary: On 16 September 1992, an arson fire at a Hague hostel for homeless people killed eleven residents whose only home was the building that burned down around them.

subject: Perm State University shooting
summary: On September 20, 2021, an 18-year-old gunman opened fire at Perm State University, killing six people and injuring 47 in one of Russia's deadliest mass shootings at an educational institution.

subject: Pinlaung massacre
summary: In March 2023, Myanmar Army troops killed at least 30 civilians, including three Buddhist monks, sheltering in a monastery in the village of Namneng -- one of the post-coup civil war's most devastating atrocities.

story.title: Tree of Life: Squirrel Hill's Darkest Morning

subject: Pittsburgh synagogue shooting
summary: The deadliest attack on a Jewish community in American history took place during Shabbat morning services in Pittsburgh's Squirrel Hill neighborhood on October 27, 2018, killing eleven worshippers and transforming Jewish security across the nation.

subject: Point Ellice Bridge disaster
summary: On a holiday afternoon in 1896, an overloaded streetcar took the Point Ellice Bridge into Victoria's Upper Harbour, killing 55 people — the worst transit disaster in British Columbia's history.

subject: Porto Boat Bridge disaster
summary: On a March morning in 1809, thousands of Porto's civilians fled French troops across a pontoon bridge over the Douro. The bridge collapsed. An estimated 4,000 people died.

story.title: Postlegate: The Scandal That Shook Poker's Trust

subject: Postlegate
summary: A suburban Sacramento card room became ground zero for poker's biggest cheating scandal when one player's impossibly perfect decisions, a commentator's courage, and RFID technology collided on a livestream.

subject: Poway synagogue shooting
summary: On the last day of Passover 2019, a gunman entered Chabad of Poway during Shabbat services and killed Lori Gilbert-Kaye, who died shielding her rabbi. The congregation she protected continued to gather.

subject: Prestonsburg, Kentucky bus crash
summary: On a cold February morning in 1958, a school bus on U.S. 23 went into the flooded Levisa Fork. Twenty-six children and their driver did not come home.

subject: Pyle's Massacre
summary: A Revolutionary War engagement where mistaken identity turned a handshake into a bloodbath, ending Loyalist recruitment in North Carolina weeks before Guilford Courthouse.

subject: Radisson Blu Bamako Attack
summary: On 20 November 2015, two gunmen seized roughly 170 people at a Bamako hotel and killed twenty of them, a morning of terror remembered for its victims and for the rescuers who walked into the gunfire.

subject: Ramses Station rail disaster
summary: A runaway locomotive slammed into the buffers at Cairo's main railway station in 2019, triggering an explosion and fireball that killed 25 people and exposed decades of neglect in Egypt's rail system.

subject: Rangoon bombing
summary: In October 1983, North Korean agents detonated a bomb at Yangon's Martyrs' Mausoleum in an attempt to assassinate South Korean President Chun Doo-hwan, killing 21 people and reshaping Cold War alliances across Asia.

subject: Reichstag fire
summary: On February 27, 1933, the German parliament burned. Within twenty-four hours, the Nazis had used the fire to destroy what remained of German democracy.

subject: Remembrance Day bombing
summary: On a cold November morning in 1987, eleven civilians died beside a small-town cenotaph in Enniskillen, and one father's words from his hospital bed that evening changed the moral arithmetic of the Troubles.

subject: Richmond Theatre fire
summary: On the day after Christmas in 1811, a chandelier flame touched a stage curtain and killed 72 people in minutes -- the worst urban disaster in American history at the time.

subject: River Dee ferryboat disaster
summary: Thirty-two people drowned when an overcrowded wire ferry capsized at the mouth of the River Dee in 1876 -- a tragedy that finally gave Aberdeen the bridge it had needed for years.

story.title: Rocky Creek World War Two Hospital Complex

subject: Rocky Creek World War Two Hospital Complex
summary: On the cool Atherton Tableland, the largest military hospital in wartime North Queensland treated 30,000 soldiers back from New Guinea; today little remains but concrete slabs in the cane and a curved tin theatre called the Igloo.

subject: Russo-Turkish War of 1672-1681
summary: Two empires spent years and tens of thousands of lives fighting over a single Cossack fortress on the Tiasmyn - the town of Chyhyryn, gateway to Right-bank Ukraine.

subject: Río Piedras massacre
summary: On October 24, 1935, Puerto Rico Police officers opened fire on unarmed Nationalist Party supporters at the University of Puerto Rico, killing four people in a shooting that inflamed the independence movement and triggered a chain of political violence.

subject: Saint John City Hall fire
summary: A 1977 fire in the lockup beneath Saint John City Hall killed 21 men, most jailed for minor offences, sparking outrage over conditions in Canadian holding cells.

subject: Sampoong Department Store collapse
summary: On June 29, 1995, the Sampoong Department Store in Seoul collapsed in twenty seconds, killing 502 people in the deadliest peacetime disaster in South Korean history, a catastrophe investigators traced to greed, corruption, and willful negligence.

subject: San Jose Central Fire Station
summary: Built in 1951 as the nerve center of San Jose's postwar fire protection system, the International Style firehouse on Market Street is now a museum preserving firefighting history dating back to 1810.

subject: San Patricio Church Massacre
summary: On a winter Sunday in 1976, five members of an Irish-founded religious order were murdered in their own parish in Belgrano; decades later, an Argentine pope began the case for their sainthood.

subject: San Ysidro McDonald's massacre
summary: On July 18, 1984, James Oliver Huberty walked into a McDonald's restaurant in San Ysidro and opened fire, killing 22 people and wounding 19 others in a 77-minute rampage that shocked the nation.

subject: Santa María School massacre
summary: On December 21, 1907, the Chilean Army opened fire on thousands of striking nitrate miners and their families gathered at a school in Iquique, killing an estimated 2,000 people in a massacre the government suppressed for decades.

subject: Sanxia Car Attack
summary: On a Monday afternoon in May 2025, a 78-year-old driver accelerated to over 100 km/h through a school zone in Sanxia District, killing three people and injuring eleven others -- an act prosecutors later classified as showing 'oblique intent to kill.'

subject: Sarposa prison attack of 2008
summary: A meticulously planned Taliban raid on Kandahar's main prison freed up to 1,000 inmates in thirty minutes, exposing the fragility of Afghan government control and triggering a political crisis that reshuffled the province's leadership.

subject: Saugus High School Shooting
summary: On his 16th birthday, a student opened fire in a Santa Clarita high school courtyard for sixteen seconds, killing two classmates and wounding three others before turning the gun on himself.

subject: Schio massacre
summary: A postwar revenge killing in a Veneto jail reveals how Italy's liberation from fascism unleashed its own cycle of violence, political denial, and decades of contested memory.

subject: Seattle Jewish Federation shooting
summary: On July 28, 2006, a lone gunman forced his way into the Jewish Federation of Greater Seattle building in Belltown and shot six women, killing one, in what prosecutors called 'one of the most serious crimes that has ever occurred in this city.'

subject: Second Battle of Bull Run
summary: Thirteen months after the first battle on these same fields, Robert E. Lee's audacious flanking strategy and Longstreet's devastating counterattack produced the Confederacy's greatest tactical victory in the Eastern Theater.

subject: Second Battle of Charleston Harbor
summary: For sixty days in the summer of 1863, Union forces besieged Fort Wagner on Morris Island with calcium floodlights, multi-barrel Requa guns, and a massive cannon called the Swamp Angel - weapons that previewed the industrial warfare of the next century.

subject: Second Battle of Porto
summary: A barber, a hidden skiff, and four unguarded wine barges gave Arthur Wellesley everything he needed to cross the Douro and drive the French from Porto in May 1809.

subject: Second Battle of Springfield
summary: One of the Civil War's rare urban battles unfolded in Springfield, Missouri on January 8, 1863, when Confederate cavalry attacked the Union's major supply depot and fought house-to-house through the streets -- only to be repelled by a scratch garrison defending a ring of earthen forts.

subject: Second Battle of Torreón
summary: Six months after losing Torreon, Villa returned with 8,000 men, hospital trains, 29 cannons, and a two-seat airplane to fight a brutal twelve-day battle that broke the federal army in northern Mexico.

subject: Second Battle of the Stronghold
summary: Four days after assassinating a U.S. general during peace talks, the Modoc faced 400 soldiers converging on their lava fortress, only to vanish through an unguarded crack in the rock.

subject: Sennichi Department Store Building fire
summary: A catastrophic 1972 fire in an Osaka department store building killed 118 people, most of them patrons of a seventh-floor cabaret, and rewrote Japan's fire safety codes forever.

subject: Seongsu Bridge disaster
summary: On October 21, 1994, a 48-meter section of Seoul's Seongsu Bridge collapsed into the Han River during morning rush hour, killing 32 people and exposing the dangerous shortcuts hidden beneath South Korea's economic miracle.

subject: Sepahan Airlines Flight 5915
summary: An overloaded turboprop with a known engine problem lost power on takeoff from Tehran's Mehrabad Airport on August 10, 2014, reaching only 40 meters before stalling onto a boulevard near Azadi Stadium, killing 40 of the 48 people aboard.

subject: Shek Kip Mei Fire
summary: On Christmas night 1953, a fire tore through the Shek Kip Mei squatter settlement, leaving over 53,000 people without shelter and forcing the Hong Kong colonial government to confront, for the first time, its responsibility to house its most vulnerable residents.

story.title: Siege of Akasaka: The Emperor's Impossible Gamble

subject: Siege of Akasaka
summary: A 14th-century mountain fortress where 500 samurai loyal to a rebellious emperor held off a quarter-million shogunate troops through sheer ingenuity -- losing the castle twice, escaping both times, and ultimately helping topple the Kamakura shogunate.

subject: Siege of Alicante
summary: During the War of the Spanish Succession, an Allied garrison held Alicante's castle until besiegers tunnelled a giant mine into the mountain beneath them and blew it open, killing their commander.

subject: Siege of Athens (287 BC)
summary: In 287 BC Athens rose against its Macedonian overlord, and old men and boys stormed a hilltop fort - then a king arrived from Epirus to seal the city's freedom.

story.title: Siege of Athens and Piraeus (87–86 BC)

subject: Siege of Athens and Piraeus (87–86 BC)
summary: Through a starving winter and a midnight assault, the Roman general Sulla broke Athens - and according to Plutarch, the blood of its people ran out through the city gate.

subject: Siege of Augusta
summary: A wooden tower, a fake deserter, and a house rigged to explode -- the 1781 siege of Augusta reads like a thriller, pitting Patriot ingenuity against a Loyalist commander who refused to go quietly.

subject: Siege of Bangkok
summary: In 1688, forty thousand Siamese soldiers besieged two hundred entrenched French troops at a riverside fortress in Bangkok -- and four months later, let them leave.

subject: Siege of Basing House
summary: The two-year ordeal of England's largest private house, defended by a Catholic marquess until Cromwell brought heavy guns and burned Loyalty House to the ground.

subject: Siege of Bergen op Zoom (1747)
summary: The fortress that Menno van Coehoorn designed was thought impregnable. In 1747 a French marshal proved otherwise, in the longest and bloodiest siege of the War of the Austrian Succession.

subject: Siege of Blair Castle
summary: The 1746 siege where a Jacobite lord besieged his own brother's castle, government troops nearly starved, and a messenger's fallen horse almost cost them relief -- the last castle siege in Britain.

subject: Siege of Bohus Fortress (1678)
summary: A Swedish garrison of 400 men held off 15,000 Dano-Norwegian troops for weeks in one of Scandinavia's most dramatic siege defenses.

subject: Siege of Brahan
summary: When the 1715 Jacobite rising collapsed at Sheriffmuir, government forces marched on Brahan Castle and put a long widow under siege - not to take the building, but to humiliate the house that had defeated them a month earlier.

subject: Siege of Bridgwater (1645)
summary: Ten days in July 1645 that ended Royalist control of Somerset - and left a thriving port town so badly burned that Parliament itself wrote requesting its taxes be reduced.

subject: Siege of Bunratty
summary: For four months in 1646, English Parliamentary forces held the loveliest castle in Ireland against an Irish Confederate army - until the cannon on the shore won.

subject: Siege of Burgos
summary: Wellington's only significant defeat in the Peninsular War came at Burgos in 1812, where a French garrison of 2,000 held a castle against 35,000 Allied troops for five weeks using masterful defense and relentless sorties.

subject: Siege of Cahir Castle
summary: In 1599 the Earl of Essex brought sixteen thousand men and two cannons to break the strongest fortress in Ireland. Queen Elizabeth was unimpressed - she called the defenders a rabble of rogues.

subject: Siege of Carlisle (1315)
summary: A year after Bannockburn, Robert the Bruce brought catapults, a siege tower, and a mobile shelter called a sow to Carlisle's walls, and Cumbrian rain defeated all three.

subject: Siege of Carrigafoyle Castle
summary: Easter 1580: an English fleet and army battered a Shannon-mouth tower for two days, then killed nearly everyone inside - women, children, and the Italian engineer who had built the defences.

story.title: Siege of Chihaya: The Mountain That Broke a Shogunate

subject: Siege of Chihaya
summary: In 1333, a vastly outnumbered garrison on Mount Kongo used dummy soldiers, rolling boulders, and brilliant deception to hold Chihaya Castle against the Kamakura shogunate's army for three months -- a siege that changed the course of Japanese history.

subject: Siege of Ciudad Rodrigo (1812)
summary: In January 1812, Wellington's army stormed the Spanish fortress of Ciudad Rodrigo in less than two weeks, blasting open the northern gateway to French-occupied Spain at the cost of two generals killed and a city sacked by its own liberators.

subject: Siege of Coron (1533–1534)
summary: When Sultan Suleyman the Magnificent threatened to demolish the Church of the Holy Sepulchre unless he got Koroni back, it signaled how badly he wanted this small Peloponnesian fortress — and what followed was one of the most dramatic naval showdowns of the 16th-century Mediterranean.

subject: Siege of Culloden House (1715)
summary: A seven-week siege in the first Jacobite rising during which Lady Forbes of Culloden held off a clan force from inside her own house, refused all summons to surrender, and was eventually relieved by an opportunist Highland chief who used the favour to dodge a treason charge.

subject: Siege of Culloden House (1745)
summary: On the night of 15-16 October 1745, two hundred Fraser clansmen tried to kidnap Scotland's senior law officer from the same house that had been besieged thirty years earlier - and fled when the cannon balls began to tear through their cover.

subject: Siege of Cyropolis
summary: In 329 BCE, Alexander the Great took seven Sogdian towns in a brutal campaign that left him with a stone to the skull and thousands dead, culminating at the fortress city of Cyropolis.

subject: Siege of Cēsis Castle (1577)
summary: After five days of bombardment by Ivan the Terrible's army, around 300 people inside Cēsis Castle - many of them women and children - chose to die together by lighting four barrels of gunpowder rather than surrender.

subject: Siege of Dammaj
summary: The 2011-2014 Houthi siege of a Salafi town and its religious school in northern Yemen, a local sectarian fight that reflected the larger Saudi-Iranian contest.

subject: Siege of Dimdim
summary: A Kurdish fortress on the western shore of Lake Urmia became the site of a year-long siege in 1609-1610, when Shah Abbas I crushed the Emirate of Bradost -- a struggle remembered in Kurdish oral tradition as a symbol of resistance against foreign domination.

subject: Siege of Dunboy
summary: In June 1602, one hundred and forty-three Gaelic Irish defenders held an impregnable stone tower against an English army of five thousand. Only the story of their defiance survived.

subject: Siege of Fellin (1560)
summary: Three days of artillery brought down the walls of the Livonian Order's most important fortress in August 1560 - and with them, the entire crusader state that had ruled the eastern Baltic for three centuries.

subject: Siege of Fort Augustus (1746)
summary: In the final weeks before Culloden, Jacobite forces under an Irish brigade officer captured Fort Augustus -- a government stronghold in the Great Glen that even its own commanders considered indefensible.

subject: Siege of Fort Mackinac
summary: The first British victory of the War of 1812 came without a single shot fired, when a ragtag force of soldiers, fur traders, and Native warriors captured an unsuspecting American fort on a tiny island in the Straits of Mackinac.

subject: Siege of Fort Macon
summary: In April 1862, a one-day Union bombardment of an obsolete masonry fort on Bogue Banks ended the Confederate hold on Beaufort Inlet at the cost of nine Confederate and one Union dead.

subject: Siege of Fort Nashwaak
summary: A two-day siege in 1696 where French, Acadian, and Maliseet defenders repelled a New England force at the capital of Acadia, on the site of present-day Fredericton.

story.title: Siege of Fort Pulaski: The Day Brick Walls Became Obsolete

subject: Siege of Fort Pulaski
summary: A 30-hour bombardment in April 1862 proved that rifled cannon could shatter fortifications once thought invincible, ending the age of masonry coastal defense and closing the port of Savannah to the Confederacy.

subject: Siege of Fort St Philip (1756)
summary: The 1756 siege of Menorca that ended with a British surrender, a French occupation, and the execution of the admiral sent to prevent it all.

subject: Siege of Fort St. Jean
summary: A grueling 45-day siege in the fall of 1775 that opened the gates to Montreal but cost the Continental Army precious weeks -- time that would prove fatal to the American invasion of Canada.

subject: Siege of Fort William
summary: A two-week siege in March 1746 during the Jacobite rising, in which a small Highland force tried and failed to capture the last government fortress in the Great Glen.

subject: Siege of Fort Zeelandia
summary: The nine-month siege of 1661-1662 in which Ming loyalist Koxinga's 25,000 troops overwhelmed a Dutch garrison of fewer than 2,000, ending European rule on Taiwan and launching the island's first Chinese dynasty.

subject: Siege of Galle (1640)
summary: In March 1640, Dutch and Kandyan forces stormed the Portuguese fort at Galle after four days of bombardment, seizing control of southern Sri Lanka's richest cinnamon lands and reshaping the island's colonial future.

subject: Siege of Godesberg
summary: Fifteen hundred pounds of powder blew half the castle off the mountain. The garrison kept fighting. What ended it was the latrine.

subject: Siege of Grand Pré
summary: In November 1749, a combined force of Mi'kmaq, Maliseet, Penobscot, and Acadian militia besieged a British fort at Grand-Pre, capturing soldiers and igniting a conflict whose prisoners would not be ransomed for two years.

subject: Siege of Grave (1602)
summary: A Dutch-English army of 20,000 sat outside a Spanish-held river fortress for two months in 1602. When a bullet went through Sir Francis Vere's head and the Meuse began to flood, an eighteen-year-old prince had to finish the job.

subject: Siege of Grave (1674)
summary: Three months of cannon fire, a 71-year-old general who ignored expert advice, and a future king of England all collided at a tiny Dutch fortress on the Meuse.

subject: Siege of Groenlo (1627)
summary: In one summer month, Frederick Henry's army built a sixteen-kilometer earthwork ring around a small Spanish-held fortress town - and made siegecraft a Dutch art form.

subject: Siege of Hasedō
summary: A fourteen-day samurai siege in 1600 where a small castle garrison in northern Honshu held off 20,000 troops while the fate of all Japan was decided hundreds of miles to the south at Sekigahara.

subject: Siege of Havana
summary: In 1762, a massive British fleet threaded a channel the Spanish thought impassable, trapped twelve warships in Havana Harbor, and captured the strongest fortress in the Americas after a brutal two-month siege.

subject: Siege of Helmsley Castle
summary: Three months of starvation, a musket ball that nearly killed the future commander of the New Model Army, and a surrender on terms in November 1644.

subject: Siege of Herat (1221)
summary: In 1221, Tolui's Mongol army besieged the jewel of Khorasan twice, reducing one of Central Asia's greatest cities to ruins and killing hundreds of thousands of its inhabitants.

subject: Siege of Herat (1833)
summary: The 1833 siege of Herat pitted Qajar Iran against the local Durrani ruler Kamran Mirza, drawing Britain and Russia into a geopolitical chess match over the gateway to Afghanistan.

subject: Siege of Hull (1643)
summary: The second siege of Hull in autumn 1643, at the high point of the Royalist campaign, ended in another failure that broke the king's three-pronged advance on London and turned the war in Parliament's favour.

subject: Siege of Ichijōdani Castle
summary: In 1573, Oda Nobunaga's 30,000 soldiers swept into Echizen Province and destroyed the lavish castle town of Ichijodani, ending the Asakura clan's century of rule in a catastrophe of fire, betrayal, and ritual suicide.

subject: Siege of Inabayama Castle
summary: The 1567 mountaintop siege where Oda Nobunaga captured a fortress thought impregnable, renamed it Gifu Castle, and launched his campaign to unify Japan.

subject: Siege of Inverness (1429)
summary: After James I lured fifty Highland chiefs to Inverness Castle and arrested them all, the Lord of the Isles returned with an army and burned the town to the ground -- the violent price of royal treachery.

subject: Siege of Inverness (1562)
summary: Mary, Queen of Scots arrived at Inverness Castle on 9 September 1562 to find the gates shut against her; three days of siege ended with the Earl of Huntly's man hanged on the battlements and his head displayed for the town to see.

subject: Siege of Jinju (1592)
summary: Outnumbered nearly eight to one, Korean defenders held Jinju Fortress against 30,000 Japanese troops in one of the three defining battles of the Imjin War.

subject: Siege of Julich (1621-1622)
summary: A five-month winter siege that ended the Twelve Years' Truce, handed Spain a star fortress on the Rur, and ended with the garrison eating rat meat by candlelight.

subject: Siege of Kalmar (1525)
summary: A dinner invitation triggered betrayal, a fortress held by fifty against thousands, and a king who wept before ordering a massacre.

subject: Siege of Kastania
summary: In July 1780, a small Maniot garrison held off 10,000 Ottoman soldiers for twelve days in their stone tower-houses — and among the children who escaped was a boy named Theodoros Kolokotronis, who would grow up to lead the Greek War of Independence.

story.title: The Siege of Katsurayama: White Rice and a Last Stand in the Snow

subject: Siege of Katsurayama
summary: In March 1557, a desperate garrison poured white rice down castle walls to fake a waterfall, but a temple priest's betrayal sealed their fate in one of the bloodiest sieges of the Kawanakajima campaigns.

story.title: Siege of Kawagoe Castle: The Night Attack That Decided the Kanto

subject: Siege of Kawagoe Castle
summary: In April 1546, a garrison of 3,000 Hojo samurai held Kawagoe Castle against 80,000 besiegers -- then won by stripping off their armor, abandoning the tradition of taking heads, and attacking in the dark.

subject: Siege of Kenilworth
summary: Six months of trebuchets, wooden siege towers, and lake-borne assaults could not break the twelve hundred Disinherited rebels holding Kenilworth Castle in 1266. Hunger and disease ended what military force could not - and the negotiated peace that followed reshaped medieval English law.

subject: Siege of Lal Masjid
summary: The 2007 military siege of Islamabad's Red Mosque became a turning point in Pakistan's war against militancy, with consequences that reverberate to this day.

subject: Siege of Lathom House
summary: The last Royalist stronghold in Lancashire was defended for three months in 1644 by a French countess and a garrison of three hundred against a Parliamentary army nearly seven times their size, in a siege that became one of the iconic episodes of the English Civil War.

subject: Siege of Leiden
summary: In October 1574, after a year of starvation and plague, Dutch rebels broke the dykes and sailed a flotilla across the flooded countryside to rescue Leiden from a Spanish siege - and founded a university in thanks.

subject: Siege of Leningrad
summary: For 872 days, a city of three million people was deliberately starved by the Wehrmacht while making music, building tank columns, and burying its dead in trenches dug in frozen earth.

subject: Siege of Lichfield
summary: Prince Rupert blew a hole in the wall of Lichfield Cathedral Close with one of the earliest explosive mines used in England, and the siege of 1643 was decided by gunpowder underground.

subject: Siege of Lille (1708)
summary: Marlborough and Eugene laid siege to Europe's strongest fortress for 120 days and won it at a cost of 12,000 dead — the most expensive operation of the War of the Spanish Succession.

subject: Siege of Lille (1792)
summary: Sixty thousand cannon shot, eight days of fire, a citizen-gunner whose wife was giving birth as his house burned — and a French Revolutionary city that simply refused to fall.

subject: Siege of Lincoln
summary: A four-day Civil War siege in May 1644 in which Parliament's army stormed Lincoln by night up a rain-slicked hillside, captured the Royalist governor, and pillaged the upper town.

subject: Siege of Livadeia
summary: In March 1821, Greek chieftains Athanasios Diakos and Vasilis Bousgos seized the Boeotian town of Livadeia in one of the opening moves of the Greek War of Independence — a five-day struggle that ended with the Ottoman garrison surrendering its fortress for lack of food and water.

subject: Siege of Louisbourg (1745)
summary: A ragtag army of New England merchants, farmers, and fishermen besieged the most expensive French fortress in North America -- and won, shocking both empires in the process.

subject: Siege of Lérida
summary: In 1810, the French general Suchet broke Lleida not with cannon alone but by driving its own civilians under the castle walls, then bombarding them, in one of the Peninsular War's cruelest sieges.

subject: Siege of Monemvasia (1821)
summary: In the spring of 1821, Greek forces surrounded the ancient sea-rock fortress of Monemvasia, beginning a four-month ordeal that would make it the first Ottoman stronghold to fall in the Greek War of Independence.

subject: Siege of Mostar
summary: Mostar was besieged twice during the Bosnian War -- first by Yugoslav forces in 1992, then by former Croat allies who turned on their Bosniak neighbors in a conflict that destroyed the city's iconic bridge and its multiethnic character.

subject: Siege of Myitkyina
summary: In the monsoon-drenched jungles of northern Burma, Chinese, American, and British forces fought for months to capture a single airfield that could change the course of World War II in Asia.

subject: Siege of Negroponte (1470)
summary: In the summer of 1470, Mehmed II turned the full weight of the Ottoman Empire on Venice's island-fortress at Chalcis, and the city that fell became the Aegean's answer to the fall of Constantinople.

subject: Siege of Negroponte (1688)
summary: In 1688 Venice came to take the great Ottoman fortress on Euboea and instead watched its army die of plague in the marshes outside the walls.

subject: Siege of Ninety Six
summary: A Polish engineer, a wooden sniper tower, and 28 days of digging through rock-hard Carolina clay -- the 1781 Siege of Ninety Six was the Revolutionary War battle where everything went wrong for the Patriots and a tiny Loyalist garrison refused to break.

subject: Siege of Ochakov (1737)
summary: A single accidental spark turned a besieged Ottoman fortress into an inferno, and a two-day assault into one of the deadliest days the Black Sea coast had ever seen.

subject: Siege of Odawara (1569)
summary: The legendary Takeda Shingen marched an army across three provinces to strike at the Hojo clan's impregnable fortress of Odawara -- only to burn the castle town and retreat after just three days, triggering a bloody ambush at Mimase Pass.

subject: Siege of Odawara (1590)
summary: Toyotomi Hideyoshi broke Japan's most impregnable castle not with swords or siege towers, but with jugglers, prostitutes, and a fake castle that appeared to materialize overnight -- ending a century of Hojo clan dominance.

subject: Siege of Oshi
summary: The 1590 battle where 2,619 defenders -- including a lord's daughter -- held off 23,000 troops for over a month, turning a swamp fortress into a legend and destroying the career of the general who failed to take it.

story.title: The Siege of Otate: When Brothers Tore the Dragon's Legacy Apart

subject: Siege of Otate
summary: The sudden death of Uesugi Kenshin in 1578 left no clear heir, and his two adopted sons turned the castle town below Kasugayama into a battlefield that nearly destroyed the most powerful clan in northern Japan.

subject: Siege of Patras (1821)
summary: In the first days of the Greek War of Independence in 1821, Greek fighters seized Patras and raised the flag — only for an Ottoman army to retake the city that April, beginning a seven-year occupation that left much of the city in ruins.

subject: Siege of Polotsk (1563)
summary: Ivan the Terrible's largest 16th-century campaign - a winter siege that took the Lithuanian fortress of Polotsk for Muscovy, opened the road to Vilnius, and ended in atrocities that shocked Europe.

subject: Siege of Przemyśl
summary: The longest siege in Europe during World War I, where 127,000 Austro-Hungarian soldiers held a fortress on the River San for 133 days before starvation and disease forced their surrender.

subject: Siege of Rhodes (88 BC)
summary: King Mithridates of Pontus tried to take Rhodes from the sea with a siege tower mounted on warships; smaller, faster Rhodian biremes turned the assault into a humiliating retreat.

subject: Siege of Saigon
summary: A two-year siege in which a tiny Franco-Spanish garrison clung to a captured fort in Saigon while 10,000 Vietnamese soldiers surrounded them, wars in Europe and China drained reinforcements, and the entire campaign teetered on collapse.

subject: Siege of Sanjō Palace
summary: A midnight raid on a Kyoto palace in 1160 ignited a civil war that reshaped Japan, and the burning is now immortalized in one of the most celebrated handscrolls in the history of art.

subject: Siege of St Andrews Castle
summary: The 18-month siege of 1546-1547 that began with a Cardinal's murder, made John Knox a galley slave, and turned a quarrel over religion into a chapter of European war.

subject: Siege of Steinvikholm (1537)
summary: The 1537 siege of Steinvikholm Castle was the last stand of Catholic resistance in Norway, ending a religious struggle that reshaped the nation.

subject: Siege of Stirling Castle (1746)
summary: Three weeks of Jacobite gunfire against impregnable walls, ending in a French engineer's humiliation and an exploded church.

subject: Siege of Tartu (1224)
summary: When the last Estonian fortress fell to crusaders on 15 August 1224, only one defender was allowed to live, sent to Novgorod with a horse and clothes to carry the news.

subject: Siege of Thessalonica (617)
summary: When an Avar siege tower collapsed and killed its crew at the walls of Thessalonica in 617, the city's defenders attributed their survival to Saint Demetrius, their patron saint.

subject: Siege of Thessalonica (676–678)
summary: Perboundos spoke Greek, kept a residence in Thessalonica, and dressed as a Byzantine. His arrest and execution by the emperor in 676 ignited a two-year Slavic siege of the city.

subject: Siege of Tre Kronor
summary: A seven-month siege where a queen defended Stockholm's royal castle against Swedish rebels, only to surrender when just 70 of her 1,000 soldiers remained alive.

subject: Siege of Tsingtao
summary: The only major land battle of World War I in the Asian-Pacific theater, where 23,000 Japanese and 1,500 British troops besieged a German garrison of 3,625 men defending a colonial port that would change China's political future.

story.title: The Siege of Uozu: A Victory That Arrived Too Late

subject: Siege of Uozu
summary: In June 1582, thirteen samurai defenders held Uozu Castle against an Oda army of tens of thousands for three months -- then chose mass suicide over surrender, never knowing that their enemy's lord, Oda Nobunaga, had already been assassinated in Kyoto.

subject: Siege of Valencia (1092–1094)
summary: El Cid's nineteen-month siege of Muslim Valencia, born of a palace coup and won by a daring night raid, made him lord of a city he would hold only briefly.

subject: Siege of Wardour Castle
summary: In 1643, a 60-year-old Catholic widow named Blanche Arundell defended Wardour Castle against 1,300 Parliamentarian troops with 25 soldiers. Her son retook the castle the next year by tunnelling under the walls.

subject: Siege of Wark (1138)
summary: A six-month Scottish blockade of an English border castle that helped redraw the map of Britain in 1139.

subject: Siege of Zamboanga
summary: In 1898, General Vicente Alvarez assembled an army of Christians, Muslims, and tribal warriors to besiege the Spanish garrison at Fort Pilar, culminating in one of the few successful revolutionary actions in Mindanao and the founding of the short-lived Republic of Zamboanga.

subject: Siege of the Acropolis (1687)
summary: On the evening of 26 September 1687, a Venetian mortar shell hit the Parthenon, where Ottoman defenders had stored gunpowder; the explosion killed three hundred people and tore the temple apart.

subject: Siege of the Acropolis (1821–1822)
summary: In the first year of the Greek War of Independence, revolutionaries besieged the Ottoman garrison atop the Acropolis - a siege that ended in surrender and then, tragically, in slaughter.

subject: Siege of the Acropolis (1826–1827)
summary: Four years after the Greeks took the Acropolis, the Ottomans came to take it back - and the failed attempt to relieve the garrison cost the Greek cause one of its greatest captains.

story.title: Siege of the British Residency in Kabul

subject: Siege of the British Residency in Kabul
summary: On September 3, 1879, mutinous Afghan soldiers overwhelmed a British diplomatic compound inside Kabul's Bala Hissar fortress, killing nearly all 79 occupants in an eight-hour battle that altered the course of the Second Anglo-Afghan War.

story.title: Siege of the Castle of Saint George

subject: Siege of the Castle of Saint George
summary: On Christmas Eve 1500, a Spanish-Venetian army stormed Cephalonia's hilltop fortress and ended two decades of Ottoman rule over one of the Ionian Islands.

story.title: Siege of the Chinese University of Hong Kong

subject: Siege of the Chinese University of Hong Kong
summary: For five days in November 2019, the campus of the Chinese University of Hong Kong became the epicenter of one of the most intense confrontations of Hong Kong's protest movement, as students and police clashed across the university's bridges and grounds.

subject: Siege of Älvsborg (1563)
summary: A swift Danish victory at Sweden's crucial Atlantic gateway ignited a seven-year war for Scandinavian supremacy.

subject: Siege of Älvsborg (1612)
summary: Swedish defenders blew up their own fortress entrance to halt a Danish assault, but ultimately surrendered the strategic castle to Christian IV.

subject: Siege of Đắk Đoa
summary: A seven-day siege in February 1954 that destroyed a French outpost in the highlands, and ended with an unidentified man whistling La Marseillaise in the ruins.

subject: Sigma School shooting
summary: On 28 October 2002, two fifteen-year-old students - Vanessa Carvalho Batista and Natasha Silva Ferreira - were killed at the Escola Sigma in Salvador, in one of the first recorded school shootings in Brazil.

subject: Silvertown explosion
summary: At 6.52 p.m. on a Friday in January 1917, fifty tonnes of TNT detonated at a munitions plant on the Thames. Seventy-three people died. The factory had been built in the middle of a working-class neighbourhood, and the workers were mostly women.

subject: Singapore Airlines Flight 006
summary: A Boeing 747-400 attempted takeoff on a closed runway during a typhoon at Taipei's airport in October 2000, killing 83 people in Singapore Airlines' first fatal accident.

subject: Sinking of MV Sewol
summary: The 2014 sinking of the ferry Sewol killed 304 people, most of them high school students, and became a defining national tragedy that reshaped South Korean politics and society.

story.title: South-East Asian Theatre of World War II

subject: South-East Asian theatre of World War II
summary: The vast and often overlooked theatre where Japan's lightning conquests of 1941-42 swept across the Philippines, Malaya, Burma, and the Dutch East Indies, only to be reversed by Allied forces in campaigns that soldiers themselves called 'the Forgotten War.'

subject: Southern Airways Flight 932
summary: On a rainy November evening in 1970, a chartered DC-9 carrying the Marshall University football team crashed into a West Virginia hillside, killing all 75 aboard in the deadliest sports-related air disaster in American history.

subject: Southwest Airlines Flight 812
summary: On April 1, 2011, a five-foot hole tore open in the fuselage of a Southwest Airlines 737 at 34,000 feet near Yuma — rapid decompression sent oxygen masks dropping, the plane dived 25,000 feet, and 122 people landed safely at Yuma International Airport with two minor injuries.

subject: St. Nedelya Church bombing
summary: On Holy Thursday in 1925, a bomb hidden in the dome of a Sofia cathedral killed 213 mourners and triggered one of Europe's most brutal political reprisals.

subject: Station Fire (2009)
summary: The 2009 Station Fire burned 160,557 acres of the Angeles National Forest — the largest in modern Los Angeles County history — killing two firefighters and threatening the Mount Wilson Observatory.

subject: Stockline Plastics Factory Explosion
summary: On 11 May 2004, a corroded liquefied petroleum gas pipe beneath a Maryhill factory ignited, collapsing the four-storey building and killing nine workers - a disaster whose causes had been hiding in plain sight for nearly forty years.

subject: Superga air disaster
summary: On May 4, 1949, a plane carrying the legendary Grande Torino football team crashed into the Basilica of Superga in fog, killing all 31 aboard and ending the greatest dynasty in Italian football history.

subject: Suzano massacre
summary: On March 13, 2019, a school shooting at the Professor Raul Brasil State School in Suzano, Brazil killed seven people and wounded eleven, leaving a community shattered and a nation grappling with how to protect its children.

subject: Suzugamori execution grounds
summary: A small triangular memorial wedged between modern highways in Shinagawa marks the spot where the Tokugawa shogunate executed an estimated 100,000 people over 220 years, with the original iron burning post and crucifixion stone base still standing among the traffic.

subject: Synagogue Church building collapse
summary: On September 12, 2014, a guesthouse at the Synagogue Church of All Nations in Lagos collapsed, killing at least 115 people, most of them South African pilgrims, in a disaster defined by structural failure and obstructed justice.

subject: Tangiwai disaster
summary: On Christmas Eve 1953, a lahar from Mount Ruapehu destroyed a railway bridge minutes before an express train arrived, killing 151 people in New Zealand's worst rail disaster.

subject: Tartu Credit Center massacre
summary: On 14 January 1919, hours before the Bolsheviks fled Tartu, a Red commissar took 19 prisoners one by one into the cellar of the Credit Center building and shot them.

subject: Taunton Sleeping Car Fire
summary: Twelve passengers died in a British Rail sleeping car near Taunton on 6 July 1978, killed by smoke from a fire caused by dirty bed linen stacked against an electric heater. An MP in the House of Commons asked the question that should have been asked a century earlier: should we not have learned by now?

subject: Tay Bridge disaster
summary: On the stormy night of 28 December 1879, the central spans of the Tay Bridge collapsed as a train crossed, plunging 75 people into the icy waters below in one of Britain's worst engineering disasters.

subject: Ten Children, One Night
summary: In 1923, a serial arsonist set fire to a Japanese Buddhist boarding school dormitory in Sacramento, killing ten children -- a crime born of racial hatred in an era that treated anti-Japanese violence as barely newsworthy.

subject: Tenaja Fire
summary: A September 2019 wildfire that forced 1,200 evacuations and closed three school districts as families searched for clean air while smoke blanketed Riverside County.

story.title: Tet Offensive Attack on Tan Son Nhut Air Base

subject: Tet Offensive attack on Tan Son Nhut Air Base
summary: In the predawn hours of January 31, 1968, over 2,600 Vietcong and North Vietnamese soldiers attacked Saigon's most important military airfield, launching one of the Tet Offensive's boldest strikes against the heart of American and South Vietnamese air power.

subject: Thai Airways International Flight 601
summary: On 30 June 1967, a Thai Airways Caravelle descended through Typhoon Anita toward the notoriously difficult Kai Tak Airport and never pulled up — 24 people died in the waters off Hong Kong.

subject: Thanksgiving Day Disaster
summary: On November 29, 1900, hundreds of fans climbed onto the roof of a glassworks factory to watch the Cal-Stanford Big Game for free -- and the roof collapsed into a furnace of molten glass, killing 23 people.

subject: The 26 Blocks Scandal
summary: Beginning in 1980, structural failures in Hong Kong's public housing stock revealed a pattern of shoddy construction and bribery across hundreds of tower blocks — a scandal that eventually led to the demolition of 26 buildings and forced the relocation of tens of thousands of residents.

subject: The Airline That Cracked
summary: A Boeing 737 fractured on landing at Surabaya's Juanda Airport in 2007, exposing systemic safety failures at Adam Air and triggering Indonesia's reckoning with its aviation industry.

story.title: The Assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.: The Shot That Echoed Across America

subject: The Assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.
summary: Where a single rifle shot from a rooming house bathroom killed Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. on the balcony of the Lorraine Motel in Memphis on April 4, 1968, triggering riots in over 100 American cities.

story.title: The Bomber That Hit White Hill

subject: The Bomber That Hit White Hill
summary: A fog-blinded B-17 Flying Fortress crashed into a Marin County hillside in 1946 while its crew believed they were over Oakland -- and what the military removed from the wreckage at gunpoint has fueled speculation ever since.

subject: The Choir That Never Sang
summary: A 1976 school bus crash on a Martinez freeway ramp killed 29 people, most of them high school choir students on their way to a friendship concert, in what remains the deadliest bus accident in American history.

story.title: The Crystal Palace Fire: When London's Glass Wonder Burned

subject: The Crystal Palace Fire
summary: Where the iconic glass and iron structure that had hosted the Great Exhibition of 1851 burned to the ground in 1936, creating a blaze visible from eight counties and ending an era of Victorian ambition.

story.title: The Eastland Disaster: When a Ship Capsized at the Dock

subject: The Eastland Disaster
summary: Where 844 people died when a passenger ship rolled over while still tied to a Chicago pier in 1915, trapping hundreds below decks in a disaster forgotten in the shadow of the Titanic.

story.title: The Expedition That Ended Before It Began

subject: The Expedition That Ended Before It Began
summary: In 1814, three thousand British soldiers sailed to punish a Balinese king for raiding Java - only to find him waiting at the palace door with an apology and two hostages already in hand.

story.title: The General Slocum Disaster: The Day a Sunday School Picnic Killed 1,021 People

subject: The General Slocum Disaster
summary: Where a steamboat carrying German immigrants on a church outing caught fire and sank in New York's East River in 1904, destroying an entire neighborhood's community.

story.title: The Iroquois Theatre Fire: 602 Dead in 15 Minutes

subject: The Iroquois Theatre Fire
summary: Where a fire during a matinee performance killed 602 people in 1903, mostly women and children, because the 'fireproof' theatre had locked its exit doors.

subject: The Marriott Bombing of 2003
summary: Two weeks before a car bomb tore through the lobby of the JW Marriott Jakarta, police in Semarang had captured a militant who warned them it was coming -- but the warning was not enough to stop it.

subject: The Red Bridge at Dawn
summary: The bloodiest single battle of the Indonesian Revolution turned a military defeat into the moral foundation of a nation, and gave Indonesia its Heroes' Day.

story.title: The Schoellkopf Collapse: When Niagara Ate a Power Plant

subject: The Schoellkopf Collapse
summary: The 1956 day when the cliff behind Niagara Falls simply let go - swallowing one of the world's oldest hydroelectric plants, killing one worker, and reminding humanity that the falls are eating themselves backward at three feet per year.

subject: The Siege at Lindhurst
summary: On a Friday afternoon in 1992, a former student returned to Lindhurst High School in Olivehurst with a shotgun, a grudge, and nothing left to lose - killing four people and holding eighty hostages through an eight-hour standoff that became one of America's deadliest school shootings.

story.title: The Tenerife Airport Disaster: 583 Dead in Aviation's Darkest Day

subject: The Tenerife Airport Disaster
summary: Where two Boeing 747s collided on a foggy runway in the Canary Islands in 1977, killing 583 people in the deadliest accident in aviation history - caused by a cascade of miscommunications and impatience.

story.title: The Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire: The Tragedy That Changed Labor

subject: The Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire
summary: Where 146 garment workers, mostly young immigrant women, died in a 1911 fire because their employers had locked the exit doors, transforming American workplace safety.

subject: The Warehouse on Oakdale Road
summary: A fireworks warehouse explosion near Esparto, California on July 1, 2025 killed seven workers, sparked a 78-acre wildfire, and exposed troubling questions about oversight and permitting.

subject: The Woman in Red
summary: On a September morning in 1975, a Manson Family follower pointed a pistol at President Gerald Ford on the grounds of the California State Capitol -- and the gun did not fire.

subject: Third Battle of Petersburg
summary: A predawn artillery bombardment, a Sixth Corps breakthrough, and a desperate Confederate stand at Fort Gregg cracked open the siege of Petersburg on April 2, 1865, and put Robert E. Lee on the road to Appomattox.

subject: Third Battle of Torreón
summary: In December 1916, Pancho Villa traded one city for another, abandoning Chihuahua to seize the less-defended Torreón in a three-day battle whose aftermath left a trail of mutilation, revenge, and an accidental survivor who would one day help murder Villa himself.

subject: Third Servile War
summary: In 73 BC, about seventy gladiators broke out of a training school in Capua with kitchen knives, built an army of 120,000 enslaved people, humiliated Rome's legions for two years, and gave history the name Spartacus.

subject: Three Thousand Feet Short
summary: On July 1, 1993, a Fokker F28 ignored warnings to divert and attempted to land at Jefman Airport in a tropical downpour. The aircraft struck a hill 3,000 feet short of the runway, killing 41 of the 43 people on board.

subject: Torre del Bierzo rail disaster
summary: Spain's worst rail disaster, hidden for decades by Franco's censorship, in which a runaway passenger train, a shunting engine, and a coal train collided and burned inside a tunnel on 3 January 1944.

subject: Toulouse chemical factory explosion
summary: Ten days after September 11, an explosion at a fertilizer factory in Toulouse killed 31 people, shattered two-thirds of the city's windows, and left France unsure whether it was facing terrorism or industrial catastrophe.

subject: TransAsia Airways Flight 222
summary: On the evening of 23 July 2014, a TransAsia ATR 72 carrying 58 people from Kaohsiung to Magong crashed on approach to Penghu Airport during the tail end of Typhoon Matmo. Forty-eight people died. Ten survived.

story.title: The Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire: 146 Lives and the Birth of Workplace Safety

subject: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire
summary: On March 25, 1911, a fire in a Greenwich Village garment factory killed 146 workers, most of them young immigrant women, behind doors that had been locked by their employers -- and transformed American labor law forever.

story.title: Triangle Shirtwaist Fire: The Disaster That Changed Worker Safety Forever

subject: Triangle Shirtwaist Fire
summary: The New York factory fire that killed 146 workers in 1911 - where locked doors trapped young women, where some jumped rather than burn, and where public outrage finally created the labor safety laws we take for granted today.

story.title: UPS Flight 1354: The Cost of Fatigue

subject: UPS Airlines Flight 1354
summary: On an August night in 2013, a UPS cargo plane crashed short of the runway at Birmingham-Shuttlesworth International Airport, killing both pilots -- an accident the NTSB traced to fatigue, a closed runway, and a chain of errors that began long before the final approach.

subject: University of Texas tower shooting
summary: On August 1, 1966, a former Marine turned sniper killed 17 people and wounded 31 others from atop the UT Tower observation deck, an act of mass murder that reshaped American policing and haunted Austin for decades.

subject: Varig Flight 837
summary: On the night of March 5, 1967, a Brazilian DC-8 on a multi-stop journey from Beirut to Rio de Janeiro crashed short of Roberts International Airport in Liberia, killing fifty-six people in the worst aviation disaster in the country's history.

subject: Vega de Tera disaster
summary: In January 1959, a poorly designed dam collapsed in the mountains of Zamora, sending 7.8 million cubic meters of water into the sleeping village of Ribadelago and killing 144 people.

subject: Viasa Flight 742
summary: On March 16, 1969, an overloaded DC-9 struck power lines after takeoff from Maracaibo's Grano de Oro Airport and crashed into a residential neighborhood, killing 155 people and becoming the world's deadliest civil aviation disaster at the time.

subject: Victoria Hall disaster
summary: On June 16, 1883, one hundred and eighty-three children between the ages of three and fourteen were crushed to death in a stairwell at Victoria Hall in Sunderland, making it one of the deadliest civilian disasters in British history.

subject: Vierzy tunnel disaster
summary: A railway tunnel scarred by three wars finally collapsed during routine repairs, trapping two trains in the dark and killing 108 people in France's deadliest rail disaster since 1933.

subject: Villa Tunari massacre
summary: On 27 June 1988, Bolivian security forces opened fire on unarmed coca-farming families protesting crop eradication in the Chapare, killing between nine and twelve people and shaping a generation of political resistance.

subject: Vinkt Massacre
summary: Over three days in May 1940, German soldiers at a small bridge in Flemish farmland murdered around 86 Belgian civilians. The last five were forced to dig their own graves. The killings continued for hours after Belgium had already surrendered.

subject: Vitória School Attack
summary: A planned attack on a Vitória middle school on August 19, 2022, stopped cold by staff who chose to confront the attacker.

subject: Wanggongchang Explosion
summary: In 1626, a catastrophic explosion at a Beijing gunpowder factory killed around 20,000 people, shook the ground 150 kilometers away, and may have helped topple the Ming dynasty.

subject: Wanshan Archipelago Campaign
summary: In the summer of 1950, a single 25-ton communist gunboat named Liberation attacked a nationalist fleet twenty times its size at the mouth of the Pearl River — and changed the outcome of China's Civil War in its final offshore theatre.

subject: War Eagle Field
summary: Five miles west of Lancaster, a former wartime airfield trained thousands of RAF, RCAF, and USAAF cadets to fly between 1941 and 1945. The Polaris Flight Academy's runways are still visible from the air — the site is now an LA County detention facility.

subject: War School of Kaunas
summary: An interwar military academy that trained 4,000 Lithuanian officers in two decades, then was dissolved into the Red Army in 1940.

subject: Warrington bombings
summary: Two children died on Bridge Street on a Saturday morning before Mother's Day. Out of their loss came the Peace Centre that bears their names.

subject: Weierkang Club Fire
summary: A natural gas leak in a Taichung restaurant killed 64 people in 1995 after blocked emergency exits, unbreakable windows, and fleeing employees trapped diners inside, forcing Taiwan to overhaul its fire safety laws.

subject: Welshampton Rail Crash
summary: On 11 June 1897, a Sunday school excursion train returning to Royton in Lancashire derailed near Welshampton in the Welsh borders. Twelve people died, most of them children and teachers.

subject: Welwyn Tunnel rail crash
summary: In June 1866, two telegraph needle codes that differed only by the number of beats ended up sending three trains, one after another, into the same dark tunnel - and a fire of roasting meat burned for two days above Welwyn.

story.title: West German Embassy Siege in Stockholm

subject: West German Embassy siege in Stockholm
summary: On a spring evening in 1975, West German terrorists seized their own country's embassy in Stockholm, launching a hostage crisis that ended in explosion and death.

subject: Westdene Dam Disaster
summary: On an ordinary autumn afternoon in 1985, a school bus left the road at the Westdene Dam, and forty-two children did not come home.

story.title: When the Banda Sea Stood Up: Ambon's 1674 Megatsunami

subject: When the Banda Sea Stood Up
summary: On a Saturday evening in 1674, as residents of Ambon celebrated the Chinese New Year, an earthquake shook the island so violently that church bells rang by themselves - and then a wall of water taller than the coastal hills swept everything away.

story.title: When the Towers Fell: The Waru Wora Fire

subject: When the Towers Fell
summary: A devastating fire swept through one of Sumba's most important traditional villages in December 2025, destroying 28 tower-shaped ancestral houses and displacing 139 people -- but sparing every life.

subject: Whiskey Au Go Go fire
summary: In the early hours of 8 March 1973, fifteen people died when arsonists set fire to a Fortitude Valley nightclub - a warning had been given, and ignored, and the building offered no way out.

subject: Widerøe Flight 710
summary: On 6 May 1988, a Wideroe Dash 7 flew into the side of Torghatten mountain during approach to Bronnoy sound Airport, killing all thirty-six people on board in the deadliest aviation disaster in Northern Norway's history.

subject: Widerøe Flight 839
summary: A 1990 Twin Otter crash on the wind-battered island of Værøy that killed five people, permanently closed an airport, and triggered a years-long investigation into whether wind or metal fatigue brought the plane down.

subject: Willow Island Disaster
summary: On a spring morning in 1978, a cooling tower under construction on the Ohio River peeled itself apart and took fifty-one men with it - the deadliest construction accident in American history.

subject: Wimbledon School Crash
summary: A summer tea party on the last day of term ended in tragedy when a Land Rover crashed through the fence of a Wimbledon prep school, killing two eight-year-old girls.

subject: Winecoff Hotel fire
summary: The deadliest hotel fire in American history unfolded inside a fifteen-story Atlanta building advertised as 'absolutely fireproof,' killing 119 people and reshaping fire safety codes across the nation.

subject: Worsley Hotel fire
summary: A 1974 arson at a Maida Vale hotel housing hotel workers from across the world killed seven people, including a young fireman from Kent.

subject: Ycuá Bolaños supermarket fire
summary: On August 1, 2004, a fire broke out in an Asunción supermarket, and when the owners ordered the doors locked to prevent theft, over 400 people were trapped and killed in one of the deadliest building fires in South American history.

subject: York Minster fire
summary: Three days after a controversial bishop's consecration, lightning struck York Minster - and a debate about divine retribution shared headlines with the firefighters who pulled down a burning roof to save the cathedral.

subject: YouTube Headquarters Shooting
summary: On April 3, 2018, a shooter opened fire at YouTube's headquarters in San Bruno, California, wounding three employees before taking her own life in the courtyard.

subject: Zhengzhou Airport riot
summary: A two-day uprising by stranded Chinese New Year travelers at Zhengzhou's airport in 2014 exposed the collision between China's explosive growth in air travel and infrastructure that couldn't keep pace.

subject: Ålesund fire
summary: A cow kicked a torch in a fish-packing factory at 2 AM, and by dawn nearly 850 wooden houses had burned to the ground, reshaping a Norwegian port city forever.

subject: École Polytechnique massacre
summary: On a December evening at Montreal's engineering school, fourteen women were murdered in an anti-feminist attack that transformed Canadian gun control, emergency response, and the national conversation about violence against women.

subject: 'Uruq Bani Ma'arid
summary: On the western edge of the world's largest sand desert, a Saudi reserve brought the Arabian oryx back from extinction in the wild -- earning UNESCO World Heritage status for a landscape most maps leave blank.

subject: 10 Downing Street
summary: The world's most famous front door - a 1735 conversion of three crumbling Georgian properties on a cul-de-sac built by a Cromwellian spy, almost demolished a dozen times, now the home and office of every British prime minister.

subject: 100 Terraced Rice Fields of Japan
summary: Japan's official list of its most spectacular terraced rice paddies, selected in 1999 to preserve landscapes carved into mountainsides over centuries of painstaking labor.

subject: 100% NL
summary: A Dutch radio station born from a 23-million-versus-8,000-euro lawsuit, broadcasting nederpop to a country that almost never heard its own music on its own airwaves.

story.title: 100th Anniversary of the Chinese Communist Party

subject: 100th Anniversary of the Chinese Communist Party
summary: On July 1, 2021, the Chinese Communist Party marked its centennial with a massive ceremony at Tiananmen Square featuring 71 fighter jets forming the number 100 overhead.

subject: 102.5 Radio Pembrokeshire
summary: A 30-day trial broadcast from a chapel basement in Pembroke in 1999 grew into a county-wide radio station that now serves 24,000 weekly listeners across western Wales.

subject: 115 (barge)
summary: The last shipwreck of the 1800s on the Great Lakes, whaleback Barge 115 broke free in a December storm and drifted for five days before smashing into Pic Island, where her crew survived by sheer resourcefulness and luck.

subject: 12-3 incident
summary: On December 3, 1966, eight Chinese protesters died in Macau when colonial authorities crushed a demonstration that began with a bribe and ended with Portugal signing a public apology under a portrait of Mao Zedong.

subject: 16th Avenue Tiled Steps
summary: A 163-step mosaic stairway in San Francisco's Golden Gate Heights neighborhood, where 220 neighbors hand-tiled a sea-to-stars design that Fodor's calls 'possibly the loveliest street stairway anywhere.'

subject: 1717–1718 Acts of Grace
summary: King George I's royal proclamation offered Caribbean pirates a stark choice: accept a pardon and abandon the black flag, or face the hangman's noose.

subject: 1790 Footprints
summary: Preserved in volcanic ash near Kilauea, these footprints are the haunting trace of Hawaiian warriors caught in a pyroclastic eruption during the wars that would unite the islands under Kamehameha I.

subject: 18 de Julio Avenue
summary: Montevideo's grand avenue is named for a single date — the day Uruguay swore in its first constitution — and it runs straight through the city's history, art deco palaces and all.

subject: 1811 Independence Movement
summary: On November 5, 1811, a group of priests, doctors, and merchants in San Salvador launched Central America's first revolt against Spanish rule -- and waited for a bell that never rang.

subject: 1837 Suffolk head-on collision
summary: The first fatal head-on train collision in history struck Suffolk, Virginia, on August 11, 1837, when a lumber train and a passenger express carrying 200 steamboat excursionists met on a blind curve.

subject: 1880 Southern Luzon earthquakes
summary: In July 1880, a devastating sequence of three major earthquakes shattered Manila and the surrounding provinces of Luzon, turning the colonial capital to rubble while the Pasig River ran black with mud and Taal Volcano awakened in sympathy.

subject: 1888 Barcelona Universal Exposition
summary: Spain's first World's Fair transformed a hated military citadel into Barcelona's beloved Ciutadella Park and announced the city's ambitions on the global stage.

story.title: The 1892 Sack of Salaga: When a Trade Empire Tore Itself Apart

subject: 1892 Sack of Salaga
summary: A civil war within the Gonja kingdom destroyed West Africa's greatest inland trade center, scattered its cosmopolitan population across the forest belt, and opened the door to European colonial control of northern Ghana.

subject: 1903 U.S. Open (golf)
summary: The ninth U.S. Open, held at Baltusrol Golf Club in 1903, featured a dramatic playoff in a rainstorm and launched Willie Anderson's record-setting run of three consecutive titles.

subject: 1906 Atlantic City train wreck
summary: On a sunny October Sunday in 1906, an electric train hit an open drawbridge at 40 miles per hour and dropped 15 feet into the water. Fifty-three people drowned.

subject: 1907 Vancouver Anti-Asian Riots
summary: Ten thousand people marched behind a band to Vancouver's city hall in September 1907; by three in the morning, Chinatown's windows were gone and Powell Street had fought the mob to a standstill.

story.title: 1910 Los Angeles International Air Meet at Dominguez Field

subject: 1910 Los Angeles International Air Meet at Dominguez Field
summary: In January 1910, on a hilltop south of Los Angeles, 254,000 people watched the future arrive — ten days of daring flights that launched America's love affair with aviation.

subject: 1911 South Wales Anti-Jewish Riots
summary: In the summer of 1911, mobs attacked Jewish-owned shops across the South Wales valleys until Winston Churchill sent troops to stop what he called a pogrom.

subject: 1916–1917 Nantou Earthquakes
summary: A sequence of earthquakes that struck central Taiwan's Nantou region across 1916 and 1917, killing 71 people and revealing how little the colonial government understood about the seismic forces beneath the island it administered.

subject: 1921 SNETA Farman Goliath ditching
summary: On 26 August 1921, a Belgian mail plane broke up over the English Channel and crashed three nautical miles off Calais - one of the earliest losses of the airliner that pioneered scheduled European air travel.

subject: 1926 Padang Panjang earthquakes
summary: On a single June morning in 1926, two powerful earthquakes struck the highland town of Padang Panjang less than three hours apart, leveling buildings and triggering a wave of religious fervor across West Sumatra.

subject: 1930 FIFA World Cup
summary: The very first World Cup was held in Montevideo in 1930 — the European teams crossed the ocean by steamship, the final used two different balls, and Uruguay won it all.

subject: 1932 Kimberley rescue
summary: In 1932, two German aviators attempting to circumnavigate the world crash-landed their seaplane on the Kimberley coast and spent 53 days barefoot, naked, and near death before Balanggarra Aboriginal people found them sheltering in a cave.

subject: 1934 Constantine riots
summary: A 1934 antisemitic pogrom in the Algerian city of Constantine that killed 28 people and exposed the fault lines of French colonial rule.

subject: 1935 Copperbelt strike
summary: On 29 May 1935, six African miners were killed by colonial police at the Roan Antelope mine. The strike failed. What it started changed Africa.

subject: 1936 Paraparaumu train wreck
summary: A dairy farmer saw the landslide and ran for the signal wire, but the Night Limited was already bearing down through the rain at fifty miles an hour.

subject: 1937 Heze earthquakes
summary: Two massive earthquakes struck Shandong province on consecutive days in July and August 1937, killing over 3,252 people and destroying 470,000 homes while China's attention was consumed by the outbreak of war with Japan.

subject: 1945 El Teniente Mining Accident
summary: On a June morning in 1945, fire above ground filled the tunnels of El Teniente with smoke, and 355 Chilean copper miners never came home - the deadliest metal-mining disaster in world history.

story.title: 1947 BSAA Avro Lancastrian Star Dust accident

subject: 1947 BSAA Avro Lancastrian Star Dust accident
summary: An airliner crossing the Andes vanished in 1947 after sending one final, baffling Morse word - and the mountain kept its secret for half a century.

subject: 1957 Valencia flood
summary: A catastrophic flood that killed at least 81 people and permanently reshaped Valencia, prompting the Spanish government to reroute the Turia River entirely around the city.

subject: 1959 Ryder Cup
summary: The thirteenth Ryder Cup, played at Eldorado Country Club in Indian Wells in November 1959, ended with a British team that had crossed the Atlantic and endured a turbulent flight before switching to a bus — arriving ill — to lose once again to the United States.

subject: 1966 Xingtai earthquakes
summary: A devastating sequence of six earthquakes struck southern Hebei over three weeks in March 1966, killing over 8,000 people and destroying more than five million houses.

subject: 1967 Newark riots
summary: Four days of violence in July 1967 left 26 dead in Newark, New Jersey, exposing decades of racial injustice and accelerating the city's long decline.

subject: 1968 Olympics Black Power salute
summary: The iconic moment when San Jose State sprinters Tommie Smith and John Carlos raised black-gloved fists on the Olympic podium in Mexico City, transforming a medal ceremony into one of the most powerful political protests in sports history.

subject: 1968 Washington, D.C., riots
summary: Four days after Martin Luther King Jr.'s assassination in April 1968, the nation's capital burned -- 1,180 fires, 13 dead, over 7,600 arrested -- leaving scars along 14th Street and U Street that took decades to heal.

subject: 1969 Northern Ireland riots
summary: Five days in August 1969 when sectarian violence spread from Derry's Bogside to Belfast, killed eight people, displaced thousands of families, and is generally counted as the beginning of the Troubles.

subject: 1969 Sudanese coup d'état
summary: The coup that ended Sudan's second democratic era and started the 16-year rule of Gaafar Nimeiry - an Arab nationalist, socialist, and eventual Islamist whose contradictions shaped a generation.

subject: 1971 Sudanese coup d'état
summary: The three-day communist coup that almost changed Sudan forever - foiled when Libya's Gaddafi ordered two fighter jets to force down a British Airways jetliner carrying its leaders home.

story.title: 1973 Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce Bank Robbery

subject: 1973 Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce bank robbery
summary: On May 10, 1973, a masked man walked into a Kenora, Ontario bank with six sticks of dynamite and a dead man's switch clenched in his teeth. He was killed by a police sniper, and more than fifty years later, nobody knows who he was.

subject: 1973 Dutch Grand Prix
summary: Jackie Stewart broke Jim Clark's all-time win record at Zandvoort on 29 July 1973 - but the day belongs to Roger Williamson, who burned to death in his car while only one man tried to save him.

subject: 1973 Rwandan coup d'état
summary: On July 5, 1973, army chief Juvenal Habyarimana overthrew his own friend, President Gregoire Kayibanda, in a bloodless coup that set Rwanda on the path toward totalitarian one-party rule and, eventually, genocide.

subject: 1973 Santiago Gay Protest
summary: In Santiago's main square in 1973, a small group of queer Chileans staged the country's first LGBT demonstration - a landmark act of courage that the press of the day met with scorn.

subject: 1973 Sunnyvale Mid-Air Collision
summary: A NASA research plane and a Navy patrol aircraft collided on approach to Moffett Field, crashing onto a golf course and killing 16 of the 17 people aboard both aircraft.

subject: 1974–1975 Shatt al-Arab conflict
summary: A year of border clashes between Iran and Iraq over the disputed Shatt al-Arab waterway killed over a thousand people and produced a fragile agreement that would unravel into full-scale war five years later.

subject: 1976 Anapa Mid-Air Collision
summary: Two Aeroflot airliners, cleared to the same altitude over the same stretch of Black Sea coast, met in the air off Anapa in September 1976 - and seventy people were gone in an instant.

subject: 1976 Schiedam train accident
summary: On May 4, 1976, the international Rhine Express collided with a commuter train near Rotterdam, killing 24 people in one of the Netherlands' deadliest rail accidents.

subject: 1976 Sudanese coup attempt
summary: Two thousand men crossed the desert from Libya disguised as Sudanese villagers, with disassembled machine guns in their suitcases, convinced Khartoum would welcome them as liberators. It did not.

subject: 1976 Zaire Ebola virus outbreak
summary: In a remote village in northern Zaire, five unsterilized syringes at a mission hospital turned a single infection into humanity's first encounter with Ebola -- a virus that killed 280 of the 318 people it touched.

subject: 1977 Barcelona gay pride demonstration
summary: Two years after Franco's death, some five thousand people marched down Barcelona's La Rambla in Spain's first great act of LGBT visibility, met with police charges and rubber bullets, in a country where their very existence was still a crime.

subject: 1977 Dutch Train Hijacking
summary: For twenty days in 1977, a commuter train sat motionless in a Drenthe meadow, and a quiet quarrel that began on a different continent and a different generation became impossible to look away from.

subject: 1979 Equatorial Guinea coup d'état
summary: On August 3, 1979, Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo overthrew his uncle, the dictator Francisco Macias Nguema, in a bloody coup that ended one of Africa's most brutal regimes but installed a ruler who remains in power decades later.

subject: 1981 Gulf of Corinth Earthquakes
summary: Three earthquakes struck the eastern Gulf of Corinth in February and March 1981, destroying nearly 8,000 homes across the Corinth–Athens region and killing 22 people — the most destructive seismic sequence to hit the area in the modern era.

subject: 1982 World's Fair
summary: When The Wall Street Journal dismissed Knoxville as a 'scruffy little city,' the Tennessee town responded by hosting a World's Fair that introduced Cherry Coke, pay-at-the-pump gas, and brought China back to the international stage for the first time since 1904.

subject: 1985 Lahad Datu Ambush
